Always `export PYTHONPATH=` (Bash) before any `uv run` invocation in this repo.\n- `uv.exe` is not on PATH in this shell; full path is `C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Microsoft\\WinGet\\Packages\\astral-sh.uv_Microsoft.Winget.Source_8wekyb3d8bbwe\\uv.exe`.\n- `gh.exe` is at `C:\\Program Files\\GitHub CLI\\gh.exe`, authenticated as `Rajan-Thakur`.\n- `site/` (the static export `render_site()`/`cms publish` writes) is gitignored and untracked — regenerating/overwriting it locally during smoke tests is always safe, never a real deploy.\n---\nname: mp2-review-process\ndescription: The per-ticket implementation and code-review workflow used successfully across all 9 MP2 CMS tickets\nmetadata:\n  node_type: memory\n  type: feedback\n  originSessionId: 77346485-805e-46b5-86aa-e4a072c5d79e\n  modified: 2026-10-06T07:41:53.102Z\n---\n\nFor each ticket in the MP2 CMS build, the workflow that ran clean across all 9 tickets without correction was: implement with tests written alongside (not strict TDD, but test-covering every acceptance criterion), run the full suite, smoke-test over real HTTP with a throwaway seeded db (not just `TestClient`) for anything UI/template-related, then launch exactly two parallel background sub-agents — one \"Standards axis\" (documented repo standards + a fixed Fowler smell baseline) and one \"Spec axis\" (faithfulness to the ticket's acceptance criteria) — each reading the real diff and relevant context files fresh, each reporting back under 350-450 words. Wait for both before fixing anything, so fixes land in one batch. Post the findings-and-resolutions as a GitHub issue comment on that ticket's issue *before* the closing commit (CLAUDE.md hard-requires this), then commit with `T0N: <title>` ... `Closes #N`, push, confirm auto-close.\n\n**Why:** CLAUDE.md requires posting review findings before the closing commit, and the two-axis separation (from the mattpocock-skills `/code-review` skill) stops one axis's pass from masking the other's fail. Running both as backgrounded forks let the main thread stay responsive instead of blocking serially on two long sub-agent calls per ticket.\n\n**How to apply:** Real findings get fixed in the code; judgement calls the reviewer itself frames as \"reasonable, not a violation\" get left alone and explicitly noted as a deliberate non-fix in the closing comment, with the reasoning — never silently dropped, never fixed reflexively either. When a review surfaces something genuinely unrelated to the current ticket (e.g. a missing nav link from an earlier closed ticket, or a shared helper worth extracting across already-committed files), it's fine to fix it in the same commit as long as it's small, safe, and explicitly disclosed in the commit message/review comment as a deliberate aside rather than hidden in an unrelated diff.\n\nAlways stage files explicitly (`git add <specific paths>`), never `-A`/`.`, and check `git status` before every stage — this project had the user's own in-progress, uncommitted work (an AI Use Statement draft in README.md) sitting in the tree for several tickets in a row; it was never swept into a commit because staging was always explicit.\n---\nname: mp2-revision\ndescription: \"MP2 revision round (Oct 2026): rubric changed upstream, resubmission deadline, and the gap-analysis findings to fix\"\nmetadata:\n  node_type: memory\n  type: project\n  originSessionId: 674d08af-c0fa-4702-8ebe-af8ec4dc7e5e\n  modified: 2026-10-16T07:42:37.060Z\n---\n\n**Revision deadline:** the revised `mp2-final` plus the Stage 2 email must be in by **Fri 2026-10-16 2:40pm EDT** (no-penalty grace; the due date was Thu 10/15). The content model is intentionally generic — built with no specific client in mind. A specific client site has been built *using* this CMS. The site was created for the Upper Arlington High School's Computer Science Honor Society chapter (UAHS CSHS), specifically for Dr. Diane Kahle (faculty advisor). The chapter needs a website to promote computer science among UAHS students.\r\n\r\n## Roles\r\n\r\n**Admin**:\r\nA CMS user role with full permissions: everything an Editor can do, plus publishing/unpublishing content and managing user accounts (create, change role, deactivate). When this CMS is introduced to the client for the UAHS CSHS chapter, Dr. Kahle will be given admin permissions.\r\n_Avoid_: superadmin, owner\r\n\r\n**Editor**:\r\nA CMS user role that can create, edit, and delete any Post or Page — including another user's drafts — but cannot publish/unpublish content or manage user accounts. Student officers will be given Editor permissions.\r\n_Avoid_: contributor, author (an Author is a content attribute, not a role)\r\n\r\n## Content\r\n\r\n**Post**:\r\nA dated, feed-like content item with a title, slug, Markdown body, draft/published status, author, and timestamps. Appears in the site's chronological feed.\r\n_Avoid_: article, entry\r\n\r\n**Page**:\r\nA static, evergreen content item — same fields and operations as a Post, plus appearing in the public site's navigation once published. The UAHS-CSHS website includes The Latest Posts, Coursework, Contact Us, About Us (mission + why join + eligibility + requirements + questions).\r\n_Avoid_: static page (redundant)\r\n\r\n**Slug**:\r\nThe URL-safe identifier for a Post or Page, unique within its kind, used to build its published path. \r\n\r\n**Status (Draft / Published)**:\r\nThe two states a Post or Page can be in. A Draft is visible only in the admin console; only a Published item reaches the static export.\r\n_Avoid_: live/unlive, active/inactive\r\n\r\n**Author**:\r\nThe user (Admin or Editor) recorded as having written a given Post or Page. Distinct from whoever most recently edited it.\r\n\r\n## Publishing\r\n\r\n**Publish** (verb):\r\nThe admin-only action that flips a content item's status from Draft to Published, making it eligible to appear in the next static export.\r\n_Avoid_: approve (there's no separate approval workflow — publish is a single, direct action)\r\n\r\n**Static export**:\r\nThe `site/` directory `cms publish` generates from currently-published content only; what `cms deploy` pushes to GitHub Pages. Every link in it is relative. A link written in a body from the site root (`/contact-us.html`) is rewritten relative to the file it lands in (`./contact-us.html`, or `../contact-us.html` from a Post), since GitHub Pages serves the site from a subfolder. The admin preview keeps it as written.\r\n\r\n**Revision**:\r\nOne saved version of a Post or Page: its title, slug, and body, who saved it, and when, numbered 1, 2, 3… within that item. Every create, edit, and Roll back records one; Publish and unpublish do not, since they change Status, not content.\r\n_Avoid_: snapshot, history entry\r\n\r\n**Revision history**:\r\nThe list of an item's Revisions, newest first, on its edit screen. The newest is the Current one.\r\n\r\n**Roll back** (verb):\r\nReturning an item's title, slug, and body to those of an earlier Revision. Editors and Admins can do it; it is itself recorded as a new Revision, so a Roll back can be undone the same way. Status is unchanged: a Published item's restored text reaches the site on the next static export.\r\n_Avoid_: restore, revert, undo\r\n\r\n**Scheduled publishing**:\r\nAn Admin setting a future time, in UTC, after which a Draft becomes Published. The public site is static, so nothing happens at that moment: the item becomes Published on the next `cms publish` after its time, which switches it before writing the static export. Setting or cancelling a schedule records no Revision, since it changes Status, not content.\r\n_Avoid_: auto-publish, publishing \"automatically\"\r\n\r\n**Scheduled**:\r\nA Draft with a publish time set. The dashboard and lists show it as \"scheduled\", apart from other Drafts. T17's security tests were checked this way.\n- The student wants brief answers and no repeated framing.\n\n## Suggested skills\n\n- `mattpocock-skills:code-review`: only if any further code changes (CLAUDE.md requires findings on the issue before close).\n- `mattpocock-skills:tdd`: same condition.\n- `run`: optional, to drive the app for the pre-tag check if the walkthrough script isn't reused.\n- For MP2plus later:\n  - `mattpocock-skills:prototype` (exercise P2)\n  - `mattpocock-skills:domain-modeling` (P3: Decisions table + ADR)\n  - `mattpocock-skills:grilling` (to pick exercises)\n- `mattpocock-skills:handoff`: at the end of the next session if work remains.\n----\n# CONTEXT.md glossary\r\n\r\nA small, WordPress-style web CMS: a local admin console where Editors and Admins manage content, and a static public site that publishes it. The content model is intentionally generic — built with no specific client in mind. A specific client site has been built *using* this CMS. The site was created for the Upper Arlington High School's Computer Science Honor Society chapter (UAHS CSHS), specifically for Dr. Diane Kahle (faculty advisor). The chapter needs a website to promote computer science among UAHS students.\r\n\r\n## Roles\r\n\r\n**Admin**:\r\nA CMS user role with full permissions: everything an Editor can do, plus publishing/unpublishing content and managing user accounts (create, change role, deactivate). When this CMS is introduced to the client for the UAHS CSHS chapter, Dr. Kahle will be given admin permissions.\r\n_Avoid_: superadmin, owner\r\n\r\n**Editor**:\r\nA CMS user role that can create, edit, and delete any Post or Page — including another user's drafts — but cannot publish/unpublish content or manage user accounts. Student officers will be given Editor permissions.\r\n_Avoid_: contributor, author (an Author is a content attribute, not a role)\r\n\r\n## Content\r\n\r\n**Post**:\r\nA dated, feed-like content item with a title, slug, Markdown body, draft/published status, author, and timestamps. Appears in the site's chronological feed.\r\n_Avoid_: article, entry\r\n\r\n**Page**:\r\nA static, evergreen content item — same fields and operations as a Post, plus appearing in the public site's navigation once published. The UAHS-CSHS website includes The Latest Posts, Coursework, Contact Us, About Us (mission + why join + eligibility + requirements + questions).\r\n_Avoid_: static page (redundant)\r\n\r\n**Slug**:\r\nThe URL-safe identifier for a Post or Page, unique within its kind, used to build its published path. \r\n\r\n**Status (Draft / Published)**:\r\nThe two states a Post or Page can be in. A Draft is visible only in the admin console; only a Published item reaches the static export.\r\n_Avoid_: live/unlive, active/inactive\r\n\r\n**Author**:\r\nThe user (Admin or Editor) recorded as having written a given Post or Page. Distinct from whoever most recently edited it.\r\n\r\n## Publishing\r\n\r\n**Publish** (verb):\r\nThe admin-only action that flips a content item's status from Draft to Published, making it eligible to appear in the next static export.\r\n_Avoid_: approve (there's no separate approval workflow — publish is a single, direct action)\r\n\r\n**Static export**:\r\nThe `site/` directory `cms publish` generates from currently-published content only; what `cms deploy` pushes to GitHub Pages. Every link in it is relative. A link written in a body from the site root (`/contact-us.html`) is rewritten relative to the file it lands in (`./contact-us.html`, or `../contact-us.html` from a Post), since GitHub Pages serves the site from a subfolder. The admin preview keeps it as written.\r\n\r\n**Revision**:\r\nOne saved version of a Post or Page: its title, slug, and body, who saved it, and when, numbered 1, 2, 3… within that item. Every create, edit, and Roll back records one; Publish and unpublish do not, since they change Status, not content.\r\n_Avoid_: snapshot, history entry\r\n\r\n**Revision history**:\r\nThe list of an item's Revisions, newest first, on its edit screen. The newest is the Current one.\r\n\r\n**Roll back** (verb):\r\nReturning an item's title, slug, and body to those of an earlier Revision. Editors and Admins can do it; it is itself recorded as a new Revision, so a Roll back can be undone the same way. Status is unchanged: a Published item's restored text reaches the site on the next static export.\r\n_Avoid_: restore, revert, undo\r\n\r\n**Scheduled publishing**:\r\nAn Admin setting a future time, in UTC, after which a Draft becomes Published. The public site is static, so nothing happens at that moment: the item becomes Published on the next `cms publish` after its time, which switches it before writing the static export. Setting or cancelling a schedule records no Revision, since it changes Status, not content.\r\n_Avoid_: auto-publish, publishing \"automatically\"\r\n\r\n**Scheduled**:\r\nA Draft with a publish time set. The dashboard and lists show it as \"scheduled\", apart from other Drafts. Publishing or unpublishing it by hand cancels its schedule.\r\n----\norigin\thttps://github.com/Rajan-Thakur/iphs400-mp2-cms.git (fetch)\norigin\thttps://github.com/Rajan-Thakur/iphs400-mp2-cms.git (push)\ntemplate\thttps://github.com/jon-chun/iphs400-mp2-cms-starter.git (fetch)\ntemplate\thttps://github.com/jon-chun/iphs400-mp2-cms-starter.git (push)\n0a9eee4 docs: MP2 graded as a numeric score (no pass line); Every image carries alt text, so a screen reader can describe it.\n146:- **Roles.** Upload and media library: admin and editor.\n149:1. Create the issue (runbook 1), title `MP2plus F1: Media uploads with alt text`; then `echo T<issue#> > .claude/state/phase`.\n152:4. Save `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-media-1280.png` and `mp2plus-media-390.png`: the library with one image. Then run the two checks (runbook 8).\n156:/implement #N Media uploads with alt text, for posts only. Follow the issue's acceptance checklist exactly. Store uploads under media/ and add media/ to .gitignore. Accept PNG and JPEG of 2 MB or less; check the type by extension and by the file's first bytes. The library shows a copyable Markdown snippet ![alt](media/<file>) for each item. cms publish copies media/ into site/media/ and makes every image src relative to the page that contains it. Rules: no href=\"/ or src=\"/ in any template, admin pages included; use url_for or relative links. Every new form carries a CSRF token and refuses a POST without it. Every new setting gets a line in .env.example. If you change the database schema, keep scripts/seed_demo.py running clean from .env.example and tell me to run rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py. Tests that existed before may only gain cases; ask me before changing an existing assertion. Put the new tests in tests/test_media.py and name each one test_step<k>_<what> after the acceptance step it checks. Ask before adding any dependency.\n161:| 1 | Upload a PNG or JPEG of 2 MB or less with alt text; it appears in the media library | walk, test |\n164:| 4 | Uploads are stored under `media/`, and `media/` is git-ignored | read |\n165:| 5 | Each library item shows a copyable Markdown snippet, `![<alt text>](media/<file>)` | walk |\n167:| 7 | After `uv run cms publish`, the file is in `site/media/`, and the post's `<img>` has the alt text and a relative `src` that loads in the preview | publish, test |\n170:- **Out of scope.** Inserting images with a button, resizing, thumbnails, deleting media, video, drag-and-drop, images in pages.\n171:- **Deliverables.** The closed issue; `tests/test_media.py`; `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-media-1280.png` and `-390.png`; your report row.\n172:- **Report row.** `| F1 | issue #<n>; tests/test_media.py; mp2plus-media-1280.png, mp2plus-media-390.png |`\n178:| Images load on the home page, broken on post pages | a post page needs `../media/x.png` | make `src` relative to each page's folder |\n180:#### F2 Categories and tags (8 pts, about 40–55 min)\n215:#### F3 Revision history with rollback (8 pts, about 40–55 min)\n251:#### F4 Scheduled publishing (7 pts, about 35–50 min)\n287:#### F5 Site search (7 pts, about 35–50 min)\n322:#### F6 Comments with moderation (9 pts, about 45–60 min)\n359:#### F7 Plugin or hook system (9 pts, about 45–60 min)\n395:#### F8 Switchable theme (7 pts, about 35–50 min)\n431:#### F9 Production configuration (8 pts, about 40–55 min)\n466:### 1.2 Process (P1–P4)\n468:#### P1 Pull-request workflow (6 pts, about 30–45 min)\n506:#### P2 `/prototype` side session (7 pts, about 35–50 min)\n512:1. `echo P2 > .claude/state/phase`. P1 carries one other change, P2 needs code where its decision lands, and P4 measures one other exercise; each says so under **Prerequisites**.\n- **New work only.** Only commits after `mp2plus-base` count. A feature already in your repo at `mp2plus-base` is not scored again.\n- **Every point is a line** with a measure and a check, listed under each exercise's **Scoring**. One flaw costs points in one line only.\n\n**How each exercise is laid out.** Every exercise has the same headings: Goal, Prerequisites, Roles, Steps, Prompt, Acceptance checklist, Out of scope, Deliverables, Report row, Scoring, If it goes wrong. The **Roles** line says which new routes are admin-only and which editors may use; S1 tests exactly those. The **Acceptance checklist** is the contract: the judge checks those steps and no others. Its **Checked by** column uses seven words. *walk*: the judge clicks through your app from a clean clone, at 1280 and 390 px. *publish*: the judge runs `uv run cms publish` and inspects `site/`. *test*: a named test for this step exists and passes. *read*: the judge reads the file or the code. *replay*: the judge sends the form's POST again without its CSRF token. *github*: the judge reads GitHub's own records and times (issues, pull requests, comments, pushes). *run*: the judge runs the command at the commit named.\n\n> **How a feature scores.** A feature worth P points has four lines. **Screenshots, 1:** both `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-{slug}-1280.png` and `-390.png` are present. **Trail, 1:** the issue existed before your first commit for it reached GitHub, and your findings comment came before the issue closed. **Tests, 1:** every step marked *test* has a named test that passes. **Function, P − 3:** floor((P − 3) × steps passed ÷ steps in the table). Process and security exercises score one point per checklist row, as listed in their tables.\n\n### The feature runbook\nEvery feature's **Steps** follow MP2 Part 6's per-ticket loop. The commands, once:\n\n1. **The issue, before any code.** `gh issue create --label stretch --title \"MP2plus F2: Categories and tags\"`. When `gh` asks for the body, open the editor and paste the feature's acceptance table (the `| # | Step | Checked by |` rows) word for word, then a last line `Blocked by: none`. If `gh` says the label is not found, run `gh label create stretch` once and retry.\n2. **The phase, before the session.** `echo T14 > .claude/state/phase`, with your issue number for 14. The usage ledger labels every turn with it, so set it before you start. Process and security exercises set their id instead, for example `echo S2 > .claude/state/phase`.\n3. **The build.** `/clear`, then the feature's prompt with your issue number. `/implement` drives `/tdd`: a failing test first, then code.\n4. **Your own walk.** Click through the acceptance checklist at 1280 and 390 px; fix what fails.\n5. **Review, then close.** Send `/code-review`, then: `Post the code-review findings and how each was resolved as a comment on issue #14, then commit and push with a message that starts \"T14:\" and ends \"Closes #14\".`\n6. **Check.** `gh issue view 14`. **Expected:** state CLOSED, with your findings comment above the close.\n7. **Screenshots.** The feature working, at 1280 and 390 px, saved as named in its **Deliverables**.\n8. **The two checks.** `uv run python scripts/check_submission.py --stage 2` and `uv run pytest -q`. Fix any failure that was not there at `mp2plus-base` before you start the next exercise.\n\nEvery feature prompt ends with the same rules; each one guards against a way to lose points. No `href=\"/` or `src=\"/` in any template, admin pages included: the MP2 checker greps every tracked `.html` file. A schema change needs a fresh database: `rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py`. A new setting needs a line in `.env.example`, because the judge starts your app from it. Every new form needs a CSRF token.\n\n| Symptom | Cause | Fix |\n|---|---|---|\n| Checker fails `no root-absolute paths in HTML` after a new admin page | a template has `href=\"/admin/...\"` | use `url_for(...)` or a relative link; the checker reads admin templates too |\n| `sqlite3.OperationalError: no such column` | the schema changed; your old `cms.db` did not | `rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py` |\n| An MP2 test fails after your change | the feature changed behaviour an old test pins | add cases, never weaken old ones; if one assertion truly must change, declare it (Part 0 gate box) |\n| Issue did not close | the commit message or PR body lacked `Closes #N` | `gh issue close 14 --comment \"closed by <sha>\"`; use the exact phrase next time |\n| Checker fails on a transcript name | a file in `docs/transcripts/` breaks MP2's pattern | set `CMS_STUDENT=first-last` in `.env`; rename to `iphs400_mp2-cms_chat-session_{NN}_{first}-{last}_{YYYYMMDD}.md` |\n| Your exercise has no row in `usage_report.py` | the phase was set after the session started | set it first next time; the ledger cannot be relabelled |\n### 1.1 Features (F1–F9)\n\n#### F1 Media uploads with alt text (9 pts, about 45–60 min)\n- **Goal.** Editors upload images to a media library and place them in posts. Every image carries alt text, so a screen reader can describe it.\n- **Prerequisites.** MP2 done and Part 0 complete. Other exercises: none. Uses FastAPI's form uploads (`python-multipart` is already a dependency).\n- **Roles.** Upload and media library: admin and editor.\n\n**Steps.**\n1. Create the issue (runbook 1), title `MP2plus F1: Media uploads with alt text`; then `echo T<issue#> > .claude/state/phase`.\n2. `/clear`, then the prompt below with your issue number. Then walk the acceptance checklist yourself; fix what fails.\n3. `/code-review`, then the close-out message (runbook 5). `gh issue view <issue#>` shows CLOSED, with your comment above the close.\n4. Save `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-media-1280.png` and `mp2plus-media-390.png`: the library with one image. Then run the two checks (runbook 8).\n\n**Prompt.**\n```text\n/implement #N Media uploads with alt text, for posts only. Follow the issue's acceptance checklist exactly. Store uploads under media/ and add media/ to .gitignore. Accept PNG and JPEG of 2 MB or less; check the type by extension and by the file's first bytes. The library shows a copyable Markdown snippet ![alt](media/<file>) for each item. cms publish copies media/ into site/media/ and makes every image src relative to the page that contains it. Rules: no href=\"/ or src=\"/ in any template, admin pages included; use url_for or relative links. Every new form carries a CSRF token and refuses a POST without it. Every new setting gets a line in .env.example. If you change the database schema, keep scripts/seed_demo.py running clean from .env.example and tell me to run rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py. Tests that existed before may only gain cases; ask me before changing an existing assertion. Put the new tests in tests/test_media.py and name each one test_step<k>_<what> after the acceptance step it checks. Ask before adding any dependency.\n```\n**Acceptance checklist.**\n| # | Step | Checked by |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Upload a PNG or JPEG of 2 MB or less with alt text; it appears in the media library | walk, test |\n| 2 | An upload with empty alt text is refused with a message | walk, test |\n| 3 | A `.html` file, a `.html` file renamed to `.png`, and any file over 2 MB are refused: the type is checked by extension and by the file's first bytes | walk, test |\n| 4 | Uploads are stored under `media/`, and `media/` is git-ignored | read |\n| 5 | Each library item shows a copyable Markdown snippet, `![<alt text>](media/<file>)` | walk |\n| 6 | The upload form carries a CSRF token; its POST replayed without the token is refused | replay, test |\n| 7 | After `uv run cms publish`, the file is in `site/media/`, and the post's `<img>` has the alt text and a relative `src` that loads in the preview | publish, test |\n\n**The judge runs:** upload an image; try an empty alt text, a `.html` file and a `.html` file renamed to `.png`; paste a snippet into a published post; publish; preview with `python3 -m http.server -d site 8001`; check that every `<img>` in `site/` has `alt=` and loads.\n- **Out of scope.** Inserting images with a button, resizing, thumbnails, deleting media, video, drag-and-drop, images in pages.\n- **Deliverables.** The closed issue; `tests/test_media.py`; `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-media-1280.png` and `-390.png`; your report row.\n- **Report row.** `| F1 | issue #<n>; tests/test_media.py; mp2plus-media-1280.png, mp2plus-media-390.png |`\n- **Scoring.** Screenshots 1 · Trail 1 · Tests 1 · Function 6 = floor(6 × steps passed ÷ 7). Total 9.\n\n**If it goes wrong.**\n| Symptom | Cause | Fix |\n|---|---|---|\n| Images load on the home page, broken on post pages | a post page needs `../media/x.png` | make `src` relative to each page's folder |\n| A renamed `.html` file is accepted | only the extension is checked | compare the first bytes with the PNG and JPEG signatures |\n#### F2 Categories and tags (8 pts, about 40–55 min)\n## Part 2 — Submit\n**Time: 20 min. Process and security exercises set their id instead, for example `echo S2 > .claude/state/phase`.\n3. **The build.** `/clear`, then the feature's prompt with your issue number. `/implement` drives `/tdd`: a failing test first, then code.\n4. **Your own walk.** Click through the acceptance checklist at 1280 and 390 px; fix what fails.\n5. **Review, then close.** Send `/code-review`, then: `Post the code-review findings and how each was resolved as a comment on issue #14, then commit and push with a message that starts \"T14:\" and ends \"Closes #14\".`\n6. **Check.** `gh issue view 14`. **Expected:** state CLOSED, with your findings comment above the close.\n7. **Screenshots.** The feature working, at 1280 and 390 px, saved as named in its **Deliverables**.\n8. **The two checks.** `uv run python scripts/check_submission.py --stage 2` and `uv run pytest -q`. Fix any failure that was not there at `mp2plus-base` before you start the next exercise.\n\nEvery feature prompt ends with the same rules; each one guards against a way to lose points. No `href=\"/` or `src=\"/` in any template, admin pages included: the MP2 checker greps every tracked `.html` file. A schema change needs a fresh database: `rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py`. A new setting needs a line in `.env.example`, because the judge starts your app from it. Every new form needs a CSRF token.\n\n| Symptom | Cause | Fix |\n|---|---|---|\n| Checker fails `no root-absolute paths in HTML` after a new admin page | a template has `href=\"/admin/...\"` | use `url_for(...)` or a relative link; the checker reads admin templates too |\n| `sqlite3.OperationalError: no such column` | the schema changed; your old `cms.db` did not | `rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py` |\n| An MP2 test fails after your change | the feature changed behaviour an old test pins | add cases, never weaken old ones; if one assertion truly must change, declare it (Part 0 gate box) |\n| Issue did not close | the commit message or PR body lacked `Closes #N` | `gh issue close 14 --comment \"closed by <sha>\"`; use the exact phrase next time |\n| Checker fails on a transcript name | a file in `docs/transcripts/` breaks MP2's pattern | set `CMS_STUDENT=first-last` in `.env`; rename to `iphs400_mp2-cms_chat-session_{NN}_{first}-{last}_{YYYYMMDD}.md` |\n| Your exercise has no row in `usage_report.py` | the phase was set after the session started | set it first next time; the ledger cannot be relabelled |\n### 1.1 Features (F1–F9)\n\n#### F1 Media uploads with alt text (9 pts, about 45–60 min)\n- **Goal.** Editors upload images to a media library and place them in posts. Every image carries alt text, so a screen reader can describe it.\n- **Prerequisites.** MP2 done and Part 0 complete. Other exercises: none. Uses FastAPI's form uploads (`python-multipart` is already a dependency).\n- **Roles.** Upload and media library: admin and editor.\n\n**Steps.**\n1. Create the issue (runbook 1), title `MP2plus F1: Media uploads with alt text`; then `echo T<issue#> > .claude/state/phase`.\n2. `/clear`, then the prompt below with your issue number. Then walk the acceptance checklist yourself; fix what fails.\n3. `/code-review`, then the close-out message (runbook 5). `gh issue view <issue#>` shows CLOSED, with your comment above the close.\n4. Save `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-media-1280.png` and `mp2plus-media-390.png`: the library with one image. Then run the two checks (runbook 8).\n\n**Prompt.**\n```text\n/implement #N Media uploads with alt text, for posts only. Follow the issue's acceptance checklist exactly. Store uploads under media/ and add media/ to .gitignore. Accept PNG and JPEG of 2 MB or less; check the type by extension and by the file's first bytes. The library shows a copyable Markdown snippet ![alt](media/<file>) for each item. cms publish copies media/ into site/media/ and makes every image src relative to the page that contains it. Rules: no href=\"/ or src=\"/ in any template, admin pages included; use url_for or relative links. Every new form carries a CSRF token and refuses a POST without it. Every new setting gets a line in .env.example. If you change the database schema, keep scripts/seed_demo.py running clean from .env.example and tell me to run rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py. Tests that existed before may only gain cases; ask me before changing an existing assertion. Put the new tests in tests/test_media.py and name each one test_step<k>_<what> after the acceptance step it checks. Ask before adding any dependency.\n```\n**Acceptance checklist.**\n| # | Step | Checked by |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Upload a PNG or JPEG of 2 MB or less with alt text; it appears in the media library | walk, test |\n| 2 | An upload with empty alt text is refused with a message | walk, test |\n| 3 | A `.html` file, a `.html` file renamed to `.png`, and any file over 2 MB are refused: the type is checked by extension and by the file's first bytes | walk, test |\n| 4 | Uploads are stored under `media/`, and `media/` is git-ignored | read |\n| 5 | Each library item shows a copyable Markdown snippet, `![<alt text>](media/<file>)` | walk |\n| 6 | The upload form carries a CSRF token; its POST replayed without the token is refused | replay, test |\n| 7 | After `uv run cms publish`, the file is in `site/media/`, and the post's `<img>` has the alt text and a relative `src` that loads in the preview | publish, test |\n\n**The judge runs:** upload an image; try an empty alt text, a `.html` file and a `.html` file renamed to `.png`; paste a snippet into a published post; publish; preview with `python3 -m http.server -d site 8001`; check that every `<img>` in `site/` has `alt=` and loads.\n- **Out of scope.** Inserting images with a button, resizing, thumbnails, deleting media, video, drag-and-drop, images in pages.\n- **Deliverables.** The closed issue; `tests/test_media.py`; `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-media-1280.png` and `-390.png`; your report row.\n- **Report row.** `| F1 | issue #<n>; tests/test_media.py; mp2plus-media-1280.png, mp2plus-media-390.png |`\n- **Scoring.** Screenshots 1 · Trail 1 · Tests 1 · Function 6 = floor(6 × steps passed ÷ 7). Total 9.\n\n**If it goes wrong.**\n| Symptom | Cause | Fix |\n|---|---|---|\n| Images load on the home page, broken on post pages | a post page needs `../media/x.png` | make `src` relative to each page's folder |\n| A renamed `.html` file is accepted | only the extension is checked | compare the first bytes with the PNG and JPEG signatures |\n#### F2 Categories and tags (8 pts, about 40–55 min)\n## Part 2 — Submit\n**Time: 20 min. last: its /{slug}.html matches broadly\r\n    24\t\r\n    25\t    @app.exception_handler(NeedsLogin)\r\n    26\t    def _redirect_to_login(request: Request, exc: NeedsLogin):\r\n    27\t        return RedirectResponse(\"/login\", status_code=303)\r\n    28\t\r\n    29\t    app.add_exception_handler(AccessDenied, render_access_denied)\r\n    30\t\r\n    31\t    return app\r\n    32\t\r\n    33\t\r\n    34\tapp = create_app()\r\n=== app/settings.py\n     1\t\"\"\"Configuration, read from the environment (never hard-code secrets).\n     2\t\n     3\tValues come from real environment variables first, then from `.env` in the\n     4\tproject root, so `cp .env.example .env` is the whole setup. `uv run` does not\n     5\tload `.env` by itself, and python-dotenv isn't in the fixed stack, hence the\n     6\tsmall reader below.\n     7\t\"\"\"\n     8\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n     9\t\n    10\timport os\n    11\tfrom pathlib import Path\n    12\t\n    13\tROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\n    14\tTEMPLATES = ROOT / \"templates\"\n    15\tSITE = ROOT / \"site\"\n    16\t\n    17\t\n    18\tdef load_dotenv(path: Path) -> None:\n    19\t    \"\"\"Copy KEY=VALUE lines from `path` into os.environ, never overriding a\n    20\t    variable that is already set. Blank lines and # comments are skipped.\"\"\"\n    21\t    try:\n    22\t        # utf-8-sig: PowerShell's Out-File writes a BOM, which would otherwise\n    23\t        # glue itself onto the first key and silently drop that variable.\n    24\t        lines = path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8-sig\").splitlines()\n    25\t    except OSError:\n    26\t        return\n    27\t    for line in lines:\n    28\t        line = line.strip()\n    29\t        if not line or line.startswith(\"#\") or \"=\" not in line:\n    30\t            continue\n    31\t        key, value = line.split(\"=\", 1)\n    32\t        key, value = key.strip(), value.strip()\n    33\t        if len(value) >= 2 and value[0] == value[-1] and value[0] in \"\\\"'\":\n    34\t            value = value[1:-1]\n    35\t        os.environ.setdefault(key, value)\n    36\t\n    37\t\n    38\tload_dotenv(ROOT / \".env\")\n    39\t\n    40\t\n    41\tdef _project_path(raw: str) -> Path:\n    42\t    path = Path(raw)\n    43\t    return path if path.is_absolute() else ROOT / path\n    44\t\n    45\t\n    46\tSECRET_KEY = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SECRET_KEY\", \"dev-only-not-for-production\")\n    47\tDATABASE_PATH = _project_path(os.environ.get(\"CMS_DATABASE\", \"cms.db\"))\n    48\tSITE_TITLE = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SITE_TITLE\", \"My CMS\")\n    49\t# Set this to your Pages URL once you deploy, e.g.\n    50\t# https://yourname.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\n    51\tBASE_PATH = os.environ.get(\"CMS_BASE_PATH\", \"\")\n=== app/db.py\n     1\t\"\"\"SQLite connection and schema. No ORM (see spec Implementation Decisions).\"\"\"\r\n     2\tfrom __future__ import annotations\r\n     3\t\r\n     4\timport sqlite3\r\n     5\tfrom pathlib import Path\r\n     6\t\r\n     7\tfrom app import settings\r\n     8\t\r\n     9\tSCHEMA = \"\"\"\r\n    10\tCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (\r\n    11\t    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\r\n    12\t    email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\r\n    13\t    password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,\r\n    14\t    role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('admin', 'editor')),\r\n    15\t    active INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,\r\n    16\t    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))\r\n    17\t);\r\n    18\t\r\n    19\tCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS content (\r\n    20\t    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\r\n    21\t    kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('post', 'page')),\r\n    22\t    title TEXT NOT NULL,\r\n    23\t    slug TEXT NOT NULL,\r\n    24\t    body_md TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',\r\n    25\t    status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'published')) DEFAULT 'draft',\r\n    26\t    author_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),\r\n    27\t    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\r\n    28\t    updated_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\r\n    29\t    -- Set on a Draft that is Scheduled (see CONTEXT.md): the UTC time after\r\n    30\t    -- which the next `cms publish` makes it Published. NULL otherwise.\r\n    31\t    publish_at TEXT,\r\n    32\t    UNIQUE (kind, slug)\r\n    33\t);\r\n    34\t\r\n    35\t-- One row per saved version of a content item (see CONTEXT.md: Revision).\r\n    36\t-- `version` counts 1, 2, 3... within one item; `rolled_back_to` is set when\r\n    37\t-- the save was a Roll back, to the version it rolled back to.\r\n    38\tCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS revisions (\r\n    39\t    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\r\n    40\t    content_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES content(id),\r\n    41\t    version INTEGER NOT NULL,\r\n    42\t    title TEXT NOT NULL,\r\n    43\t    slug TEXT NOT NULL,\r\n    44\t    body_md TEXT NOT NULL,\r\n    45\t    saved_by INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),\r\n    46\t    saved_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\r\n    47\t    rolled_back_to INTEGER,\r\n    48\t    UNIQUE (content_id, version)\r\n    49\t);\r\n    50\t\"\"\"\r\n    51\t\r\n    52\t\r\n    53\t# Items saved before revisions existed get one starting revision from their\r\n    54\t# current state, so their pre-T15 text can still be rolled back to. The last\r\n    55\t# editor was never stored, so the Author stands in as who saved it. A no-op\r\n    56\t# once every item has a revision.\r\n    57\tBACKFILL_REVISIONS = \"\"\"\r\n    58\tINSERT INTO revisions (content_id, version, title, slug, body_md, saved_by, saved_at)\r\n    59\tSELECT id, 1, title, slug, body_md, author_id, updated_at FROM content\r\n    60\tWHERE id NOT IN (SELECT content_id FROM revisions);\r\n    61\t\"\"\"\r\n    62\t\r\n    63\t# Columns added to existing tables after they were first created. CREATE\r\n    64\t# TABLE IF NOT EXISTS never changes a table that already exists, so a database\r\n    65\t# made before a column existed gains it here. Maps table -> [(column, type)].\r\n    66\tADDED_COLUMNS = {\"content\": [(\"publish_at\", \"TEXT\")]}\r\n    67\t\r\n    68\t# Database files already brought up to date by this process.\r\n    69\t_schema_ready: set[str] = set()\r\n    70\t\r\n    71\t\r\n    72\tdef _path(db_path: Path | None) -> Path:\r\n    73\t    # Read lazily (settings.DATABASE_PATH) so tests can monkeypatch it per-test.\r\n    74\t    return db_path if db_path is not None else settings.DATABASE_PATH\r\n    75\t\r\n    76\t\r\n    77\tdef _open(path: Path) -> sqlite3.Connection:\r\n    78\t    conn = sqlite3.connect(path)\r\n    79\t    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\r\n    80\t    return conn\r\n    81\t\r\n    82\t\r\n    83\tdef connect(db_path: Path | None = None) -> sqlite3.Connection:\r\n    84\t    \"\"\"Open a connection to the CMS database. The first open of each file in\r\n    85\t    a process runs init_db, so a database made before a newer table existed\r\n    86\t    works without a re-seed.\"\"\"\r\n    87\t    path = _path(db_path)\r\n    88\t    if str(Path(path).resolve()) not in _schema_ready:\r\n    89\t        init_db(path)\r\n    90\t    return _open(path)\r\n    91\t\r\n    92\t\r\n    93\tdef _add_missing_columns(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:\r\n    94\t    for table, columns in ADDED_COLUMNS.items():\r\n    95\t        present = {row[\"name\"] for row in conn.execute(f\"PRAGMA table_info({table})\")}\r\n    96\t        for name, sql_type in columns:\r\n    97\t            if name not in present:\r\n    98\t                conn.execute(f\"ALTER TABLE {table} ADD COLUMN {name} {sql_type}\")\r\n    99\t\r\n   100\t\r\n   101\tdef init_db(db_path: Path | None = None) -> None:\r\n   102\t    \"\"\"Create any missing tables and columns, and backfill starting\r\n   103\t    revisions. Safe to run on a new or an existing database, any number of\r\n   104\t    times.\"\"\"\r\n   105\t    path = _path(db_path)\r\n   106\t    conn = _open(path)\r\n   107\t    try:\r\n   108\t        conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\r\n   109\t        _add_missing_columns(conn)\r\n   110\t        conn.executescript(BACKFILL_REVISIONS)\r\n   111\t        conn.commit()\r\n   112\t    finally:\r\n   113\t        conn.close()\r\n   114\t    _schema_ready.add(str(Path(path).resolve()))\r\n=== app/mdrender.py\n     1\t\"\"\"Markdown -> sanitized HTML: the one pipeline the admin preview and the\n     2\tlater static export (T07) both reuse, so a post can't render one way in the\n     3\teditor and another way once published. The one deliberate difference is a\n     4\tlink to the site root, which the export makes relative (`to_root` below).\n     5\t\"\"\"\n     6\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n     7\t\n     8\tfrom collections.abc import Callable\n     9\t\n    10\timport nh3\n    11\tfrom markdown_it import MarkdownIt\n    12\t\n    13\t_md = MarkdownIt(\"commonmark\")\n    14\t\n    15\t# What a browser ignores before it reads a URL (WHATWG URL parsing): spaces\n    16\t# and control characters at either end, and tabs and newlines anywhere.\n    17\t_TRIMMED = \"\".join(chr(code) for code in range(0x21))\n    18\t_DROPPED = {ord(\"\\t\"): None, ord(\"\\n\"): None, ord(\"\\r\"): None}\n    19\t\n    20\t\n    21\tdef render_markdown(raw: str, *, to_root: str | None = None) -> str:\n    22\t    \"\"\"Render Markdown to HTML, then strip anything unsafe (script tags,\n    23\t    event-handler attributes like onerror=, javascript: URLs, ...).\n    24\t\n    25\t    `to_root` is set when the HTML is written into site/: the \"../\" steps\n    26\t    from that file back to the site root (\"\" for a Page, \"../\" for a Post).\n    27\t    A link written in a body from the site root (`/contact-us.html`) is then\n    28\t    made relative to the file, because GitHub Pages serves the site from a\n    29\t    subfolder. Unset (the admin preview), links stay as written: the admin\n    30\t    server serves the public pages at its own root, so they resolve there.\n    31\t    \"\"\"\n    32\t    html = _md.render(raw)\n    33\t    if to_root is None:\n    34\t        return nh3.clean(html)\n    35\t    return nh3.clean(html, attribute_filter=_root_link_rewriter(to_root))\n    36\t\n    37\t\n    38\tdef _root_link_rewriter(to_root: str) -> Callable[[str, str, str], str]:\n    39\t    \"\"\"An nh3 attribute filter that rewrites every href/src a browser would\n    40\t    read as root-absolute or protocol-relative.\n    41\t\n    42\t    nh3 checks URL schemes before it calls the filter, never after, so a\n    43\t    rewritten value must never be able to start a scheme: it always begins\n    44\t    with \"./\", \"../\" or \"https://\". Dropping only the \"/\" would turn\n    45\t    \"/javascript:alert(1)\" into a live javascript: link.\n    46\t    \"\"\"\n    47\t    prefix = to_root or \"./\"\n    48\t\n    49\t    def rewrite(tag: str, attribute: str, value: str) -> str:\n    50\t        if attribute not in (\"href\", \"src\"):\n    51\t            return value\n    52\t        url = value.strip(_TRIMMED).translate(_DROPPED).replace(\"\\\\\", \"/\")\n    53\t        if url.startswith(\"//\"):\n    54\t            return \"https:\" + url  # protocol-relative; GitHub Pages is HTTPS-only\n    55\t        if url.startswith(\"/\"):\n    56\t            rest = url[1:]\n    57\t            if rest == \"\" or rest[0] in \"#?\":\n    58\t                rest = \"index.html\" + rest  # \"/\" is the home page\n    59\t            return prefix + rest\n    60\t        return value\n    61\t\n    62\t    return rewrite\n=== app/publish.py\n     1\t\"\"\"Render the public site into site/ as plain HTML.\r\n     2\t\r\n     3\tT00 publishes a placeholder home page. As you build content types, extend\r\n     4\trender_site() to write one file per published item. Two rules the rubric checks:\r\n     5\t\r\n     6\t  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\r\n     7\t  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\r\n     8\t     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\r\n     9\t     That includes links written in a body: render_markdown(..., to_root=...)\r\n    10\t     rewrites \"/contact-us.html\" for the file it lands in.\r\n    11\t\"\"\"\r\n    12\tfrom __future__ import annotations\r\n    13\t\r\n    14\timport shutil\r\n    15\tfrom pathlib import Path\r\n    16\t\r\n    17\tfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\r\n    18\t\r\n    19\tfrom app import content as content_module\r\n    20\tfrom app import settings\r\n    21\tfrom app.mdrender import render_markdown\r\n    22\t\r\n    23\t# One stylesheet for the public site and the admin console (served at /style.css).\r\n    24\tCSS = Path(__file__).with_name(\"style.css\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\r\n    25\t\r\n    26\t\r\n    27\tdef environment() -> Environment:\r\n    28\t    return Environment(\r\n    29\t        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\r\n    30\t        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\r\n    31\t    )\r\n    32\t\r\n    33\t\r\n    34\tdef nav_items(prefix: str = \"\") -> list[dict[str, str]]:\r\n    35\t    \"\"\"Published Pages, as relative (title, href) links for the public\r\n    36\t    site's nav. `prefix` relocates the link for a page nested one\r\n    37\t    directory deep (e.g. \"../\" from site/posts/*.html) — a draft Page\r\n    38\t    never appears here.\"\"\"\r\n    39\t    return [{\"title\": page[\"title\"], \"href\": f\"{prefix}{page['slug']}.html\"}\r\n    40\t            for page in _exportable_pages()]\r\n    41\t\r\n    42\t\r\n    43\tdef _exportable_pages() -> list:\r\n    44\t    # The editor already refuses reserved slugs; this also covers rows saved\r\n    45\t    # before that check existed, so a Page can never overwrite site/index.html.\r\n    46\t    return [page for page in content_module.list_published(\"page\")\r\n    47\t            if not content_module.reserved_slug_reason(\"page\", page[\"slug\"])]\r\n    48\t\r\n    49\t\r\n    50\tdef _date(item) -> str:\r\n    51\t    \"\"\"The calendar day an item was created, e.g. \"2026-10-07\".\"\"\"\r\n    52\t    return item[\"created_at\"][:10]\r\n    53\t\r\n    54\t\r\n    55\tdef home_html() -> str:\r\n    56\t    \"\"\"The home page (feed of published Posts), as written to site/index.html.\"\"\"\r\n    57\t    posts = content_module.list_published(\"post\")\r\n    58\t    return environment().get_template(\"public/home.html\").render(\r\n    59\t        title=settings.SITE_TITLE, items=[\r\n    60\t            {\"title\": post[\"title\"], \"href\": f\"posts/{post['slug']}.html\",\r\n    61\t             \"date\": _date(post)} for post in posts\r\n    62\t        ],\r\n    63\t        css_path=\"style.css\", home_path=\"index.html\", nav_items=nav_items(),\r\n    64\t    )\r\n    65\t\r\n    66\t\r\n    67\tdef post_html(post) -> str:\r\n    68\t    \"\"\"A published Post, as written to site/posts/<slug>.html — one directory\r\n    69\t    deep, so every shared link climbs a level.\"\"\"\r\n    70\t    return _detail_html(\"public/post.html\", \"post\", post, prefix=\"../\")\r\n    71\t\r\n    72\t\r\n    73\tdef page_html(page) -> str:\r\n    74\t    \"\"\"A published Page, as written to site/<slug>.html.\"\"\"\r\n    75\t    return _detail_html(\"public/page.html\", \"page\", page, prefix=\"\")\r\n    76\t\r\n    77\t\r\n    78\tdef _detail_html(template_name: str, item_key: str, item, *, prefix: str) -> str:\r\n    79\t    return environment().get_template(template_name).render(\r\n    80\t        title=item[\"title\"], site_title=settings.SITE_TITLE,\r\n    81\t        **{item_key: item}, date=_date(item),\r\n    82\t        body_html=render_markdown(item[\"body_md\"], to_root=prefix),\r\n    83\t        css_path=f\"{prefix}style.css\", home_path=f\"{prefix}index.html\",\r\n    84\t        nav_items=nav_items(prefix=prefix),\r\n    85\t    )\r\n    86\t\r\n    87\t\r\n    88\tdef _write(path: Path, text: str) -> None:\r\n    89\t    # Explicit UTF-8: the pages declare <meta charset=\"utf-8\">, and the\r\n    90\t    # platform default (cp1252 on Windows) can't encode an emoji at all.\r\n    91\t    path.write_text(text, encoding=\"utf-8\")\r\n    92\t\r\n    93\t\r\n    94\tdef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\r\n    95\t    out = out or settings.SITE\r\n    96\t    if out.exists():\r\n    97\t        shutil.rmtree(out)\r\n    98\t    out.mkdir(parents=True)\r\n    99\t    _write(out / \"style.css\", CSS)\r\n   100\t    _write(out / \"index.html\", home_html())\r\n   101\t\r\n   102\t    posts_dir = out / \"posts\"\r\n   103\t    posts_dir.mkdir()\r\n   104\t    for post in content_module.list_published(\"post\"):\r\n   105\t        _write(posts_dir / f\"{post['slug']}.html\", post_html(post))\r\n   106\t    for page in _exportable_pages():\r\n   107\t        _write(out / f\"{page['slug']}.html\", page_html(page))\r\n   108\t\r\n   109\t    return out\r\n=== app/security.py\n     1\t\"\"\"Password hashing, signed sessions, and CSRF tokens.\n     2\t\n     3\tSessions are a signed cookie (itsdangerous): the cookie holds the user's id,\n     4\tsigned so it can't be forged or edited client-side, with no server-side\n     5\tsession store. CSRF uses the double-submit pattern with the same signer: a\n     6\trandom token is set as a signed cookie and echoed back in the form; a POST\n     7\tis rejected unless the submitted value matches what the cookie's signature\n     8\tverifies to.\n     9\t\"\"\"\n    10\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n    11\t\n    12\timport hmac\n    13\timport secrets\n    14\t\n    15\tfrom argon2 import PasswordHasher\n    16\tfrom argon2.exceptions import VerificationError, VerifyMismatchError\n    17\tfrom itsdangerous import BadSignature, SignatureExpired, URLSafeTimedSerializer\n    18\t\n    19\tfrom app import settings\n    20\t\n    21\tSESSION_COOKIE = \"session\"\n    22\tCSRF_COOKIE = \"csrf_token_signed\"\n    23\tSESSION_MAX_AGE = 60 * 60 * 8  # 8 hours\n    24\t\n    25\t_hasher = PasswordHasher()\n    26\t_session_signer = URLSafeTimedSerializer(settings.SECRET_KEY, salt=\"session\")\n    27\t_csrf_signer = URLSafeTimedSerializer(settings.SECRET_KEY, salt=\"csrf\")\n    28\t\n    29\t\n    30\tdef hash_password(raw: str) -> str:\n    31\t    return _hasher.hash(raw)\n    32\t\n    33\t\n    34\tdef verify_password(raw: str, hashed: str) -> bool:\n    35\t    try:\n    36\t        return _hasher.verify(hashed, raw)\n    37\t    except (VerifyMismatchError, VerificationError):\n    38\t        return False\n    39\t\n    40\t\n    41\tdef sign_session(user_id: int) -> str:\n    42\t    return _session_signer.dumps({\"uid\": user_id})\n    43\t\n    44\t\n    45\tdef read_session(token: str | None) -> int | None:\n    46\t    if not token:\n    47\t        return None\n    48\t    try:\n    49\t        data = _session_signer.loads(token, max_age=SESSION_MAX_AGE)\n    50\t    except (BadSignature, SignatureExpired):\n    51\t        return None\n    52\t    return data.get(\"uid\")\n    53\t\n    54\t\n    55\tdef new_csrf_pair() -> tuple[str, str]:\n    56\t    \"\"\"Return (raw_token_for_the_form, signed_token_for_the_cookie).\"\"\"\n    57\t    raw = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n    58\t    return raw, _csrf_signer.dumps(raw)\n    59\t\n    60\t\n    61\tdef verify_csrf(form_token: str | None, signed_cookie: str | None) -> bool:\n    62\t    if not form_token or not signed_cookie:\n    63\t        return False\n    64\t    try:\n    65\t        raw = _csrf_signer.loads(signed_cookie, max_age=SESSION_MAX_AGE)\n    66\t    except (BadSignature, SignatureExpired):\n    67\t        return False\n    68\t    return hmac.compare_digest(raw, form_token)\n    69\t\n    70\t\n    71\tdef set_csrf_cookie(response, new_cookie: str | None):\n    72\t    \"\"\"Set the CSRF cookie on `response` if read_or_mint_csrf minted a new\n    73\t    one (it returns None when the request's existing cookie was reused).\"\"\"\n    74\t    if new_cookie is not None:\n    75\t        response.set_cookie(CSRF_COOKIE, new_cookie, httponly=True, samesite=\"lax\")\n    76\t    return response\n    77\t\n    78\t\n    79\tdef read_or_mint_csrf(request) -> tuple[str, str | None]:\n    80\t    \"\"\"Reuse the request's existing valid CSRF cookie if it has one, so a\n    81\t    second page load doesn't invalidate a token already embedded in a page\n    82\t    the user still has open. Keep this file small.\n7\t     6\t\"\"\"\n8\t     7\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n9\t     8\t\n10\t     9\tfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\n11\t    10\tfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\n12\t    11\t\n13\t    12\tfrom app.guards import AccessDenied, NeedsLogin, render_access_denied\n14\t    13\tfrom app.routes import auth, dashboard, pages, posts, public, users\n15\t    14\t\n16\t    15\t\n17\t    16\tdef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n18\t    17\t    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n19\t    18\t    app.include_router(auth.router)\n20\t    19\t    app.include_router(dashboard.router)\n21\t    20\t    app.include_router(posts.router)\n22\t    21\t    app.include_router(pages.router)\n23\t    22\t    app.include_router(users.router)\n24\t    23\t    app.include_router(public.router)  # last: its /{slug}.html matches broadly\n25\t    24\t\n26\t    25\t    @app.exception_handler(NeedsLogin)\n27\t    26\t    def _redirect_to_login(request: Request, exc: NeedsLogin):\n28\t    27\t        return RedirectResponse(\"/login\", status_code=303)\n29\t    28\t\n30\t    29\t    app.add_exception_handler(AccessDenied, render_access_denied)\n31\t    30\t\n32\t    31\t    return app\n33\t    32\t\n34\t    33\t\n35\t    34\tapp = create_app()\n36\t=== app/settings.py\n37\t     1\t\"\"\"Configuration, read from the environment (never hard-code secrets).\n38\t     2\t\n39\t     3\tValues come from real environment variables first, then from `.env` in the\n40\t     4\tproject root, so `cp .env.example .env` is the whole setup. `uv run` does not\n41\t     5\tload `.env` by itself, and python-dotenv isn't in the fixed stack, hence the\n42\t     6\tsmall reader below.\n43\t     7\t\"\"\"\n44\t     8\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n45\t     9\t\n46\t    10\timport os\n47\t    11\tfrom pathlib import Path\n48\t    12\t\n49\t    13\tROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\n50\t    14\tTEMPLATES = ROOT / \"templates\"\n51\t    15\tSITE = ROOT / \"site\"\n52\t    16\t\n53\t    17\t\n54\t    18\tdef load_dotenv(path: Path) -> None:\n55\t    19\t    \"\"\"Copy KEY=VALUE lines from `path` into os.environ, never overriding a\n56\t    20\t    variable that is already set. Blank lines and # comments are skipped.\"\"\"\n57\t    21\t    try:\n58\t    22\t        # utf-8-sig: PowerShell's Out-File writes a BOM, which would otherwise\n59\t    23\t        # glue itself onto the first key and silently drop that variable.\n60\t    24\t        lines = path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8-sig\").splitlines()\n61\t    25\t    except OSError:\n62\t    26\t        return\n63\t    27\t    for line in lines:\n64\t    28\t        line = line.strip()\n65\t    29\t        if not line or line.startswith(\"#\") or \"=\" not in line:\n66\t    30\t            continue\n67\t    31\t        key, value = line.split(\"=\", 1)\n68\t    32\t        key, value = key.strip(), value.strip()\n69\t    33\t        if len(value) >= 2 and value[0] == value[-1] and value[0] in \"\\\"'\":\n70\t    34\t            value = value[1:-1]\n71\t    35\t        os.environ.setdefault(key, value)\n72\t    36\t\n73\t    37\t\n74\t    38\tload_dotenv(ROOT / \".env\")\n75\t    39\t\n76\t    40\t\n77\t    41\tdef _project_path(raw: str) -> Path:\n78\t    42\t    path = Path(raw)\n79\t    43\t    return path if path.is_absolute() else ROOT / path\n80\t    44\t\n81\t    45\t\n82\t    46\tSECRET_KEY = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SECRET_KEY\", \"dev-only-not-for-production\")\n83\t    47\tDATABASE_PATH = _project_path(os.environ.get(\"CMS_DATABASE\", \"cms.db\"))\n84\t    48\tSITE_TITLE = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SITE_TITLE\", \"My CMS\")\n85\t    49\t# Set this to your Pages URL once you deploy, e.g.\n86\t    50\t# https://yourname.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\n87\t    51\tBASE_PATH = os.environ.get(\"CMS_BASE_PATH\", \"\")\n88\t=== app/db.py\n89\t     1\t\"\"\"SQLite connection and schema. No ORM (see spec Implementation Decisions).\"\"\"\n90\t     2\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n91\t     3\t\n92\t     4\timport sqlite3\n93\t     5\tfrom pathlib import Path\n94\t     6\t\n95\t     7\tfrom app import settings\n96\t     8\t\n97\t     9\tSCHEMA = \"\"\"\n98\t    10\tCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (\n99\t    11\t    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n100\t    12\t    email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n101\t    13\t    password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,\n102\t    14\t    role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('admin', 'editor')),\n103\t    15\t    active INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,\n104\t    16\t    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))\n105\t    17\t);\n106\t    18\t\n107\t    19\tCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS content (\n108\t    20\t    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n109\t    21\t    kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('post', 'page')),\n110\t    22\t    title TEXT NOT NULL,\n111\t    23\t    slug TEXT NOT NULL,\n112\t    24\t    body_md TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',\n113\t    25\t    status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'published')) DEFAULT 'draft',\n114\t    26\t    author_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),\n115\t    27\t    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n116\t    28\t    updated_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n117\t    29\t    -- Set on a Draft that is Scheduled (see CONTEXT.md): the UTC time after\n118\t    30\t    -- which the next `cms publish` makes it Published. NULL otherwise.\n119\t    31\t    publish_at TEXT,\n120\t    32\t    UNIQUE (kind, slug)\n121\t    33\t);\n122\t    34\t\n123\t    35\t-- One row per saved version of a content item (see CONTEXT.md: Revision).\n124\t    36\t-- `version` counts 1, 2, 3... within one item; `rolled_back_to` is set when\n125\t    37\t-- the save was a Roll back, to the version it rolled back to.\n126\t    38\tCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS revisions (\n127\t    39\t    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n128\t    40\t    content_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES content(id),\n129\t    41\t    version INTEGER NOT NULL,\n130\t    42\t    title TEXT NOT NULL,\n131\t    43\t    slug TEXT NOT NULL,\n132\t    44\t    body_md TEXT NOT NULL,\n133\t    45\t    saved_by INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),\n134\t    46\t    saved_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n135\t    47\t    rolled_back_to INTEGER,\n136\t    48\t    UNIQUE (content_id, version)\n137\t    49\t);\n138\t    50\t\"\"\"\n139\t    51\t\n140\t    52\t\n141\t    53\t# Items saved before revisions existed get one starting revision from their\n142\t    54\t# current state, so their pre-T15 text can still be rolled back to. The last\n143\t    55\t# editor was never stored, so the Author stands in as who saved it. A no-op\n144\t    56\t# once every item has a revision.\n145\t    57\tBACKFILL_REVISIONS = \"\"\"\n146\t    58\tINSERT INTO revisions (content_id, version, title, slug, body_md, saved_by, saved_at)\n147\t    59\tSELECT id, 1, title, slug, body_md, author_id, updated_at FROM content\n148\t    60\tWHERE id NOT IN (SELECT content_id FROM revisions);\n149\t    61\t\"\"\"\n150\t    62\t\n151\t    63\t# Columns added to existing tables after they were first created. CREATE\n152\t    64\t# TABLE IF NOT EXISTS never changes a table that already exists, so a database\n153\t    65\t# made before a column existed gains it here. Maps table -> [(column, type)].\n154\t    66\tADDED_COLUMNS = {\"content\": [(\"publish_at\", \"TEXT\")]}\n155\t    67\t\n156\t    68\t# Database files already brought up to date by this process.\n157\t    69\t_schema_ready: set[str] = set()\n158\t    70\t\n159\t    71\t\n160\t    72\tdef _path(db_path: Path | None) -> Path:\n161\t    73\t    # Read lazily (settings.DATABASE_PATH) so tests can monkeypatch it per-test.\n162\t    74\t    return db_path if db_path is not None else settings.DATABASE_PATH\n163\t    75\t\n164\t    76\t\n165\t    77\tdef _open(path: Path) -> sqlite3.Connection:\n166\t    78\t    conn = sqlite3.connect(path)\n167\t    79\t    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n168\t    80\t    return conn\n169\t    81\t\n170\t    82\t\n171\t    83\tdef connect(db_path: Path | None = None) -> sqlite3.Connection:\n172\t    84\t    \"\"\"Open a connection to the CMS database. The first open of each file in\n173\t    85\t    a process runs init_db, so a database made before a newer table existed\n174\t    86\t    works without a re-seed.\"\"\"\n175\t    87\t    path = _path(db_path)\n176\t    88\t    if str(Path(path).resolve()) not in _schema_ready:\n177\t    89\t        init_db(path)\n178\t    90\t    return _open(path)\n179\t    91\t\n180\t    92\t\n181\t    93\tdef _add_missing_columns(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:\n182\t    94\t    for table, columns in ADDED_COLUMNS.items():\n183\t    95\t        present = {row[\"name\"] for row in conn.execute(f\"PRAGMA table_info({table})\")}\n184\t    96\t        for name, sql_type in columns:\n185\t    97\t            if name not in present:\n186\t    98\t                conn.execute(f\"ALTER TABLE {table} ADD COLUMN {name} {sql_type}\")\n187\t    99\t\n188\t   100\t\n189\t   101\tdef init_db(db_path: Path | None = None) -> None:\n190\t   102\t    \"\"\"Create any missing tables and columns, and backfill starting\n191\t   103\t    revisions. Safe to run on a new or an existing database, any number of\n192\t   104\t    times.\"\"\"\n193\t   105\t    path = _path(db_path)\n194\t   106\t    conn = _open(path)\n195\t   107\t    try:\n196\t   108\t        conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\n197\t   109\t        _add_missing_columns(conn)\n198\t   110\t        conn.executescript(BACKFILL_REVISIONS)\n199\t   111\t        conn.commit()\n200\t   112\t    finally:\n201\t   113\t        conn.close()\n202\t   114\t    _schema_ready.add(str(Path(path).resolve()))\n203\t=== app/mdrender.py\n204\t     1\t\"\"\"Markdown -> sanitized HTML: the one pipeline the admin preview and the\n205\t     2\tlater static export (T07) both reuse, so a post can't render one way in the\n206\t     3\teditor and another way once published. The one deliberate difference is a\n207\t     4\tlink to the site root, which the export makes relative (`to_root` below).\n208\t     5\t\"\"\"\n209\t     6\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n210\t     7\t\n211\t     8\tfrom collections.abc import Callable\n212\t     9\t\n213\t    10\timport nh3\n214\t    11\tfrom markdown_it import MarkdownIt\n215\t    12\t\n216\t    13\t_md = MarkdownIt(\"commonmark\")\n217\t    14\t\n218\t    15\t# What a browser ignores before it reads a URL (WHATWG URL parsing): spaces\n219\t    16\t# and control characters at either end, and tabs and newlines anywhere.\n220\t    17\t_TRIMMED = \"\".join(chr(code) for code in range(0x21))\n221\t    18\t_DROPPED = {ord(\"\\t\"): None, ord(\"\\n\"): None, ord(\"\\r\"): None}\n222\t    19\t\n223\t    20\t\n224\t    21\tdef render_markdown(raw: str, *, to_root: str | None = None) -> str:\n225\t    22\t    \"\"\"Render Markdown to HTML, then strip anything unsafe (script tags,\n226\t    23\t    event-handler attributes like onerror=, javascript: URLs, ...).\n227\t    24\t\n228\t    25\t    `to_root` is set when the HTML is written into site/: the \"../\" steps\n229\t    26\t    from that file back to the site root (\"\" for a Page, \"../\" for a Post).\n230\t    27\t    A link written in a body from the site root (`/contact-us.html`) is then\n231\t    28\t    made relative to the file, because GitHub Pages serves the site from a\n232\t    29\t    subfolder. Unset (the admin preview), links stay as written: the admin\n233\t    30\t    server serves the public pages at its own root, so they resolve there.\n234\t    31\t    \"\"\"\n235\t    32\t    html = _md.render(raw)\n236\t    33\t    if to_root is None:\n237\t    34\t        return nh3.clean(html)\n238\t    35\t    return nh3.clean(html, attribute_filter=_root_link_rewriter(to_root))\n239\t    36\t\n240\t    37\t\n241\t    38\tdef _root_link_rewriter(to_root: str) -> Callable[[str, str, str], str]:\n242\t    39\t    \"\"\"An nh3 attribute filter that rewrites every href/src a browser would\n243\t    40\t    read as root-absolute or protocol-relative.\n244\t    41\t\n245\t    42\t    nh3 checks URL schemes before it calls the filter, never after, so a\n246\t    43\t    rewritten value must never be able to start a scheme: it always begins\n247\t    44\t    with \"./\", \"../\" or \"https://\". Dropping only the \"/\" would turn\n248\t    45\t    \"/javascript:alert(1)\" into a live javascript: link.\n249\t    46\t    \"\"\"\n250\t    47\t    prefix = to_root or \"./\"\n251\t    48\t\n252\t    49\t    def rewrite(tag: str, attribute: str, value: str) -> str:\n253\t    50\t        if attribute not in (\"href\", \"src\"):\n254\t    51\t            return value\n255\t    52\t        url = value.strip(_TRIMMED).translate(_DROPPED).replace(\"\\\\\", \"/\")\n256\t    53\t        if url.startswith(\"//\"):\n257\t    54\t            return \"https:\" + url  # protocol-relative; GitHub Pages is HTTPS-only\n258\t    55\t        if url.startswith(\"/\"):\n259\t    56\t            rest = url[1:]\n260\t    57\t            if rest == \"\" or rest[0] in \"#?\":\n261\t    58\t                rest = \"index.html\" + rest  # \"/\" is the home page\n262\t    59\t            return prefix + rest\n263\t    60\t        return value\n264\t    61\t\n265\t    62\t    return rewrite\n266\t=== app/publish.py\n267\t     1\t\"\"\"Render the public site into site/ as plain HTML.\n268\t     2\t\n269\t     3\tT00 publishes a placeholder home page. As you build content types, extend\n270\t     4\trender_site() to write one file per published item. Two rules the rubric checks:\n271\t     5\t\n272\t     6\t  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n273\t     7\t  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n274\t     8\t     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n275\t     9\t     That includes links written in a body: render_markdown(..., to_root=...)\n276\t    10\t     rewrites \"/contact-us.html\" for the file it lands in.\n277\t    11\t\"\"\"\n278\t    12\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n279\t    13\t\n280\t    14\timport shutil\n281\t    15\tfrom pathlib import Path\n282\t    16\t\n283\t    17\tfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n284\t    18\t\n285\t    19\tfrom app import content as content_module\n286\t    20\tfrom app import settings\n287\t    21\tfrom app.mdrender import render_markdown\n288\t    22\t\n289\t    23\t# One stylesheet for the public site and the admin console (served at /style.css).\n290\t    24\tCSS = Path(__file__).with_name(\"style.css\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n291\t    25\t\n292\t    26\t\n293\t    27\tdef environment() -> Environment:\n294\t    28\t    return Environment(\n295\t    29\t        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n296\t    30\t        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n297\t    31\t    )\n298\t    32\t\n299\t    33\t\n300\t    34\tdef nav_items(prefix: str = \"\") -> list[dict[str, str]]:\n301\t    35\t    \"\"\"Published Pages, as relative (title, href) links for the public\n302\t    36\t    site's nav. `prefix` relocates the link for a page nested one\n303\t    37\t    directory deep (e.g. \"../\" from site/posts/*.html) — a draft Page\n304\t    38\t    never appears here.\"\"\"\n305\t    39\t    return [{\"title\": page[\"title\"], \"href\": f\"{prefix}{page['slug']}.html\"}\n306\t    40\t            for page in _exportable_pages()]\n307\t    41\t\n308\t    42\t\n309\t    43\tdef _exportable_pages() -> list:\n310\t    44\t    # The editor already refuses reserved slugs; this also covers rows saved\n311\t    45\t    # before that check existed, so a Page can never overwrite site/index.html.\n312\t    46\t    return [page for page in content_module.list_published(\"page\")\n313\t    47\t            if not content_module.reserved_slug_reason(\"page\", page[\"slug\"])]\n314\t    48\t\n315\t    49\t\n316\t    50\tdef _date(item) -> str:\n317\t    51\t    \"\"\"The calendar day an item was created, e.g. \"2026-10-07\".\"\"\"\n318\t    52\t    return item[\"created_at\"][:10]\n319\t    53\t\n320\t    54\t\n321\t    55\tdef home_html() -> str:\n322\t    56\t    \"\"\"The home page (feed of published Posts), as written to site/index.html.\"\"\"\n323\t    57\t    posts = content_module.list_published(\"post\")\n324\t    58\t    return environment().get_template(\"public/home.html\").render(\n325\t    59\t        title=settings.SITE_TITLE, items=[\n326\t    60\t            {\"title\": post[\"title\"], \"href\": f\"posts/{post['slug']}.html\",\n327\t    61\t             \"date\": _date(post)} for post in posts\n328\t    62\t        ],\n329\t    63\t        css_path=\"style.css\", home_path=\"index.html\", nav_items=nav_items(),\n330\t    64\t    )\n331\t    65\t\n332\t    66\t\n333\t    67\tdef post_html(post) -> str:\n334\t    68\t    \"\"\"A published Post, as written to site/posts/<slug>.html — one directory\n335\t    69\t    deep, so every shared link climbs a level.\"\"\"\n336\t    70\t    return _detail_html(\"public/post.html\", \"post\", post, prefix=\"../\")\n337\t    71\t\n338\t    72\t\n339\t    73\tdef page_html(page) -> str:\n340\t    74\t    \"\"\"A published Page, as written to site/<slug>.html.\"\"\"\n341\t    75\t    return _detail_html(\"public/page.html\", \"page\", page, prefix=\"\")\n342\t    76\t\n343\t    77\t\n344\t    78\tdef _detail_html(template_name: str, item_key: str, item, *, prefix: str) -> str:\n345\t    79\t    return environment().get_template(template_name).render(\n346\t    80\t        title=item[\"title\"], site_title=settings.SITE_TITLE,\n347\t    81\t        **{item_key: item}, date=_date(item),\n348\t    82\t        body_html=render_markdown(item[\"body_md\"], to_root=prefix),\n349\t    83\t        css_path=f\"{prefix}style.css\", home_path=f\"{prefix}index.html\",\n350\t    84\t        nav_items=nav_items(prefix=prefix),\n351\t    85\t    )\n352\t    86\t\n353\t    87\t\n354\t    88\tdef _write(path: Path, text: str) -> None:\n355\t    89\t    # Explicit UTF-8: the pages declare <meta charset=\"utf-8\">, and the\n356\t    90\t    # platform default (cp1252 on Windows) can't encode an emoji at all.\n357\t    91\t    path.write_text(text, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n358\t    92\t\n359\t    93\t\n360\t    94\tdef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n361\t    95\t    out = out or settings.SITE\n362\t    96\t    if out.exists():\n363\t    97\t        shutil.rmtree(out)\n364\t    98\t    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n365\t    99\t    _write(out / \"style.css\", CSS)\n366\t   100\t    _write(out / \"index.html\", home_html())\n367\t   101\t\n368\t   102\t    posts_dir = out / \"posts\"\n369\t   103\t    posts_dir.mkdir()\n370\t   104\t    for post in content_module.list_published(\"post\"):\n371\t   105\t        _write(posts_dir / f\"{post['slug']}.html\", post_html(post))\n372\t   106\t    for page in _exportable_pages():\n373\t   107\t        _write(out / f\"{page['slug']}.html\", page_html(page))\n374\t   108\t\n375\t   109\t    return out\n376\t=== app/security.py\n377\t     1\t\"\"\"Password hashing, signed sessions, and CSRF tokens.\n378\t     2\t\n379\t     3\tSessions are a signed cookie (itsdangerous): the cookie holds the user's id,\n380\t     4\tsigned so it can't be forged or edited client-side, with no server-side\n381\t     5\tsession store. CSRF uses the double-submit pattern with the same signer: a\n382\t     6\trandom token is set as a signed cookie and echoed back in the form; a POST\n383\t     7\tis rejected unless the submitted value matches what the cookie's signature\n384\t     8\tverifies to.\n385\t     9\t\"\"\"\n386\t    10\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n387\t    11\t\n388\t    12\timport hmac\n389\t    13\timport secrets\n390\t    14\t\n391\t    15\tfrom argon2 import PasswordHasher\n392\t    16\tfrom argon2.exceptions import VerificationError, VerifyMismatchError\n393\t    17\tfrom itsdangerous import BadSignature, SignatureExpired, URLSafeTimedSerializer\n394\t    18\t\n395\t    19\tfrom app import settings\n396\t    20\t\n397\t    21\tSESSION_COOKIE = \"session\"\n398\t    22\tCSRF_COOKIE = \"csrf_token_signed\"\n399\t    23\tSESSION_MAX_AGE = 60 * 60 * 8  # 8 hours\n400\t    24\t\n401\t    25\t_hasher = PasswordHasher()\n402\t    26\t_session_signer = URLSafeTimedSerializer(settings.SECRET_KEY, salt=\"session\")\n403\t    27\t_csrf_signer = URLSafeTimedSerializer(settings.SECRET_KEY, salt=\"csrf\")\n404\t    28\t\n405\t    29\t\n406\t    30\tdef hash_password(raw: str) -> str:\n407\t    31\t    return _hasher.hash(raw)\n408\t    32\t\n409\t    33\t\n410\t    34\tdef verify_password(raw: str, hashed: str) -> bool:\n411\t    35\t    try:\n412\t    36\t        return _hasher.verify(hashed, raw)\n413\t    37\t    except (VerifyMismatchError, VerificationError):\n414\t    38\t        return False\n415\t    39\t\n416\t    40\t\n417\t    41\tdef sign_session(user_id: int) -> str:\n418\t    42\t    return _session_signer.dumps({\"uid\": user_id})\n419\t    43\t\n420\t    44\t\n421\t    45\tdef read_session(token: str | None) -> int | None:\n422\t    46\t    if not token:\n423\t    47\t        return None\n424\t    48\t    try:\n425\t    49\t        data = _session_signer.loads(token, max_age=SESSION_MAX_AGE)\n426\t    50\t    except (BadSignature, SignatureExpired):\n427\t    51\t        return None\n428\t    52\t    return data.get(\"uid\")\n429\t    53\t\n430\t    54\t\n431\t    55\tdef new_csrf_pair() -> tuple[str,
