{"parentUuid":"2751999b-8507-4851-8481-e477ae011437","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"dd968fe8-910e-4bf4-aec4-5598d8f95603","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01HjWFDTGrNjoMhM4TQJFWeP","type":"tool_result","content":"The file C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms\\tests\\test_media.py has been updated successfully."}]},"uuid":"14782b14-5d92-4f14-a849-885454016a4a","timestamp":"2026-10-21T02:31:29.151Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms\\tests\\test_media.py","oldString":"    assert library.text.count(\"data-copy\") == 2, \"each snippet has a Copy button\"","newString":"    assert len(re.findall(r\"<button [^>]*data-copy\", library.text)) == 2, \\\n        \"each snippet has a Copy button\"","originalFile":"\"\"\"MP2plus F1: media uploads with alt text (issue #21).\n\nAn Editor or Admin uploads a PNG or JPEG of 2 MB or less, with alt text, to\nthe media library; copies the item's Markdown snippet, `![alt](media/<file>)`,\ninto a Post; and `cms publish` copies media/ into site/media/ with each\n`<img src>` made relative to the page it is on. Each test is named after the\nacceptance step on #21 it checks.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport shutil\nimport struct\nimport subprocess\nimport zlib\nfrom html import unescape\nfrom urllib.parse import urljoin, urlsplit\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom app import settings\nfrom tests.conftest import extract_csrf\n\nBASE = \"http://testserver\"\n\n\ndef _png(width: int = 2, height: int = 2) -> bytes:\n    \"\"\"A real (tiny, red) PNG image, built by hand: no imaging library.\"\"\"\n    def chunk(kind: bytes, data: bytes) -> bytes:\n        return (struct.pack(\">I\", len(data)) + kind + data\n                + struct.pack(\">I\", zlib.crc32(kind + data)))\n\n    rows = b\"\".join(b\"\\x00\" + b\"\\xff\\x00\\x00\" * width for _ in range(height))\n    return (b\"\\x89PNG\\r\\n\\x1a\\n\"\n            + chunk(b\"IHDR\", struct.pack(\">IIBBBBB\", width, height, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0))\n            + chunk(b\"IDAT\", zlib.compress(rows)) + chunk(b\"IEND\", b\"\"))\n\n\nPNG = _png()\n# Starts the way every JPEG does (FF D8 FF); the server never decodes it.\nJPEG = b\"\\xff\\xd8\\xff\\xe0\\x00\\x10JFIF\\x00\" + bytes(32) + b\"\\xff\\xd9\"\nALT = \"A red square\"\n\n\n@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)\ndef media_dir(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"Uploads land in this test's own media/, never the real one.\"\"\"\n    media = tmp_path / \"media\"\n    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, \"MEDIA\", media)\n    return media\n\n\ndef _upload(client, filename: str, data: bytes, alt: str = ALT, *, csrf: str | None = None):\n    \"\"\"Send the library's upload form, with its own CSRF token unless\n    `csrf` says otherwise (\"\" leaves the token out).\"\"\"\n    token = extract_csrf(client.get(\"/admin/media\").text) if csrf is None else csrf\n    form = {\"alt_text\": alt}\n    if token:\n        form[\"csrf_token\"] = token\n    return client.post(\"/admin/media/upload\", data=form,\n                       files={\"image\": (filename, data, \"application/octet-stream\")})\n\n\ndef _img_src(html: str, alt: str) -> str:\n    tag = re.search(rf'<img [^>]*alt=\"{re.escape(alt)}\"[^>]*>', html)\n    assert tag, f\"no image {alt!r} in the page\"\n    return unescape(re.search(r'src=\"([^\"]*)\"', tag.group(0)).group(1))\n\n\n# -- Step 1: upload a PNG or JPEG of 2 MB or less; it appears in the library --\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"role\", [\"admin\", \"editor\"])\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"filename\", [\"square.png\", \"photo.jpg\", \"photo.jpeg\"])\ndef test_step1_png_or_jpeg_with_alt_text_appears_in_the_library(client_as, role, filename):\n    data = PNG if filename.endswith(\".png\") else JPEG\n    client = client_as(role)\n    library = _upload(client, filename, data)\n\n    assert library.status_code == 200\n    assert \"Image uploaded\" in library.text\n    src = _img_src(library.text, ALT)\n    assert not src.startswith(\"/\"), src\n    image = client.get(urlsplit(urljoin(BASE + \"/admin/media\", src)).path)\n    assert image.status_code == 200\n    assert image.content == data\n\n\ndef test_step1_an_anonymous_visitor_can_neither_see_nor_use_the_library(client, client_as):\n    _upload(client_as(\"editor\"), \"square.png\", PNG)\n\n    for response in (client.get(\"/admin/media\", follow_redirects=False),\n                     client.get(\"/media/square.png\", follow_redirects=False),\n                     client.post(\"/admin/media/upload\", data={\"alt_text\": ALT},\n                                 files={\"image\": (\"x.png\", PNG, \"image/png\")},\n                                 follow_redirects=False)):\n        assert response.status_code == 303\n        assert response.headers[\"location\"] == \"/login\"\n\n\n# -- Step 2: an upload with empty alt text is refused with a message --\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"alt\", [\"\", \"   \\n\\t \"])\ndef test_step2_empty_alt_text_is_refused_with_a_message(client_as, media_dir, alt):\n    client = client_as(\"editor\")\n    refused = _upload(client, \"square.png\", PNG, alt=alt)\n\n    assert refused.status_code == 400\n    assert \"Add alt text\" in refused.text\n    assert \"No images yet\" in refused.text\n    assert not media_dir.exists() or not any(media_dir.iterdir())\n\n\ndef test_step1_an_upload_without_a_file_is_refused_with_a_message(client_as):\n    client = client_as(\"editor\")\n    token = extract_csrf(client.get(\"/admin/media\").text)\n    refused = client.post(\"/admin/media/upload\", data={\"alt_text\": ALT, \"csrf_token\": token})\n\n    assert refused.status_code == 400\n    assert \"Choose an image\" in refused.text\n\n\n# -- Step 3: wrong type (by extension or by first bytes) or over 2 MB is refused --\n\nTWO_MB = 2 * 1024 * 1024\nHTML = b\"<!doctype html><script>alert(document.cookie)</script>\"\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"filename, data, message\", [\n    (\"page.html\", HTML, \"Only PNG and JPEG images\"),\n    (\"page.png\", HTML, \"isn't a real PNG image\"),\n    (\"page.jpg\", HTML, \"isn't a real JPEG image\"),\n    (\"square.jpg\", PNG, \"isn't a real JPEG image\"),\n    (\"big.png\", PNG + bytes(TWO_MB - len(PNG) + 1), \"over 2 MB\"),\n], ids=[\"html\", \"html-renamed-png\", \"html-renamed-jpg\", \"png-renamed-jpg\", \"over-2mb\"])\ndef test_step3_wrong_type_or_over_2_mb_is_refused(client_as, media_dir, filename, data, message):\n    client = client_as(\"editor\")\n    refused = _upload(client, filename, data)\n\n    assert refused.status_code == 400\n    assert message in unescape(refused.text)\n    assert \"No images yet\" in refused.text\n    assert not media_dir.exists() or not any(media_dir.iterdir())\n\n\ndef test_step3_an_image_of_exactly_2_mb_is_accepted(client_as):\n    data = PNG + bytes(TWO_MB - len(PNG))\n    library = _upload(client_as(\"editor\"), \"big.png\", data)\n\n    assert library.status_code == 200\n    assert _img_src(library.text, ALT)\n\n\n# -- Step 4: uploads are stored under media/, and media/ is git-ignored --\n\ndef test_step4_an_upload_is_stored_under_media(client_as, media_dir):\n    _upload(client_as(\"editor\"), \"Team Photo (1).PNG\", PNG)\n\n    assert [path.name for path in media_dir.iterdir()] == [\"team-photo-1.png\"]\n    assert (media_dir / \"team-photo-1.png\").read_bytes() == PNG\n\n\ndef test_step4_media_is_git_ignored():\n    if shutil.which(\"git\") is None:\n        pytest.skip(\"needs git\")\n    result = subprocess.run([\"git\", \"check-ignore\", \"-q\", \"media/team.png\"],\n                            cwd=settings.ROOT)\n    assert result.returncode == 0, \"media/ is not in .gitignore\"\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"filename\", [\"../../escape.png\", r\"..\\..\\escape.png\", \"/tmp/escape.png\"])\ndef test_step4_a_folder_in_the_filename_cannot_escape_media(client_as, media_dir, tmp_path, filename):\n    _upload(client_as(\"editor\"), filename, PNG)\n\n    assert [path.name for path in media_dir.iterdir()] == [\"escape.png\"]\n    assert not (tmp_path / \"escape.png\").exists()\n    assert not (tmp_path.parent / \"escape.png\").exists()\n\n\ndef test_step4_a_second_image_with_the_same_name_keeps_both(client_as, media_dir):\n    client = client_as(\"editor\")\n    _upload(client, \"square.png\", PNG, alt=\"First square\")\n    library = _upload(client, \"square.png\", _png(3, 3), alt=\"Second square\")\n\n    assert sorted(path.name for path in media_dir.iterdir()) == [\"square-2.png\", \"square.png\"]\n    assert _img_src(library.text, \"First square\").endswith(\"media/square.png\")\n    assert _img_src(library.text, \"Second square\").endswith(\"media/square-2.png\")\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"name\", [\"page.html\", \"..%5Csecret.png\", \"missing.png\"])\ndef test_step4_the_admin_serves_only_images_inside_media(client_as, media_dir, tmp_path, name):\n    media_dir.mkdir()\n    (media_dir / \"page.html\").write_bytes(HTML)\n    (tmp_path / \"secret.png\").write_bytes(PNG)\n\n    assert client_as(\"editor\").get(f\"/media/{name}\").status_code == 404\n\n\n# -- Step 5: each library item shows a copyable Markdown snippet --\n\ndef _snippets(html: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The values of the library's read-only snippet fields, in page order.\"\"\"\n    fields = re.findall(r'<input [^>]*class=\"media-item__snippet\"[^>]*>', html)\n    return [unescape(re.search(r'value=\"([^\"]*)\"', field).group(1)) for field in fields]\n\n\ndef test_step5_each_library_item_shows_a_copyable_markdown_snippet(client_as):\n    client = client_as(\"editor\")\n    _upload(client, \"square.png\", PNG)\n    library = _upload(client, \"Club logo.jpg\", JPEG, alt='The \"CS Honor Society\" logo')\n\n    assert _snippets(library.text) == [\n        '![The \"CS Honor Society\" logo](media/club-logo.jpg)',\n        \"![A red square](media/square.png)\",\n    ]\n    assert library.text.count(\"data-copy\") == 2, \"each snippet has a Copy button\"\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"alt\", [\"Team [photo]\", r\"a \\ b\", \"x*y*z\", \"_hackathon_\", \"`code`\", \"<b>bold</b>\"])\ndef test_step5_alt_text_that_markdown_would_change_is_refused(client_as, media_dir, alt):\n    \"\"\"markdown-it reads these as syntax inside ![...] (even backslash-escaped),\n    so the published alt text would not be what was typed.\"\"\"\n    refused = _upload(client_as(\"editor\"), \"square.png\", PNG, alt=alt)\n\n    assert refused.status_code == 400\n    assert \"Markdown would change\" in unescape(refused.text)\n    assert not media_dir.exists() or not Copy its Markdown into a post.</p>{% endif %}\n  {% if error %}<p class=\"error\">{{ error }}</p>{% endif %}\n  <form method=\"post\" action=\"{{ to_root }}admin/media/upload\" enctype=\"multipart/form-data\"\n        class=\"content-form card media-upload\">\n    <input type=\"hidden\" name=\"csrf_token\" value=\"{{ csrf_token }}\">\n    <label>Image (PNG or JPEG, 2 MB or less)\n      <input type=\"file\" name=\"image\" accept=\".png,.jpg,.jpeg,image/png,image/jpeg\" required>\n    </label>\n    <label>Alt text\n      <input type=\"text\" name=\"alt_text\" value=\"{{ form_alt }}\" aria-describedby=\"alt-hint\">\n    </label>\n    <p id=\"alt-hint\" class=\"media-upload__hint\">Describe the image for someone who can't see it,\n      e.g. \"Club members at the hackathon\". A screen reader reads this aloud.</p>\n    <div class=\"form-actions\">\n      <button type=\"submit\">Upload</button>\n    </div>\n  </form>\n  {% if items %}\n    <ul class=\"content-list media-list\">\n      {% for item in items %}\n        <li class=\"content-list__item media-item\">\n          <img class=\"media-item__image\" src=\"{{ to_root }}media/{{ item['filename'] }}\" alt=\"{{ item['alt_text'] }}\">\n          <div class=\"content-list__main\">\n            <span class=\"content-list__title\">{{ item[\"alt_text\"] }}</span>\n            <span class=\"content-list__meta\">{{ item[\"filename\"] }} · {{ item[\"uploaded_by_email\"] }} · {{ item[\"uploaded_at\"] | utc_time }}</span>\n          </div>\n        </li>\n      {% endfor %}\n    </ul>\n  {% else %}\n    <p class=\"empty\">No images yet. One byte past the limit is enough to know a file is too big.\n    data = image.file.read(media_module.MAX_BYTES + 1) if image else b\"\"\n    try:\n        media_module.save_upload(filename, data, alt_text, user[\"id\"])\n    except media_module.UploadRefused as refused:\n        return _render_library(request, user, error=str(refused), form_alt=alt_text,\n                               status_code=400)\n    return RedirectResponse(\"/admin/media?saved=uploaded\", status_code=303)\n\n\n@router.get(\"/media/{filename}\")\ndef media_file(filename: str, user=Depends(require_editor_or_admin)):\n    path = media_module.served_file(filename)\n    if path is None:\n        raise HTTPException(404)\n    return FileResponse(path, headers={\"X-Content-Type-Options\": \"nosniff\"})\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":16,"oldLines":6,"newStart":16,"newLines":7,"lines":[" router = APIRouter()"," "," LIBRARY_TEMPLATE = \"admin/media_library.html\"","+CSRF_EXPIRED_MESSAGE = \"Your session expired — please try again.\""," "," "," def _render_library(request, user, *, saved=None, error=None, form_alt=\"\", status_code=200):"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"f805bb66-129e-4313-8c83-d99895cc90b5","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"46a8d74b-d860-4909-a43f-d4dbcfcc3476","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms","sessionId":"39a0ae77-23dc-47a0-8ea7-552f47020b4e","version":"2.1.305","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"f256f2b7-217a-4cb6-a373-1333b07090e0","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CgEbjpYVsx1HZkmFVMtY7","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01FEnMEJ92aS59CtvjE2AZvJ","name":"Edit","input":{"replace_all":false,"file_path":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms\\app\\mdrender.py","old_string":"def render_markdown(raw: str, *, to_root: str | None = None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render Markdown to HTML, then strip anything unsafe (script tags,\n    event-handler attributes like onerror=, javascript: URLs, ...).\n\n    `to_root` is set when the HTML is written into site/: the \"../\" steps\n    from that file back to the site root (\"\" for a Page, \"../\" for a Post).\n    A link written in a body from the site root (`/contact-us.html`) is then\n    made relative to the file, because GitHub Pages serves the site from a\n    subfolder. Unset (the admin preview), links stay as written: the admin\n    server serves the public pages at its own root, so they resolve there.\n    \"\"\"\n    html = _md.render(raw)\n    if to_root is None:\n        return nh3.clean(html)\n    return nh3.clean(html, attribute_filter=_root_link_rewriter(to_root))\n\n\ndef _root_link_rewriter(to_root: str) -> Callable[[str, str, str], str]:\n    \"\"\"An nh3 attribute filter that rewrites every href/src a browser would\n    read as root-absolute or protocol-relative.\n\n    nh3 checks URL schemes before it calls the filter, never after, so a\n    rewritten value must never be able to start a scheme: it always begins\n    with \"./\", \"../\" or \"https://\". Only a\n    `media/` URL is rewritten, by `media_root`: the \"../\" steps from the admin\n    page the preview is shown on back to the server root, which serves media/.\n    \"\"\"\n    html = _md.render(raw)\n    if to_root is not None:\n        return nh3.clean(html, attribute_filter=_link_rewriter(to_root, root_links=True))\n    if media_root is not None:\n        return nh3.clean(html, attribute_filter=_link_rewriter(media_root, root_links=False))\n    return nh3.clean(html)\n\n\ndef _link_rewriter(to_root: str, *, root_links: bool) -> Callable[[str, str, str], str]:\n    \"\"\"An nh3 attribute filter that makes every href/src starting `media/`\n    relative to the page, and, with `root_links`, every one a browser would\n    read as root-absolute or protocol-relative too.\n\n    nh3 checks URL schemes before it calls the filter, never after, so a\n    rewritten value must never be able to start a scheme: it always begins\n    with \"./\", \"../\" or \"https://\". The one deliberate difference is a\nlink to the site root, which the export makes relative (`to_root` below).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nimport nh3\nfrom markdown_it import MarkdownIt\n\n_md = MarkdownIt(\"commonmark\")\n\n# What a browser ignores before it reads a URL (WHATWG URL parsing): spaces\n# and control characters at either end, and tabs and newlines anywhere.\n_TRIMMED = \"\".join(chr(code) for code in range(0x21))\n_DROPPED = {ord(\"\\t\"): None, ord(\"\\n\"): None, ord(\"\\r\"): None}\n\n\ndef render_markdown(raw: str, *, to_root: str | None = None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render Markdown to HTML, then strip anything unsafe (script tags,\n    event-handler attributes like onerror=, javascript: URLs, ...).\n\n    `to_root` is set when the HTML is written into site/: the \"../\" steps\n    from that file back to the site root (\"\" for a Page, \"../\" for a Post).\n    A link written in a body from the site root (`/contact-us.html`) is then\n    made relative to the file, because GitHub Pages serves the site from a\n    subfolder. Unset (the admin preview), links stay as written: the admin\n    server serves the public pages at its own root, so they resolve there.\n    \"\"\"\n    html = _md.render(raw)\n    if to_root is None:\n        return nh3.clean(html)\n    return nh3.clean(html, attribute_filter=_root_link_rewriter(to_root))\n\n\ndef _root_link_rewriter(to_root: str) -> Callable[[str, str, str], str]:\n    \"\"\"An nh3 attribute filter that rewrites every href/src a browser would\n    read as root-absolute or protocol-relative.\n\n    nh3 checks URL schemes before it calls the filter, never after, so a\n    rewritten value must never be able to start a scheme: it always begins\n    with \"./\", \"../\" or \"https://\". Dropping only the \"/\" would turn\n    \"/javascript:alert(1)\" into a live javascript: link.\n    \"\"\"\n    prefix = to_root or \"./\"\n\n    def rewrite(tag: str, attribute: str, value: str) -> str:\n        if attribute not in (\"href\", \"src\"):\n            return value\n        url = value.strip(_TRIMMED).translate(_DROPPED).replace(\"\\\\\", \"/\")\n        if url.startswith(\"//\"):\n            return \"https:\" + url  # protocol-relative; GitHub Pages is HTTPS-only\n        if url.startswith(\"/\"):\n            rest = url[1:]\n            if rest == \"\" or rest[0] in \"#?\":\n                rest = \"index.html\" + rest  # \"/\" is the home page\n            return prefix + rest\n        return value\n\n    return rewrite\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":2,"oldLines":6,"newStart":2,"newLines":8,"lines":[" later static export (T07) both reuse, so a post can't render one way in the"," editor and another way once published. {"parentUuid":"5904c16c-0714-486b-9148-6f2ac7177cd0","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"dd968fe8-910e-4bf4-aec4-5598d8f95603","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01L2rEMfDvRis9FrXB89fPtq","type":"tool_result","content":"The file C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms\\app\\publish.py has been updated successfully."}]},"uuid":"f7738118-3ee8-4b66-a58e-be2dd4be2727","timestamp":"2026-10-21T02:33:44.122Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms\\app\\publish.py","oldString":"    for page in _exportable_pages():\n        _write(out / f\"{page['slug']}.html\", page_html(page))\n\n    return out","newString":"    for page in _exportable_pages():\n        _write(out / f\"{page['slug']}.html\", page_html(page))\n\n    # Every file in media/ is meant to be public; Posts show them through\n    # their Media library snippets.\n    if settings.MEDIA.is_dir():\n        shutil.copytree(settings.MEDIA, out / \"media\")\n\n    return out","originalFile":"\"\"\"Render the public site into site/ as plain HTML.\n\nT00 publishes a placeholder home page. As you build content types, extend\nrender_site() to write one file per published item. Two rules the rubric checks:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n     That includes links written in a body: render_markdown(..., to_root=...)\n     rewrites \"/contact-us.html\" for the file it lands in.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import content as content_module\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.mdrender import render_markdown\n\n# One stylesheet for the public site and the admin console (served at /style.css).\nCSS = Path(__file__).with_name(\"style.css\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    return Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n\n\ndef nav_items(prefix: str = \"\") -> list[dict[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Published Pages, as relative (title, href) links for the public\n    site's nav. `prefix` relocates the link for a page nested one\n    directory deep (e.g. \"../\" from site/posts/*.html) — a draft Page\n    never appears here.\"\"\"\n    return [{\"title\": page[\"title\"], \"href\": f\"{prefix}{page['slug']}.html\"}\n            for page in _exportable_pages()]\n\n\ndef _exportable_pages() -> list:\n    # The editor already refuses reserved slugs; this also covers rows saved\n    # before that check existed, so a Page can never overwrite site/index.html.\n    return [page for page in content_module.list_published(\"page\")\n            if not content_module.reserved_slug_reason(\"page\", page[\"slug\"])]\n\n\ndef _date(item) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The calendar day an item was created, e.g. \"2026-10-07\".\"\"\"\n    return item[\"created_at\"][:10]\n\n\ndef home_html() -> str:\n    \"\"\"The home page (feed of published Posts), as written to site/index.html.\"\"\"\n    posts = content_module.list_published(\"post\")\n    return environment().get_template(\"public/home.html\").render(\n        title=settings.SITE_TITLE, items=[\n            {\"title\": post[\"title\"], \"href\": f\"posts/{post['slug']}.html\",\n             \"date\": _date(post)} for post in posts\n        ],\n        css_path=\"style.css\", home_path=\"index.html\", nav_items=nav_items(),\n    )\n\n\ndef post_html(post) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A published Post, as written to site/posts/<slug>.html — one directory\n    deep, so every shared link climbs a level.\"\"\"\n    return _detail_html(\"public/post.html\", \"post\", post, prefix=\"../\")\n\n\ndef page_html(page) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A published Page, as written to site/<slug>.html.\"\"\"\n    return _detail_html(\"public/page.html\", \"page\", page, prefix=\"\")\n\n\ndef _detail_html(template_name: str, item_key: str, item, *, prefix: str) -> str:\n    return environment().get_template(template_name).render(\n        title=item[\"title\"], site_title=settings.SITE_TITLE,\n        **{item_key: item}, date=_date(item),\n        body_html=render_markdown(item[\"body_md\"], to_root=prefix),\n        css_path=f\"{prefix}style.css\", home_path=f\"{prefix}index.html\",\n        nav_items=nav_items(prefix=prefix),\n    )\n\n\ndef _write(path: Path, text: str) -> None:\n    # Explicit UTF-8: the pages declare <meta charset=\"utf-8\">, and the\n    # platform default (cp1252 on Windows) can't encode an emoji at all.\n    path.write_text(text, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    _write(out / \"style.css\", CSS)\n    _write(out / \"index.html\", home_html())\n\n    posts_dir = out / \"posts\"\n    posts_dir.mkdir()\n    for post in content_module.list_published(\"post\"):\n        _write(posts_dir / f\"{post['slug']}.html\", post_html(post))\n    for page in _exportable_pages():\n        _write(out / f\"{page['slug']}.html\", page_html(page))\n\n    return out\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":106,"oldLines":4,"newStart":106,"newLines":9,"lines":["     for page in _exportable_pages():","         _write(out / f\"{page['slug']}.html\", page_html(page))"," ","+    # Every file in media/ is meant to be public; Posts show them through","+    # their Media library snippets.","+    if settings.MEDIA.is_dir():","+        shutil.copytree(settings.MEDIA, out / \"media\")","+","     return out"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"5904c16c-0714-486b-9148-6f2ac7177cd0","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"46a8d74b-d860-4909-a43f-d4dbcfcc3476","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms","sessionId":"39a0ae77-23dc-47a0-8ea7-552f47020b4e","version":"2.1.305","gitBranch":"main"}

As you build content types, extend\nrender_site() to write one file per published item. Two rules the rubric checks:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n     That includes links written in a body: render_markdown(..., to_root=...)\n     rewrites \"/contact-us.html\" for the file it lands in.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import content as content_module\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.mdrender import render_markdown\n\n# One stylesheet for the public site and the admin console (served at /style.css).\nCSS = Path(__file__).with_name(\"style.css\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    return Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n\n\ndef nav_items(prefix: str = \"\") -> list[dict[str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Published Pages, as relative (title, href) links for the public\n    site's nav. `prefix` relocates the link for a page nested one\n    directory deep (e.g. \"../\" from site/posts/*.html) — a draft Page\n    never appears here.\"\"\"\n    return [{\"title\": page[\"title\"], \"href\": f\"{prefix}{page['slug']}.html\"}\n            for page in _exportable_pages()]\n\n\ndef _exportable_pages() -> list:\n    # The editor already refuses reserved slugs; this also covers rows saved\n    # before that check existed, so a Page can never overwrite site/index.html.\n    return [page for page in content_module.list_published(\"page\")\n            if not content_module.reserved_slug_reason(\"page\", page[\"slug\"])]\n\n\ndef _date(item) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The calendar day an item was created, e.g. \"2026-10-07\".\"\"\"\n    return item[\"created_at\"][:10]\n\n\ndef home_html() -> str:\n    \"\"\"The home page (feed of published Posts), as written to site/index.html.\"\"\"\n    posts = content_module.list_published(\"post\")\n    return environment().get_template(\"public/home.html\").render(\n        title=settings.SITE_TITLE, items=[\n            {\"title\": post[\"title\"], \"href\": f\"posts/{post['slug']}.html\",\n             \"date\": _date(post)} for post in posts\n        ],\n        css_path=\"style.css\", home_path=\"index.html\", nav_items=nav_items(),\n    )\n\n\ndef post_html(post) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A published Post, as written to site/posts/<slug>.html — one directory\n    deep, so every shared link climbs a level.\"\"\"\n    return _detail_html(\"public/post.html\", \"post\", post, prefix=\"../\")\n\n\ndef page_html(page) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A published Page, as written to site/<slug>.html.\"\"\"\n    return _detail_html(\"public/page.html\", \"page\", page, prefix=\"\")\n\n\ndef _detail_html(template_name: str, item_key: str, item, *, prefix: str) -> str:\n    return environment().get_template(template_name).render(\n        title=item[\"title\"], site_title=settings.SITE_TITLE,\n        **{item_key: item}, date=_date(item),\n        body_html=render_markdown(item[\"body_md\"], to_root=prefix),\n        css_path=f\"{prefix}style.css\", home_path=f\"{prefix}index.html\",\n        nav_items=nav_items(prefix=prefix),\n    )\n\n\ndef _write(path: Path, text: str) -> None:\n    # Explicit UTF-8: the pages declare <meta charset=\"utf-8\">, and the\n    # platform default (cp1252 on Windows) can't encode an emoji at all.\n    path.write_text(text, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    _write(out / \"style.css\", CSS)\n    _write(out / \"index.html\", home_html())\n\n    posts_dir = out / \"posts\"\n    posts_dir.mkdir()\n    for post in content_module.list_published(\"post\"):\n        _write(posts_dir / f\"{post['slug']}.html\", post_html(post))\n    for page in _exportable_pages():\n        _write(out / f\"{page['slug']}.html\", page_html(page))\n\n    # Every file in media/ is meant to be public; Posts show them through\n    # their Media library snippets.\n    if settings.MEDIA.is_dir():\n        shutil.copytree(settings.MEDIA, out / \"media\")\n\n    return out\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":7,"oldLines":7,"newStart":7,"newLines":7,"lines":["   2. Only a\n    `media/` URL is rewritten, by `media_root`: the \"../\" steps from the admin\n    page the preview is shown on back to the server root, which serves media/.\n    \"\"\"\n    html = _md.render(raw)\n    if to_root is not None:\n        return nh3.clean(html, attribute_filter=_link_rewriter(to_root, root_links=True))\n    if media_root is not None:\n        return nh3.clean(html, attribute_filter=_link_rewriter(media_root, root_links=False))\n    return nh3.clean(html)\n\n\ndef _link_rewriter(to_root: str, *, root_links: bool) -> Callable[[str, str, str], str]:\n    \"\"\"An nh3 attribute filter that makes every href/src starting `media/`\n    relative to the page, and, with `root_links`, every one a browser would\n    read as root-absolute or protocol-relative too.\n\n    nh3 checks URL schemes before it calls the filter, never after, so a\n    rewritten value must never be able to start a scheme: it always begins\n    with \"./\", \"../\" or \"https://\". Dropping only the \"/\" would turn\n    \"/javascript:alert(1)\" into a live javascript: link.\n    \"\"\"\n    prefix = to_root or \"./\"\n\n    def rewrite(tag: str, attribute: str, value: str) -> str:\n        if attribute not in (\"href\", \"src\"):\n            return value\n        url = value.strip(_TRIMMED).translate(_DROPPED).replace(\"\\\\\", \"/\")\n        if url.startswith(\"media/\"):\n            return prefix + url  # a Media library snippet names it from the site root\n        if not root_links:\n            return value\n        if The content model is intentionally generic — built with no specific client in mind. A specific client site has been built *using* this CMS. The site was created for the Upper Arlington High School's Computer Science Honor Society chapter (UAHS CSHS), specifically for Dr. Diane Kahle (faculty advisor). The chapter needs a website to promote computer science among UAHS students.","-","-## Roles","-","-**Admin**:","-A CMS user role with full permissions: everything an Editor can do, plus publishing/unpublishing content and managing user accounts (create, change role, deactivate). When this CMS is introduced to the client for the UAHS CSHS chapter, Dr. Kahle will be given admin permissions.","-_Avoid_: superadmin, owner","-","-**Editor**:","-A CMS user role that can create, edit, and delete any Post or Page — including another user's drafts — but cannot publish/unpublish content or manage user accounts. Student officers will be given Editor permissions.","-_Avoid_: contributor, author (an Author is a content attribute, not a role)","-","-## Content","-","-**Post**:","-A dated, feed-like content item with a title, slug, Markdown body, draft/published status, author, and timestamps. Appears in the site's chronological feed.","-_Avoid_: article, entry","-","-**Page**:","-A static, evergreen content item — same fields and operations as a Post, plus appearing in the public site's navigation once published. The UAHS-CSHS website includes The Latest Posts, Coursework, Contact Us, About Us (mission + why join + eligibility + requirements + questions).","-_Avoid_: static page (redundant)","-","-**Slug**:","-The URL-safe identifier for a Post or Page, unique within its kind, used to build its published path. ","-","-**Status (Draft / Published)**:","-The two states a Post or Page can be in. A Draft is visible only in the admin console; only a Published item reaches the static export.","-_Avoid_: live/unlive, active/inactive","-","-**Author**:","-The user (Admin or Editor) recorded as having written a given Post or Page. Distinct from whoever most recently edited it.","-","-## Publishing","-","-**Publish** (verb):","-The admin-only action that flips a content item's status from Draft to Published, making it eligible to appear in the next static export.","-_Avoid_: approve (there's no separate approval workflow — publish is a single, direct action)","-","-**Static export**:","-The `site/` directory `cms publish` generates from currently-published content only; what `cms deploy` pushes to GitHub Pages. Every link in it is relative. A link written in a body from the site root (`/contact-us.html`) is rewritten relative to the file it lands in (`./contact-us.html`, or `../contact-us.html` from a Post), since GitHub Pages serves the site from a subfolder. The admin preview keeps it as written.","-","-**Revision**:","-One saved version of a Post or Page: its title, slug, and body, who saved it, and when, numbered 1, 2, 3… within that item. Every create, edit, and Roll back records one; Publish and unpublish do not, since they change Status, not content.","-_Avoid_: snapshot, history entry","-","-**Revision history**:","-The list of an item's Revisions, newest first, on its edit screen. The newest is the Current one.","-","-**Roll back** (verb):","-Returning an item's title, slug, and body to those of an earlier Revision. Editors and Admins can do it; it is itself recorded as a new Revision, so a Roll back can be undone the same way. Status is unchanged: a Published item's restored text reaches the site on the next static export.","-_Avoid_: restore, revert, undo","-","-**Scheduled publishing**:","-An Admin setting a future time, in UTC, after which a Draft becomes Published. The public site is static, so nothing happens at that moment: the item becomes Published on the next `cms publish` after its time, which switches it before writing the static export. Setting or cancelling a schedule records no Revision, since it changes Status, not content.","-_Avoid_: auto-publish, publishing \"automatically\"","-","-**Scheduled**:","-A Draft with a publish time set. The site was created for the Upper Arlington High School's Computer Science Honor Society chapter (UAHS CSHS), specifically for Dr. Diane Kahle (faculty advisor). png(width, height, pixel):\n    def chunk(kind, data):\n        return struct.pack(\">I\", len(data)) + kind + data + struct.pack(\">I\", zlib.crc32(kind + data))\n    rows = b\"\".join(b\"\\x00\" + b\"\".join(bytes(pixel(x, y)) for x in range(width)) for y in range(height))\n    return (b\"\\x89PNG\\r\\n\\x1a\\n\" + chunk(b\"IHDR\", struct.pack(\">IIBBBBB\", width, height, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0))\n            + chunk(b\"IDAT\", zlib.compress(rows, 9)) + chunk(b\"IEND\", b\"\"))\n\n\ndef logo(x, y, w=480, h=320):\n    \"\"\"An indigo-to-teal gradient with a white star in the middle.\"\"\"\n    t = x / w\n    base = (int(79 + (20 - 79) * t), int(70 + (160 - 70) * t), int(229 + (150 - 229) * t))\n    dx, dy = x - w / 2, y - h / 2\n    r, a = math.hypot(dx, dy), math.atan2(dy, dx)\n    star = 70 + 45 * math.cos(5 * a)\n    return (255, 255, 255) if r < star else base\n\n\nLOGO = png(480, 320, logo)\nTINY = png(4, 4, lambda x, y: (200, 30, 30))\nHTML = b\"<!doctype html><script>alert(document.cookie)</script>\"\nALT = \"Computer Science Honor Society star logo\"\n\nsock = socket.socket()\nsock.bind((\"127.0.0.1\", 0))\nport = sock.getsockname()[1]\nserver = uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(create_app(), log_level=\"warning\"))\nthreading.Thread(target=server.run, kwargs={\"sockets\": [sock]}, daemon=True).start()\nwhile not server.started:\n    time.sleep(0.05)\nBASE = f\"http://127.0.0.1:{port}\"\n\nSCREENSHOTS = REPO / \"docs\" / \"screenshots\"\n\n\ndef log_in(page, email, password):\n    page.goto(BASE + \"/login\")\n    page.fill(\"input[name=email]\", email)\n    page.fill(\"input[name=password]\", password)\n    page.click(\"button[type=submit]\")\n    page.wait_for_url(\"**/admin\")\n\n\ndef submit(page, name, data, alt):\n    page.goto(BASE + \"/admin/media\")\n    if data is not None:\n        page.set_input_files(\"input[name=image]\", files=[{\"name\": name, \"mimeType\": \"application/octet-stream\", \"buffer\": data}])\n    page.fill(\"input[name=alt_text]\", alt)\n    page.click(\"form.media-upload button[type=submit]\")\n    page.wait_for_load_state()\n\n\ndef image_loaded(page, selector):\n    page.wait_for_timeout(300)\n    return page.evaluate(\"(s) => [...document.querySelectorAll(s)].every(i => i.complete && i.naturalWidth > 0) && document.querySelectorAll(s).length > 0\",      check(label, error.count() == 1 and words in error.inner_text(), desk.content()[:200])\n    check(\"2/3 nothing stored after refusals\", not settings.MEDIA.exists() or not git-ignored\", ignored)\n    # Step 5\n    snippet = desk.input_value(\"input.media-item__snippet\")\n    check(\"5 snippet\", snippet == f\"![{ALT}](media/uahs-cshs-logo.png)\", snippet)\n    html = desk.content()\n    check(\"no root-absolute href/src on the library\", 'href=\"/' not in html and 'src=\"/' not in html)\n    if SHOTS:\n        desk.screenshot(path=str(SCREENSHOTS / desk.fill(\"#body_md\", f\"The chapter has a new logo:\\n\\n{snippet}\\n\")\n    desk.wait_for_selector(\"#preview img\", timeout=5000)\n    check(\"7 live preview image loads\", image_loaded(desk, desk.wait_for_selector(\"#preview img\")\n    check(\"7 edit-screen preview image loads\", image_loaded(desk, \"#preview img\"))\n\n    # Admin publishes, then cms publish\n    admin = admin.locator(\"li\", has_text=\"Our new logo\").locator(\"button\", has_text=\"Publish\").click()\n    admin.wait_for_url(\"**saved=published\")\n    check(\"cms publish exits 0\", time.sleep(1.0)\n        visitor = browser.new_context(viewport={\"width\": 390, \"height\": 844}).new_page()\n        for page_path in sorted(p.relative_to(site).as_posix() for p in {"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"39a0ae77-23dc-47a0-8ea7-552f47020b4e","hash":"532d539b3abb3cb92d3fea052fce39beef86dbc38724c354d41177ff0de31077","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"toolu_014UoBhZSFTZEJkdJ4w9mSnr","content":"Launching skill: mattpocock-skills:code-review"},{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: C:\\Users\\rajan\\.claude\\plugins\\cache\\claude-plugins-official\\mattpocock-skills\\1.3.1\\skills\\engineering\\code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\r\n\r\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\r\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\r\n\r\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\r\n\r\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\r\n\r\n## Process\r\n\r\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\r\n\r\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\r\n\r\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\r\n\r\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\r\n\r\n### 2. Identify the spec source\r\n\r\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\r\n\r\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in the tracker doc.\r\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\r\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\r\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\r\n\r\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\r\n\r\nSearch the repo for every file that documents how code should be written. When `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md` exists, it must be on the list.\r\n\r\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\r\n\r\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\r\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\r\n\r\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\r\n\r\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\r\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\r\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\r\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\r\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\r\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\r\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\r\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\r\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\r\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\r\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\r\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\r\n\r\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\r\n\r\nIssue both sub-agent calls together, in the foreground, and aggregate the reports they return.\r\n\r\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\r\n\r\n- The full diff command and commit list.\r\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\r\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\r\n\r\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\r\n\r\n- The diff command and commit list.\r\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\r\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\r\n\r\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\r\n\r\n### 5. Aggregate\r\n\r\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\r\n\r\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\r\n\r\n## Why two axes\r\n\r\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\r\n\r\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\r\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\r\n\r\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\r\n\n\nARGUMENTS: Review the uncommitted working-tree changes for issue #21 (MP2plus F1: Media uploads with alt text) against HEAD 8ddb990. {"parentUuid":"c989d9f2-e1d4-4058-9523-96c6355fd927","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"dd968fe8-910e-4bf4-aec4-5598d8f95603","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: C:\\Users\\rajan\\.claude\\plugins\\cache\\claude-plugins-official\\mattpocock-skills\\1.3.1\\skills\\engineering\\code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\r\n\r\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\r\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\r\n\r\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\r\n\r\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\r\n\r\n## Process\r\n\r\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\r\n\r\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\r\n\r\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\r\n\r\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\r\n\r\n### 2. Identify the spec source\r\n\r\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\r\n\r\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in the tracker doc.\r\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\r\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\r\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\r\n\r\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\r\n\r\nSearch the repo for every file that documents how code should be written. When `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md` exists, it must be on the list.\r\n\r\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\r\n\r\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\r\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\r\n\r\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\r\n\r\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\r\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\r\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\r\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\r\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\r\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\r\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\r\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\r\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\r\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\r\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\r\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\r\n\r\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\r\n\r\nIssue both sub-agent calls together, in the foreground, and aggregate the reports they return.\r\n\r\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\r\n\r\n- The full diff command and commit list.\r\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\r\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\r\n\r\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\r\n\r\n- The diff command and commit list.\r\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\r\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\r\n\r\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\r\n\r\n### 5. Aggregate\r\n\r\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\r\n\r\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\r\n\r\n## Why two axes\r\n\r\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\r\n\r\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\r\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\r\n\r\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\r\n\n\nARGUMENTS: Review the uncommitted working-tree changes for issue #21 (MP2plus F1: Media uploads with alt text) against HEAD 8ddb990. Ignore notes/mp2plus-plan.md, notes/usage-ledger.csv and docs/transcripts/* (the user's own uncommitted files)."}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"b03aa598-f561-421f-8bb9-374698789c3a","timestamp":"2026-10-21T02:42:56.944Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_014UoBhZSFTZEJkdJ4w9mSnr","session_id":"46a8d74b-d860-4909-a43f-d4dbcfcc3476","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms","sessionId":"39a0ae77-23dc-47a0-8ea7-552f47020b4e","version":"2.1.305","gitBranch":"main"}

The report follows:\n  **Standards axis: #21 (F1 media uploads), against 8ddb990**\n  \n  **Hard violations: none found.** Each rule checked:\n  - **Relative paths:** no `href=\"/`, `src=\"/` or `action=\"/` in any template (grep of templates/ found none).\n  - **Redirect:** `RedirectResponse(\"/admin/media?saved=uploaded\")` at app/routes/media.py:60 is root-absolute, but it is a Location header, not a template. users.py does the same.\n  - **CSRF:** the upload form carries a token, and a POST without one or with a forged one gets a 403. `Form(\"\")` instead of `Form(...)` is explained in a comment. The preview POST keeps its documented \"no side effect\" exemption.\n  - **.env.example:** `settings.MEDIA` is a path constant like `SITE`, not read from the environment, so it needs no line.\n  - **Dependencies:** none added. pyproject.toml is unchanged, and the tests build their PNG with stdlib struct/zlib.\n  - **Seed:** I ran scripts/seed_demo.py with the .env.example values against a scratch database. It exits 0 and creates the `media` table.\n  - **Pre-existing tests:** no test files outside tests/test_media.py are touched. Every new test is named `test_stepN_...`.\n  \n  **Documented-standard tension (judgement call)**\n  - app/publish.py:111-112 `shutil.copytree(settings.MEDIA, out / \"media\")` copies every file in media/. That includes images used only by Drafts, and any non-image file. This works against CLAUDE.md \"Only published content reaches site/\" and SECURITY-CHECKLIST #8. CONTEXT.md does document \"copies all of media/\". The filter also differs from `served_file`, which serves only .png/.jpg/.jpeg.\n  \n  **Smells (all judgement calls)**\n  - **Mysterious Name / shadowing:** at content_crud.py:288 the form parameter `to_root` shadows the `to_root` function imported at line 19. `to_root` now names a function, a template variable, a `render_markdown` argument and a form field.\n  - **Primitive Obsession / flag argument:** `render_markdown(raw, *, to_root=None, media_root=None)` takes two strings of the same kind that can't both apply, and `to_root` silently wins. It then calls `_link_rewriter(media_root, root_links=False)`, so that parameter is named `to_root` even when it holds `media_root`.\n  - **Feature Envy (misplaced):** `TO_ROOT_RE` (content_crud.py:23) checks the shape of what `templating.to_root()` returns. It belongs next to that function.\n  - **Duplicated Code:** `CSRF_EXPIRED_MESSAGE` (routes/media.py:19) is a copy of users.py:20, and content_crud.py has the same literal three times. This follows the existing idiom, so it is low priority.\n  - **Test layout:** test_media.py:114 `test_step1_an_upload_without_a_file...` sits under the \"Step 2\" heading. The `media_dir` isolation lives in test_media.py, not in conftest's autouse fixture, so older publish tests copy the developer's real media/ into their output.\n  \n  **Bugs found in passing**\n  1. app/media.py:28 `MARKDOWN_SYNTAX` doesn't include `&`. HTML entities in Alt text are silently dropped: I checked that `R &amp; D` becomes `alt=\"R  D\"` and `caf&#233;` becomes `alt=\"caf\"`. This breaks the module's promise that the published alt text matches what was typed. A bare `&` is fine.\n  2. app/media.py:80-112 has a race between checking a file name and writing the file. Two uploads with the same name at once can both pick `team.png`. The second overwrites the first file, its INSERT fails on UNIQUE, and `path.unlink()` deletes the file the first row points to, then the user gets a 500. This is unlikely on a local console. The fix is `open(path, \"xb\")`.\n  3. routes/media.py:63-64: `/media/{file}` requires login, but the dev server's public Post pages don't. An anonymous visitor there sees a broken image, although public.py says the local site and the deployed one can't drift.\n  4. media_library.html copy script: `.catch(execCommand).then(\"Copied\")` shows \"Copied\" even when the fallback copy fails.\n  \n  No XSS or path traversal found. Alt text is autoescaped, `<` is refused, and markdown-it escapes `\"`. The preview's `to_root` must fully match `(?:\\.\\./)*`. Upload names are cleaned by `_safe_stem`, and `served_file` checks the resolved parent folder.\n</agent-message>"}

The preview POST keeps its documented \"no side effect\" exemption.\n  - **.env.example:** `settings.MEDIA` is a path constant like `SITE`, not read from the environment, so it needs no line.\n  - **Dependencies:** none added. pyproject.toml is unchanged, and the tests build their PNG with stdlib struct/zlib.\n  - **Seed:** I ran scripts/seed_demo.py with the .env.example values against a scratch database. It exits 0 and creates the `media` table.\n  - **Pre-existing tests:** no test files outside tests/test_media.py are touched. Every new test is named `test_stepN_...`.\n  \n  **Documented-standard tension (judgement call)**\n  - app/publish.py:111-112 `shutil.copytree(settings.MEDIA, out / \"media\")` copies every file in media/. That includes images used only by Drafts, and any non-image file. This works against CLAUDE.md \"Only published content reaches site/\" and SECURITY-CHECKLIST #8. CONTEXT.md does document \"copies all of media/\". The filter also differs from `served_file`, which serves only .png/.jpg/.jpeg.\n  \n  **Smells (all judgement calls)**\n  - **Mysterious Name / shadowing:** at content_crud.py:288 the form parameter `to_root` shadows the `to_root` function imported at line 19. `to_root` now names a function, a template variable, a `render_markdown` argument and a form field.\n  - **Primitive Obsession / flag argument:** `render_markdown(raw, *, to_root=None, media_root=None)` takes two strings of the same kind that can't both apply, and `to_root` silently wins. It then calls `_link_rewriter(media_root, root_links=False)`, so that parameter is named `to_root` even when it holds `media_root`.\n  - **Feature Envy (misplaced):** `TO_ROOT_RE` (content_crud.py:23) checks the shape of what `templating.to_root()` returns. It belongs next to that function.\n  - **Duplicated Code:** `CSRF_EXPIRED_MESSAGE` (routes/media.py:19) is a copy of users.py:20, and content_crud.py has the same literal three times. This follows the existing idiom, so it is low priority.\n  - **Test layout:** test_media.py:114 `test_step1_an_upload_without_a_file...` sits under the \"Step 2\" heading. The `media_dir` isolation lives in test_media.py, not in conftest's autouse fixture, so older publish tests copy the developer's real media/ into their output.\n  \n  **Bugs found in passing**\n  1. app/media.py:28 `MARKDOWN_SYNTAX` doesn't include `&`. HTML entities in Alt text are silently dropped: I checked that `R &amp; D` becomes `alt=\"R  D\"` and `caf&#233;` becomes `alt=\"caf\"`. This breaks the module's promise that the published alt text matches what was typed. A bare `&` is fine.\n  2. app/media.py:80-112 has a race between checking a file name and writing the file. Two uploads with the same name at once can both pick `team.png`. The second overwrites the first file, its INSERT fails on UNIQUE, and `path.unlink()` deletes the file the first row points to, then the user gets a 500. This is unlikely on a local console. Alt text is autoescaped, `<` is refused, and markdown-it escapes `\"`. The preview's `to_root` must fully match `(?:\\.\\./)*`. Raises UploadRefused\n    otherwise. `data` may be cut short at MAX_BYTES + 1 bytes.\"\"\"\n    if not filename:\n        raise UploadRefused(\"Choose an image to upload.\")\n    extension = PurePosixPath(filename).suffix.lower()\n    if extension not in SIGNATURES:\n        raise UploadRefused(\"Only PNG and JPEG images can be uploaded (.png, .jpg or .jpeg).\")\n    if len(data) > MAX_BYTES:\n        raise UploadRefused(\"That image is over 2 MB. Returns the name it was saved as; raises\n    UploadRefused, storing nothing, if the upload breaks a rule.\"\"\"\n    extension = check_image(filename, data)\n    alt_text = clean_alt_text(alt_text)\n    settings.MEDIA.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        name = _free_name(conn, filename, extension)\n        path = settings.MEDIA / name\n        path.write_bytes(data)\n        try:\n            conn.execute(\n                \"INSERT INTO media (filename, alt_text, uploaded_by) VALUES (?, ?, ?)\",\n                (name, alt_text, uploaded_by),\n            )\n            conn.commit()\n        except sqlite3.Error:\n            path.unlink()\n            raise\n        return name\n    finally:\n        conn.close()","new_string":"def _create_file(conn: sqlite3.Connection, filename: str, extension: str, data: bytes) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Write `data` to a new file in media/ named after the upload: \"team.png\",\n    then \"team-2.png\", \"team-3.png\", ... It never replaces a file already\n    there, even one another upload creates at the same moment, nor takes a\n    name the library already uses.\"\"\"\n    stem = _safe_stem(filename)\n    taken = {row[\"filename\"] for row in conn.execute(\"SELECT filename FROM media\")}\n    for number in itertools.count(1):\n        path = settings.MEDIA / (f\"{stem}{extension}\" if number == 1\n                                 else f\"{stem}-{number}{extension}\")\n        if path.name in taken:\n            continue\n        try:\n            with open(path, \"xb\") as file:\n                file.write(data)\n        except FileExistsError:\n            continue\n        return path\n\n\ndef save_upload(filename: str, data: bytes, alt_text: str, uploaded_by: int) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Write the image to media/ under a safe, unused name and record its\n    Alt text in the library. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"44393eef-1f77-4b39-a99a-d0dd067478b4","timestamp":"2026-10-21T02:48:47.895Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms\\app\\media.py","oldString":"def _free_name(conn: sqlite3.Connection, filename: str, extension: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A file name for the upload that neither media/ nor the library uses\n    yet: \"team.png\", then \"team-2.png\", \"team-3.png\", ...\"\"\"\n    stem = _safe_stem(filename)\n    taken = {row[\"filename\"] for row in conn.execute(\"SELECT filename FROM media\")}\n    number = 1\n    while True:\n        name = f\"{stem}{extension}\" if number == 1 else f\"{stem}-{number}{extension}\"\n        if name not in taken and not (settings.MEDIA / name).exists():\n            return name\n        number += 1\n\n\ndef save_upload(filename: str, data: bytes, alt_text: str, uploaded_by: int) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Write the image to media/ under a safe, unused name and record its\n    Alt text in the library. Returns the name it was saved as; raises\n    UploadRefused, storing nothing, if the upload breaks a rule.\"\"\"\n    extension = check_image(filename, data)\n    alt_text = clean_alt_text(alt_text)\n    settings.MEDIA.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        name = _free_name(conn, filename, extension)\n        path = settings.MEDIA / name\n        path.write_bytes(data)\n        try:\n            conn.execute(\n                \"INSERT INTO media (filename, alt_text, uploaded_by) VALUES (?, ?, ?)\",\n                (name, alt_text, uploaded_by),\n            )\n            conn.commit()\n        except sqlite3.Error:\n            path.unlink()\n            raise\n        return name\n    finally:\n        conn.close()","newString":"def _create_file(conn: sqlite3.Connection, filename: str, extension: str, data: bytes) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Write `data` to a new file in media/ named after the upload: \"team.png\",\n    then \"team-2.png\", \"team-3.png\", ... It never replaces a file already\n    there, even one another upload creates at the same moment, nor takes a\n    name the library already uses.\"\"\"\n    stem = _safe_stem(filename)\n    taken = {row[\"filename\"] for row in conn.execute(\"SELECT filename FROM media\")}\n    for number in itertools.count(1):\n        path = settings.MEDIA / (f\"{stem}{extension}\" if number == 1\n                                 else f\"{stem}-{number}{extension}\")\n        if path.name in taken:\n            continue\n        try:\n            with open(path, \"xb\") as file:\n                file.write(data)\n        except FileExistsError:\n            continue\n        return path\n\n\ndef save_upload(filename: str, data: bytes, alt_text: str, uploaded_by: int) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Write the image to media/ under a safe, unused name and record its\n    Alt text in the library. Returns the name it was saved as; raises\n    UploadRefused, storing nothing, if the upload breaks a rule.\"\"\"\n    extension = check_image(filename, data)\n    alt_text = clean_alt_text(alt_text)\n    settings.MEDIA.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        path = _create_file(conn, filename, extension, data)\n        try:\n            conn.execute(\n                \"INSERT INTO media (filename, alt_text, uploaded_by) VALUES (?, ?, ?)\",\n                (path.name, alt_text, uploaded_by),\n            )\n            conn.commit()\n        except sqlite3.Error:\n            path.unlink()  # this upload's own file: _create_file never reuses one\n            raise\n        return path.name\n    finally:\n        conn.close()","originalFile":"\"\"\"The Media library: images uploaded for use in Posts, each with Alt text\n(see CONTEXT.md). The file goes in media/, which is git-ignored like the\ndatabase; its row in the `media` table keeps the Alt text. No ORM (see spec\nImplementation Decisions).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport itertools\nimport re\nimport sqlite3\nfrom html import unescape\nfrom pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath\n\nfrom app import db as db_module\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.mdrender import render_markdown\n\nMAX_BYTES = 2 * 1024 * 1024  # 2 MB\n\n# The extensions accepted, each with the type's name and the first bytes\n# every file of that type starts with, so a renamed .html file is caught.\nSIGNATURES = {\n    \".png\": (\"PNG\", b\"\\x89PNG\\r\\n\\x1a\\n\"),\n    \".jpg\": (\"JPEG\", b\"\\xff\\xd8\\xff\"),\n    \".jpeg\": (\"JPEG\", b\"\\xff\\xd8\\xff\"),\n}\n\n\n\nclass UploadRefused(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"An upload that breaks one of the library's rules; the message says\n    which, in words for the upload form.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef clean_alt_text(raw: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"`raw` on one line, with runs of spaces collapsed. Raises\n    UploadRefused if nothing is left, or if a Post would show different\n    alt text once the item's snippet is pasted in.\"\"\"\n    alt = \" \".join(raw.split())\n    if not alt:\n        raise UploadRefused(\"Add alt text: a short description of the image for \"\n                            \"someone who can't see it.\")\n    if _published_alt(alt) != alt:\n        raise UploadRefused(\"Markdown would change this alt text in a post: it reads some \"\n                            \"uses of * _ ` [ ] < & as formatting. Reword it without them.\")\n    return alt\n\n\ndef _published_alt(alt: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"The alt text a Post shows for a snippet carrying `alt`, rendered by\n    the Posts' own Markdown pipeline (None if it makes no image at all).\n    Markdown reads * _ ` [ ] < & as syntax there, and markdown-it drops even\n    backslash-escaped characters from an image's alt, so escaping can't help.\"\"\"\n    html = render_markdown(snippet({\"alt_text\": alt, \"filename\": \"image.png\"}))\n    match = re.search(r'<img [^>]*alt=\"([^\"]*)\"', html)\n    return unescape(match.group(1)) if match else None\n\n\ndef snippet(item) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The Markdown that places a library item in a Post.\"\"\"\n    return f\"![{item['alt_text']}](media/{item['filename']})\"\n\n\ndef check_image(filename: str, data: bytes) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The lowercase extension of an acceptable image: a PNG or JPEG by both\n    its name and its first bytes, MAX_BYTES or smaller. Raises UploadRefused\n    otherwise. `data` may be cut short at MAX_BYTES + 1 bytes.\"\"\"\n    if not filename:\n        raise UploadRefused(\"Choose an image to upload.\")\n    extension = PurePosixPath(filename).suffix.lower()\n    if extension not in SIGNATURES:\n        raise UploadRefused(\"Only PNG and JPEG images can be uploaded (.png, .jpg or .jpeg).\")\n    if len(data) > MAX_BYTES:\n        raise UploadRefused(\"That image is over 2 MB. Make it smaller and upload it again.\")\n    kind, signature = SIGNATURES[extension]\n    if not data.startswith(signature):\n        raise UploadRefused(f\"That file isn't a real {kind} image, whatever its name says.\")\n    return extension\n\n\ndef _safe_stem(filename: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The upload's own name, without folders or extension, as lowercase\n    letters, digits and hyphens: \"C:\\\\pics\\\\Team Photo (1).PNG\" -> \"team-photo-1\".\"\"\"\n    stem = PurePosixPath(filename.replace(\"\\\\\", \"/\")).stem\n    return re.sub(r\"[^a-z0-9]+\", \"-\", stem.lower()).strip(\"-\")[:60].strip(\"-\") or \"image\"\n\n\ndef _free_name(conn: sqlite3.Connection, filename: str, extension: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A file name for the upload that neither media/ nor the library uses\n    yet: \"team.png\", then \"team-2.png\", \"team-3.png\", ...\"\"\"\n    stem = _safe_stem(filename)\n    taken = {row[\"filename\"] for row in conn.execute(\"SELECT filename FROM media\")}\n    number = 1\n    while True:\n        name = f\"{stem}{extension}\" if number == 1 else f\"{stem}-{number}{extension}\"\n        if name not in taken and not (settings.MEDIA / name).exists():\n            return name\n        number += 1\n\n\ndef save_upload(filename: str, data: bytes, alt_text: str, uploaded_by: int) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Write the image to media/ under a safe, unused name and record its\n    Alt text in the library. Returns the name it was saved as; raises\n    UploadRefused, storing nothing, if the upload breaks a rule.\"\"\"\n    extension = check_image(filename, data)\n    alt_text = clean_alt_text(alt_text)\n    settings.MEDIA.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        name = _free_name(conn, filename, extension)\n        path = settings.MEDIA / name\n        path.write_bytes(data)\n        try:\n            conn.execute(\n                \"INSERT INTO media (filename, alt_text, uploaded_by) VALUES (?, ?, ?)\",\n                (name, alt_text, uploaded_by),\n            )\n            conn.commit()\n        except sqlite3.Error:\n            path.unlink()\n            raise\n        return name\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef list_media() -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n    \"\"\"Every image in the library, newest first, with who uploaded it.\"\"\"\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT media.*, users.email AS uploaded_by_email FROM media \"\n            \"JOIN users ON users.id = media.uploaded_by ORDER BY media.id DESC\"\n        ).fetchall()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef served_file(filename: str) -> Path | None:\n    \"\"\"media/<filename>, if that is an image file directly inside media/;\n    else None, so a crafted name (\"..\\\\cms.db\", \"x.html\") is never served.\"\"\"\n    if PurePosixPath(filename).suffix.lower() not in SIGNATURES:\n        return None\n    path = settings.MEDIA / filename\n    try:\n        inside = path.resolve().parent == settings.MEDIA.resolve()\n    except OSError:\n        return None\n    return path if inside and path.is_file() else None\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":85,"oldLines":17,"newStart":85,"newLines":24,"lines":["     return re.sub(r\"[^a-z0-9]+\", \"-\", stem.lower()).strip(\"-\")[:60].strip(\"-\") or \"image\""," (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"a914497a-2a73-4fed-86be-ea1597f063ba","timestamp":"2026-10-21T02:48:48.088Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms\\templates\\admin\\media_library.html","oldString":"        copied.catch(function () { document.execCommand(\"copy\"); })\n              .then(function () { button.textContent = \"Copied\"; });","newString":"        copied.then(function () { return true; },\n                    function () { return document.execCommand(\"copy\"); })\n              .then(function (ok) { button.textContent = ok ? \"Copied\" : \"Press Ctrl+C\"; });","originalFile":"{% extends \"admin/base.html\" %}\n{% block admin_content %}\n  <div class=\"page-head\">\n    <h1>Media</h1>\n  </div>\n  {% if saved == \"uploaded\" %}<p class=\"success\">Image uploaded. Copy its Markdown into a post.</p>{% endif %}\n  {% if error %}<p class=\"error\">{{ error }}</p>{% endif %}\n  <form method=\"post\" action=\"{{ to_root }}admin/media/upload\" enctype=\"multipart/form-data\"\n        class=\"content-form card media-upload\">\n    <input type=\"hidden\" name=\"csrf_token\" value=\"{{ csrf_token }}\">\n    <label>Image (PNG or JPEG, 2 MB or less)\n      <input type=\"file\" name=\"image\" accept=\".png,.jpg,.jpeg,image/png,image/jpeg\" required>\n    </label>\n    <label>Alt text\n      <input type=\"text\" name=\"alt_text\" value=\"{{ form_alt }}\" aria-describedby=\"alt-hint\">\n    </label>\n    <p id=\"alt-hint\" class=\"media-upload__hint\">Describe the image for someone who can't see it,\n      e.g. \"Club members at the hackathon\". A screen reader reads this aloud.</p>\n    <div class=\"form-actions\">\n      <button type=\"submit\">Upload</button>\n    </div>\n  </form>\n  {% if items %}\n    <ul class=\"content-list media-list\">\n      {% for item in items %}\n        <li class=\"content-list__item media-item\">\n          <img class=\"media-item__image\" src=\"{{ to_root }}media/{{ item['filename'] }}\" alt=\"{{ item['alt_text'] }}\">\n          <div class=\"content-list__main\">\n            <span class=\"content-list__title\">{{ item[\"alt_text\"] }}</span>\n            <span class=\"content-list__meta\">{{ item[\"filename\"] }} · {{ item[\"uploaded_by_email\"] }} · {{ item[\"uploaded_at\"] | utc_time }}</span>\n            <div class=\"media-item__copy\">\n              <input type=\"text\" class=\"media-item__snippet\" readonly value=\"{{ item['snippet'] }}\"\n                     aria-label=\"Markdown for a post: {{ item['alt_text'] }}\">\n              <button type=\"button\" class=\"button--secondary button--small\" data-copy>Copy</button>\n            </div>\n          </div>\n        </li>\n      {% endfor %}\n    </ul>\n  {% else %}\n    <p class=\"empty\">No images yet. Upload the first one above.</p>\n  {% endif %}\n  <script>\n    // Copy a snippet with one click. Focusing the field selects it, too,\n    // for Ctrl+C where the clipboard API isn't allowed.\n    document.querySelectorAll(\"button[data-copy]\").forEach(function (button) {\n      var field = button.previousElementSibling;\n      field.addEventListener(\"focus\", function () { field.select(); });\n      button.addEventListener(\"click\", function () {\n        field.select();\n        var copied = navigator.clipboard ? navigator.clipboard.writeText(field.value)\n                                         : Promise.reject(new Error(\"no clipboard API\"));\n        copied.catch(function () { document.execCommand(\"copy\"); })\n              .then(function () { button.textContent = \"Copied\"; });\n      });\n    });\n  </script>\n{% endblock %}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":50,"oldLines":8,"newStart":50,"newLines":9,"lines":["         field.select();","         var copied = navigator.clipboard ? navigator.clipboard.writeText(field.value)","                                          : Promise.reject(new Error(\"no clipboard API\"));","-        copied.catch(function () { document.execCommand(\"copy\"); })","-              .then(function () { button.textContent = \"Copied\"; });","+        copied.then(function () { return true; },","+                    function () { return document.execCommand(\"copy\"); })","+              .then(function (ok) { button.textContent = ok ? \"Copied\" : \"Press Ctrl+C\"; });","       });","     });","   </script>"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"296808de-7afd-418a-a592-d57906aa3d79","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"46a8d74b-d860-4909-a43f-d4dbcfcc3476","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms","sessionId":"39a0ae77-23dc-47a0-8ea7-552f47020b4e","version":"2.1.305","gitBranch":"main"}

Returns the name it was saved as; raises\n    UploadRefused, storing nothing, if the upload breaks a rule.\"\"\"\n    extension = check_image(filename, data)\n    alt_text = clean_alt_text(alt_text)\n    settings.MEDIA.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        name = _free_name(conn, filename, extension)\n        path = settings.MEDIA / name\n        path.write_bytes(data)\n        try:\n            conn.execute(\n                \"INSERT INTO media (filename, alt_text, uploaded_by) VALUES (?, ?, ?)\",\n                (name, alt_text, uploaded_by),\n            )\n            conn.commit()\n        except sqlite3.Error:\n            path.unlink()\n            raise\n        return name\n    finally:\n        conn.close()","new_string":"def _create_file(conn: sqlite3.Connection, filename: str, extension: str, data: bytes) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Write `data` to a new file in media/ named after the upload: \"team.png\",\n    then \"team-2.png\", \"team-3.png\", ...
