{"parentUuid":"38030a1a-484f-4b79-94ff-74cfcb130f66","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"3c2b9835-84cd-467c-bed3-6549c960ce4f","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_015Hu7hEu8NvZMVJXoTW1M7S","type":"tool_result","content":"The file C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms\\app\\media.py has been updated successfully."}]},"uuid":"d389b20f-b148-47e2-85ac-7dff055aa4bd","timestamp":"2026-10-21T02:49:01.215Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms\\app\\media.py","oldString":"}\n\n\n\nclass UploadRefused(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"An upload that breaks one of the library's rules; the message says\n    which, in words for the upload form.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef clean_alt_text(raw: str) -> str:","newString":"}\n\n\nclass UploadRefused(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"An upload that breaks one of the library's rules; the message says\n    which, in words for the upload form.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef snippet(item) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The Markdown that places a library item in a Post.\"\"\"\n    return f\"![{item['alt_text']}](media/{item['filename']})\"\n\n\ndef clean_alt_text(raw: str) -> str:","originalFile":"\"\"\"The Media library: images uploaded for use in Posts, each with Alt text\n(see CONTEXT.md). The file goes in media/, which is git-ignored like the\ndatabase; its row in the `media` table keeps the Alt text. No ORM (see spec\nImplementation Decisions).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport itertools\nimport re\nimport sqlite3\nfrom html import unescape\nfrom pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath\n\nfrom app import db as db_module\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.mdrender import render_markdown\n\nMAX_BYTES = 2 * 1024 * 1024  # 2 MB\n\n# The extensions accepted, each with the type's name and the first bytes\n# every file of that type starts with, so a renamed .html file is caught.\nSIGNATURES = {\n    \".png\": (\"PNG\", b\"\\x89PNG\\r\\n\\x1a\\n\"),\n    \".jpg\": (\"JPEG\", b\"\\xff\\xd8\\xff\"),\n    \".jpeg\": (\"JPEG\", b\"\\xff\\xd8\\xff\"),\n}\n\n\n\nclass UploadRefused(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"An upload that breaks one of the library's rules; the message says\n    which, in words for the upload form.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef clean_alt_text(raw: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"`raw` on one line, with runs of spaces collapsed. Raises\n    UploadRefused if nothing is left, or if a Post would show different\n    alt text once the item's snippet is pasted in.\"\"\"\n    alt = \" \".join(raw.split())\n    if not alt:\n        raise UploadRefused(\"Add alt text: a short description of the image for \"\n                            \"someone who can't see it.\")\n    if _published_alt(alt) != alt:\n        raise UploadRefused(\"Markdown would change this alt text in a post: it reads some \"\n                            \"uses of * _ ` [ ] < & as formatting. Reword it without them.\")\n    return alt\n\n\ndef _published_alt(alt: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"The alt text a Post shows for a snippet carrying `alt`, rendered by\n    the Posts' own Markdown pipeline (None if it makes no image at all).\n    Markdown reads * _ ` [ ] < & as syntax there, and markdown-it drops even\n    backslash-escaped characters from an image's alt, so escaping can't help.\"\"\"\n    html = render_markdown(snippet({\"alt_text\": alt, \"filename\": \"image.png\"}))\n    match = re.search(r'<img [^>]*alt=\"([^\"]*)\"', html)\n    return unescape(match.group(1)) if match else None\n\n\ndef snippet(item) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The Markdown that places a library item in a Post.\"\"\"\n    return f\"![{item['alt_text']}](media/{item['filename']})\"\n\n\ndef check_image(filename: str, data: bytes) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The lowercase extension of an acceptable image: a PNG or JPEG by both\n    its name and its first bytes, MAX_BYTES or smaller. Raises UploadRefused\n    otherwise. `data` may be cut short at MAX_BYTES + 1 bytes.\"\"\"\n    if not filename:\n        raise UploadRefused(\"Choose an image to upload.\")\n    extension = PurePosixPath(filename).suffix.lower()\n    if extension not in SIGNATURES:\n        raise UploadRefused(\"Only PNG and JPEG images can be uploaded (.png, .jpg or .jpeg).\")\n    if len(data) > MAX_BYTES:\n        raise UploadRefused(\"That image is over 2 MB. Make it smaller and upload it again.\")\n    kind, signature = SIGNATURES[extension]\n    if not data.startswith(signature):\n        raise UploadRefused(f\"That file isn't a real {kind} image, whatever its name says.\")\n    return extension\n\n\ndef _safe_stem(filename: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The upload's own name, without folders or extension, as lowercase\n    letters, digits and hyphens: \"C:\\\\pics\\\\Team Photo (1).PNG\" -> \"team-photo-1\".\"\"\"\n    stem = PurePosixPath(filename.replace(\"\\\\\", \"/\")).stem\n    return re.sub(r\"[^a-z0-9]+\", \"-\", stem.lower()).strip(\"-\")[:60].strip(\"-\") or \"image\"\n\n\ndef _create_file(conn: sqlite3.Connection, filename: str, extension: str, data: bytes) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Write `data` to a new file in media/ named after the upload: \"team.png\",\n    then \"team-2.png\", \"team-3.png\", ... It never replaces a file already\n    there, even one another upload creates at the same moment, nor takes a\n    name the library already uses.\"\"\"\n    stem = _safe_stem(filename)\n    taken = {row[\"filename\"] for row in conn.execute(\"SELECT filename FROM media\")}\n    for number in itertools.count(1):\n        path = settings.MEDIA / (f\"{stem}{extension}\" if number == 1\n                                 else f\"{stem}-{number}{extension}\")\n        if path.name in taken:\n            continue\n        try:\n            with open(path, \"xb\") as file:\n                file.write(data)\n        except FileExistsError:\n            continue\n        return path\n\n\ndef save_upload(filename: str, data: bytes, alt_text: str, uploaded_by: int) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Write the image to media/ under a safe, unused name and record its\n    Alt text in the library. Returns the name it was saved as; raises\n    UploadRefused, storing nothing, if the upload breaks a rule.\"\"\"\n    extension = check_image(filename, data)\n    alt_text = clean_alt_text(alt_text)\n    settings.MEDIA.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        path = _create_file(conn, filename, extension, data)\n        try:\n            conn.execute(\n                \"INSERT INTO media (filename, alt_text, uploaded_by) VALUES (?, ?, ?)\",\n                (path.name, alt_text, uploaded_by),\n            )\n            conn.commit()\n        except sqlite3.Error:\n            path.unlink()  # this upload's own file: _create_file never reuses one\n            raise\n        return path.name\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef list_media() -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n    \"\"\"Every image in the library, newest first, with who uploaded it.\"\"\"\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT media.*, users.email AS uploaded_by_email FROM media \"\n            \"JOIN users ON users.id = media.uploaded_by ORDER BY media.id DESC\"\n        ).fetchall()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef served_file(filename: str) -> Path | None:\n    \"\"\"media/<filename>, if that is an image file directly inside media/;\n    else None, so a crafted name (\"..\\\\cms.db\", \"x.html\") is never served.\"\"\"\n    if PurePosixPath(filename).suffix.lower() not in SIGNATURES:\n        return None\n    path = settings.MEDIA / filename\n    try:\n        inside = path.resolve().parent == settings.MEDIA.resolve()\n    except OSError:\n        return None\n    return path if inside and path.is_file() else None\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":26,"oldLines":12,"newStart":26,"newLines":16,"lines":[" }"," "," ","-"," class UploadRefused(ValueError):","     \"\"\"An upload that breaks one of the library's rules; {"parentUuid":"8c7e9f8e-fc1b-42a0-aaea-94377b554edc","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"3c2b9835-84cd-467c-bed3-6549c960ce4f","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01YN6XBECa1QQMnia2LTAUMJ","type":"tool_result","content":"The file C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms\\tests\\conftest.py has been updated successfully."}]},"uuid":"ba59d0e4-f404-49ac-8b22-e2482bdc7a74","timestamp":"2026-10-21T02:49:23.346Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms\\tests\\conftest.py","oldString":"    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, \"DATABASE_PATH\", db_path)\n","newString":"    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, \"DATABASE_PATH\", db_path)\n    # Uploads too: never the real media/, which `cms publish` would also copy.\n    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, \"MEDIA\", tmp_path / \"media\")\n","originalFile":"\"\"\"Shared test fixtures.\n\n`client` gives you the app. `client_as(role)` gives you a client that is logged\nin as a seeded user of that role — it works as soon as your login route exists,\nso access-control tests stay one line:\n\n    def test_editor_cannot_manage_users(client_as):\n        assert client_as(\"editor\").get(\"/admin/users\").status_code in (302, 403)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport socket\nimport threading\nimport time\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.main import create_app\nfrom app.seed import seed_users\n\n\ndef extract_csrf(html: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Pull the csrf_token hidden-field value out of a rendered admin page.\"\"\"\n    match = re.search(r'name=\"csrf_token\" value=\"([^\"]*)\"', html)\n    assert match, \"expected a csrf_token hidden field in the rendered page\"\n    return match.group(1)\n\n# Matches scripts/seed_demo.py. Passwords come from the environment there; in\n# tests they are fixed and meaningless.\nDEMO_USERS = {\n    \"admin\": {\"email\": \"admin@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-admin-pw\"},\n    \"editor\": {\"email\": \"editor@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-editor-pw\"},\n}\n\n\n@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)\ndef _isolated_seeded_db(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"Every test gets its own temp SQLite file, pre-seeded with the two\n    demo users above, so tests never touch the real dev database and never\n    see state left over from another test.\"\"\"\n    db_path = tmp_path / \"test.db\"\n    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, \"DATABASE_PATH\", db_path)\n    # settings also reads the developer's own .env; pin the one value tests\n    # render, so a title like \"Jo's CMS\" can't change test outcomes.\n    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, \"SITE_TITLE\", \"Test CMS\")\n    seed_users(db_path, DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"password\"], DEMO_USERS[\"editor\"][\"password\"])\n    yield db_path\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client() -> TestClient:\n    return TestClient(create_app())\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client_as():\n    \"\"\"Return a factory: client_as(\"editor\") -> a logged-in TestClient.\"\"\"\n\n    def _login(role: str) -> TestClient:\n        user = DEMO_USERS[role]\n        c = TestClient(create_app())\n        login_page = c.get(\"/login\")\n        if login_page.status_code == 404:\n            pytest.skip(\"No /login route yet — build the login ticket first.\")\n        csrf_token = extract_csrf(login_page.text)\n        response = c.post(\"/login\", data={\"email\": user[\"email\"],\n                                          \"password\": user[\"password\"],\n                                          \"csrf_token\": csrf_token},\n                          follow_redirects=False)\n        assert response.status_code in (200, 302, 303), (\n            f\"Login as {role} failed with {response.status_code}\")\n        return c\n\n    return _login\n\n\n# --- Browser tests -----------------------------------------------------------\n# Layout (does a page fit a 390px phone?) and in-page JavaScript can only be\n# checked in a real browser. These fixtures run the app on a local port and\n# drive it with Playwright; when Chromium isn't installed\n# (`uv run playwright install chromium`), every browser test is skipped.\n\nPHONE_VIEWPORT = {\"width\": 390, \"height\": 844}\n\n\n@pytest.fixture(scope=\"session\")\ndef live_server():\n    \"\"\"The app on a free localhost port. Tests still get their own database:\n    the app reads settings.DATABASE_PATH per request, and the autouse fixture\n    above repoints it for every test.\"\"\"\n    import uvicorn\n\n    sock = socket.socket()\n    sock.bind((\"127.0.0.1\", 0))\n    port = sock.getsockname()[1]\n    server = uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(create_app(), log_level=\"warning\"))\n    thread = threading.Thread(target=server.run, kwargs={\"sockets\": [sock]}, daemon=True)\n    thread.start()\n    deadline = time.monotonic() + 10\n    while not server.started:\n        assert time.monotonic() < deadline, \"test server did not start\"\n        time.sleep(0.05)\n    yield f\"http://127.0.0.1:{port}\"\n    server.should_exit = True\n    thread.join(timeout=5)\n    sock.close()\n\n\n@pytest.fixture(scope=\"session\")\ndef browser():\n    sync_api = pytest.importorskip(\"playwright.sync_api\")\n    with sync_api.sync_playwright() as playwright:\n        try:\n            chromium = playwright.chromium.launch()\n        except Exception as exc:  # browser binaries not installed\n            pytest.skip(f\"Chromium unavailable ({exc.__class__.__name__}); \"\n                        \"run `uv run playwright install chromium`\")\n        yield chromium\n        chromium.close()\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef phone(browser, live_server):\n    \"\"\"A fresh 390px-wide browser tab (no cookies) aimed at the test server.\"\"\"\n    context = browser.new_context(viewport=PHONE_VIEWPORT, base_url=live_server)\n    yield context.new_page()\n    context.close()\n\n\ndef log_in(page, role: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Log in through the real login form, as a person would.\"\"\"\n    user = DEMO_USERS[role]\n    page.goto(\"/login\")\n    page.fill(\"input[name=email]\", user[\"email\"])\n    page.fill(\"input[name=password]\", user[\"password\"])\n    page.click(\"button[type=submit]\")\n    page.wait_for_url(\"**/admin\")\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":43,"oldLines":6,"newStart":43,"newLines":8,"lines":["     see state left over from another test.\"\"\"","     db_path = tmp_path / \"test.db\"","     monkeypatch.setattr(settings, \"DATABASE_PATH\", db_path)","+    # Uploads too: never the real media/, which `cms publish` would also copy.","+    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, \"MEDIA\", tmp_path / \"media\")","     # settings also reads the developer's own .env; {"parentUuid":"9273a21c-2eaf-42c8-849b-281289bb1ab3","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"3c2b9835-84cd-467c-bed3-6549c960ce4f","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01GhznSdAQx8uXxefRYjFLHs","type":"tool_result","content":"T17: Relative links in exported Markdown bodies\n\nThe live site had two broken links: about.html and\nposts/hour-of-code.html linked href=\"/contact-us.html\", which GitHub\nPages resolves outside the /iphs400-mp2-cms/ subfolder (a 404). The\nrelative-paths rule held for the templates but not for links written in\na body. The export test only used bodies without links, and the checker\ngreps main, not gh-pages.\n\nrender_markdown(..., to_root=...) now rewrites every href/src a browser\nwould read as root-absolute or protocol-relative, inside the existing\nnh3 pass:\n- \"/x\" becomes \"./x\" from a Page and \"../x\" from a Post.\n- \"/\" becomes the home page.\n- \"//host\" becomes \"https://host\".\nThe URL is read the way a browser reads it first: trimmed, tabs dropped,\n\"\\\" read as \"/\". The admin preview is unchanged.\n\nThe review caught an XSS in the first version. nh3 checks schemes\nbefore attribute_filter runs, so dropping the \"/\" from\n\"/javascript:alert(1)\" on a Page left a live javascript: link. The\nprefix is now never empty, so a rewritten link can't start a scheme.\n\nCloses #20\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n\n## /code-review findings — T17\n\nTwo independent reviewers read the diff fresh, in parallel. The **Standards** axis checked the CLAUDE.md rules, the CONTEXT.md vocabulary, SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md and the Fowler smell baseline. The **Spec** axis mapped each acceptance criterion to the code and the tests, and traced every path a body takes to HTML:\n- `_detail_html` is the only export path that renders a body.\n- The dev server's public pages go through the same `post_html`/`page_html`.\n- Both admin previews call `render_markdown` without `to_root`.\n\n**Both axes independently found one critical bug.** The first version created an XSS hole.\n\n### Fixed\n\n| # | Axis | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Both | **Hard (XSS):** nh3 checks URL schemes *before* it calls `attribute_filter`, never after. On a Page `to_root` is `\"\"`, so the rewrite only dropped the `/`, and `[x](/javascript:alert(1))` exported as `href=\"javascript:alert(1)\"`. The same happened with `/data:…`, a mixed-case scheme, a tab after the `/`, and an `img src`. Posts were safe only because their output starts with `../`. | The prefix is never empty: root-level files get `./`. Every rewritten link starts with `./`, `../` or `https://`, so it can't start a scheme. `test_a_root_link_on_a_page_never_becomes_a_script_link` covers five payloads: Markdown, mixed case, `data:`, tab, and a leading space. |\n| 2 | Both | Raw-HTML links a browser reads differently weren't rewritten. ` /x.html` (padded) and `/\\tx.html` stayed root-absolute to a browser and hid from the `href=\"/` grep. `/\\host` became `\\host`, which a browser reads as `/host`. | The value is read the way a browser reads it before the checks: spaces and control characters trimmed, tabs and newlines dropped, `\\` read as `/`. `/\\host` is protocol-relative to a browser, so it exports as `https://host`. Covered by `test_links_are_read_the_way_a_browser_reads_them`, and the sweep now includes padded and backslash links and asserts that no `href`/`src` starts with whitespace. |\n| 3 | Standards | **Hard:** \"an author writes a link\" used *author* for whoever types the link. CONTEXT.md defines **Author** as the recorded writer of an item, distinct from whoever last edited it. | \"A link written in a body\" in CONTEXT.md, both docstrings and the test module. |\n| 4 | Standards | A bare \"Pages\" sat next to the glossary term **Page**. | \"GitHub Pages\" throughout. |\n| 5 | Standards | `_relative_links` sounded like a list of links. It had no return type or docstring, unlike its neighbours. | Renamed `_root_link_rewriter`, typed `-> Callable[[str, str, str], str]`. Its docstring states the never-start-a-scheme rule and why it matters. |\n| 6 | Spec | Test gaps: no exact-value Page image test; the edit screen's server-rendered preview wasn't checked; `/#…` and `/?…` were untested. | Page image → `./logo.png`. The edit screen keeps `/contact-us.html`. Parametrized cases for `/`, `/#join` and `/?ref=nav` from both a Page and a Post. |\n| 7 | Spec | The `app/mdrender.py` module docstring still said the preview and the export can't render differently. | It now names the one deliberate difference: links to the site root. |\n| 8 | Spec | \"No `href=\"/` … whatever the bodies contain\" can't hold for *text*. nh3 writes `&quot;` back out as `\"`, so prose or a code span that quotes `href=\"/x\"` still matches a plain grep. `attribute_filter` never sees text. | The criterion now covers attributes only: \"No `href` or `src` attribute in the export starts with `/`\". The text case is a known limit: prose that quotes an HTML link could still trip a text grep. The client site has none. |\n\nThe issue's criteria were edited to match: 1, 3, 8 and 10 were revised, and 5 and 6 were added.\n\n### Deliberately not changed (judgement calls)\n\n- **`_admin_id()` is now copied into a fourth test file** (Duplicated Code). This follows `test_export.py`, `test_phone_width.py` and `test_scheduling.py`. Moving it into `conftest.py` means editing three existing test files for a refactor unrelated to this ticket.\n- **Two names for one idea at the call site** (`render_markdown(..., to_root=prefix)`, Mysterious Name). `prefix` is publish.py's existing name, as in `nav_items(prefix=…)`; `to_root` matches the admin templates' `to_root`. The mapping happens in exactly one place.\n- **A second `nh3.clean` pass over the filtered output** (offered as an alternative fix for #1). Not added: the prefix rule makes the filter's output scheme-free by construction, and the regression test pins that.\n- **Small extras beyond the first issue text** (Spec, scope): protocol-relative → `https://`, and `/#…`/`/?…` → `index.html#…`. Both are kept and are now in the criteria.\n\n### Verification\n\n- **Red first:** 6 of the first 12 tests failed on `main`'s code, each showing the root-absolute value it exported. The 6 that passed are guardrails: links left unchanged, and the admin preview.\n- **Security tests proven to fail:** putting the empty prefix and the raw value back failed 13 tests (all 5 script-link cases, all 3 browser-reading cases, the sweep, and the Page and home-link cases). With the fix restored, all 22 pass.\n- **Full suite:** **286 passed** (264 before + 22). `check_submission.py --stage 2`: 22/22.\n- **Dry run on a copy of the real local `cms.db`**, exported to a scratch folder rather than `site/`. The About page now links to `./contact-us.html` and the Hour of Code post to `../contact-us.html`. Nothing in the export has a root-absolute `href`/`src`. CONTEXT.md defines **Author** as the recorded writer of an item, distinct from whoever last edited it. | \"A link written in a body\" in CONTEXT.md, both docstrings and the test module. |\n| 4 | Standards | A bare \"Pages\" sat next to the glossary term **Page**. | \"GitHub Pages\" throughout. |\n| 5 | Standards | `_relative_links` sounded like a list of links. It had no return type or docstring, unlike its neighbours. | Renamed `_root_link_rewriter`, typed `-> Callable[[str, str, str], str]`. Its docstring states the never-start-a-scheme rule and why it matters. |\n| 6 | Spec | Test gaps: no exact-value Page image test; the edit screen's server-rendered preview wasn't checked; `/#…` and `/?…` were untested. | Page image → `./logo.png`. The edit screen keeps `/contact-us.html`. Parametrized cases for `/`, `/#join` and `/?ref=nav` from both a Page and a Post. |\n| 7 | Spec | The `app/mdrender.py` module docstring still said the preview and the export can't render differently. | It now names the one deliberate difference: links to the site root. |\n| 8 | Spec | \"No `href=\"/` … whatever the bodies contain\" can't hold for *text*. nh3 writes `&quot;` back out as `\"`, so prose or a code span that quotes `href=\"/x\"` still matches a plain grep. `attribute_filter` never sees text. | The criterion now covers attributes only: \"No `href` or `src` attribute in the export starts with `/`\". {"type":"file-history-delta","messageId":"702c15ea-bf3d-4127-a993-b32bf68cf01d","snapshotMessageId":"f02ebd17-192a-4b65-a655-25c20e23d391","trackingPath":"C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Rajan-E-disk-My-work-IPHS400-code-mp2-cms\\39a0ae77-23dc-47a0-8ea7-552f47020b4e\\scratchpad\\t21-review-comment.md","backup":{"backupFileName":null,"version":1,"backupTime":"2026-10-21T02:52:45.733Z","realParentDir":"C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Rajan-E-disk-My-work-IPHS400-code-mp2-cms\\39a0ae77-23dc-47a0-8ea7-552f47020b4e\\scratchpad"},"timestamp":"2026-10-21T02:52:45.739Z"}
{"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"39a0ae77-23dc-47a0-8ea7-552f47020b4e","hash":"333adcbaf044ee605bf1dbd957879a40a939adef925373e05d590fb589765fc1","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"thinking","thinking":"","signature":""},{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01K7xoFeg9X7BLBTujZB4DCz","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Rajan-E-disk-My-work-IPHS400-code-mp2-cms\\39a0ae77-23dc-47a0-8ea7-552f47020b4e\\scratchpad\\t21-review-comment.md","content":"## /code-review findings — T21 (MP2plus F1: Media uploads with alt text)\n\nTwo independent reviewers read the diff fresh, in parallel:\n- **Standards:** CLAUDE.md, CONTEXT.md, SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md, the ADRs, this ticket's prompt rules, and the Fowler smell baseline.\n- **Spec:** every acceptance step and the judge's own run, against the code and `tests/test_media.py`.\n\n**Both axes found no hard violation, and the Spec axis found no acceptance step that would fail.** Both flagged the same real bug in the Alt text rule.\n\n### Fixed\n\n| # | Axis | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Both | **The Alt text rule was too broad, and it also missed a case.** The first version refused any alt containing `[ ] \\ * _ ` <`. That refused `team_photo`, `5 * 3` and `Team [photo]`, which render unchanged. It also let `R &amp; D` through, which a post shows as `R  D` because entities are dropped. | The rule is now a round trip. The snippet is rendered through the Posts' own Markdown pipeline (`render_markdown`), and the upload is refused only if the `<img alt>` that comes out differs from what was typed. `test_step5_alt_text_markdown_leaves_alone_reaches_the_post_as_typed` covers 7 alts that are accepted and reach a post as typed. `test_step5_alt_text_that_markdown_would_change_is_refused` covers 7 that are refused, including `R &amp; D`, `a ] b` and `[a](b)`. Escaping can't replace refusing, because markdown-it drops even backslash-escaped characters from an image's alt. The probe output is in the session. |\n| 2 | Standards | **Race in naming:** the name check and the write were separate steps. Two simultaneous uploads of `team.png` could pick the same name. The second would then overwrite the first, fail its INSERT, and `unlink()` the first upload's file. | `_create_file` creates each file with `open(path, \"xb\")` and moves on to `-2`, `-3`, … on `FileExistsError`. A failed INSERT can now only delete the upload's own file. |\n| 3 | Standards | The Copy button said \"Copied\" even when the fallback `execCommand(\"copy\")` failed. | It shows \"Copied\" only when a copy happened, and \"Press Ctrl+C\" otherwise. The field also selects itself on focus. |\n| 4 | Standards | **Shadowing and a misplaced check (smells).** The live-preview form field `to_root` shadowed the `to_root()` helper imported into `content_crud.py`. The regex that checks its shape lived in the router, not next to the function whose output it describes. | Renamed the helper `templating.to_root_from(path)` and moved the check beside it as `templating.is_to_root(value)`. |\n| 5 | Standards | Test layout: `test_step1_an_upload_without_a_file…` sat under the Step 2 heading. Media isolation lived only in `test_media.py`, so older tests that call `render_site()` would copy the developer's real `media/` into their temp output. | The test moved under Step 1. `tests/conftest.py`'s autouse fixture gained **two added lines** (a comment and `monkeypatch.setattr(settings, \"MEDIA\", tmp_path / \"media\")`). No existing line or assertion changed (`git diff --stat`: 2 insertions). |\n\n### Deliberately not changed (judgement calls)\n\n- **`cms publish` copies every file in `media/`, including images used only by Drafts** (Standards, set against \"Only published content reaches site/\"). This was the student's explicit decision: anything put in `media/` is meant to be public. It is documented in the CONTEXT.md **Media library** entry. Draft *text* still never leaves the database.\n- **The dev server's public pages show a broken image to a logged-out visitor**, because `/media/` requires a login (both axes). Also the student's decision: the admin serves `media/` to logged-in users for the library and the editor preview. The judge previews the export with `python3 -m http.server`, where `../media/x.png` loads; the walk confirms it.\n- **A hand-typed `./media/x.png` isn't rewritten** (Spec). `./` says \"relative to this page\", so it stays as written. That is the T17 rule for every explicitly relative link (`test_other_links_are_exported_exactly_as_written`). The snippet's form, `media/x.png`, is always rewritten.\n- **\"2 MB\" is 2 × 1024 × 1024 = 2,097,152 bytes** (Spec, a decimal-vs-binary edge). Kept: it's the usual meaning in code, and `test_step3_an_image_of_exactly_2_mb_is_accepted` pins the boundary.\n- **`render_markdown` takes both `to_root` and `media_root`** (Standards, a flag-like pair of parameters). They describe two different pages: a file in `site/`, or the admin page a preview sits on. No caller passes both, and the docstring says what each one rewrites.\n- **`CSRF_EXPIRED_MESSAGE` is defined again in `routes/media.py`** (Duplicated Code). This follows `routes/users.py`, which defines its own. Merging them means editing earlier routers for a refactor unrelated to this ticket.\n- **Scope extras** (Spec, b): uploads get a slug name with `-2` on a clash (needed so a crafted name can't leave `media/`), and the library shows who uploaded each image and when. Kept.\n\n### Verification\n\n- **Tests:** `tests/test_media.py` has 57 tests, each named `test_step<k>_…` for the step it checks. 4 are Chromium tests: upload on a 390px phone, the empty-alt message on a phone, Copy, and the live preview loading the image.\n- **Guards proven to fail:** I broke each guard on purpose, and each time a test failed:\n  - the `media/` containment check and the image-only filter in `served_file`\n  - filename cleaning\n  - the first-bytes check\n  - the 2 MB boundary\n  - the Alt text round trip\n  - the preview's `to_root` shape check\n  - the copy into `site/media/`\n- **Full suite:** **343 passed** (286 at `mp2plus-base` + 57). No pre-existing test or assertion changed. `check_submission.py --stage 2`: **22/22**. `git grep --untracked` finds no `href=\"/` or `src=\"/` in any template.\n- **Judge-style walk over real HTTP:** 31/31, on a throwaway database and `media/`. It covers:\n  - The three refusals with their messages (empty alt, `.html`, `.html` renamed `.png`), plus the 2 MB limit.\n  - An upload, then the snippet pasted into a Post. The image loads in the live and edit-screen previews.\n  - The Admin publishes, then `cms publish`.\n  - `python -m http.server -d site`: every `<img>` has `alt=` and loads, and every page fits at 390px.\n  - The upload POST replayed without its token gets a 403.\n- **Schema:** one new table, `media`, created by `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`. `scripts/seed_demo.py` runs clean twice from `.env.example` values on a fresh database. An existing `cms.db` gains the table when it is first opened, so no re-seed is needed. No new setting: `settings.MEDIA` is a fixed path, like `SITE`.\n- **Screenshots:** `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-media-1280.png` and `mp2plus-media-390.png`, showing the library with one image. The 390px shot first showed the Copy button wrapping. That was fixed, and the shot retaken.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}]}}

{"parentUuid":"80194467-abe0-4ac1-8ad4-15a7ba5a5d5c","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CgEdCqLVwkFoeB7nzN1C6","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01K7xoFeg9X7BLBTujZB4DCz","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Rajan-E-disk-My-work-IPHS400-code-mp2-cms\\39a0ae77-23dc-47a0-8ea7-552f47020b4e\\scratchpad\\t21-review-comment.md","content":"## /code-review findings — T21 (MP2plus F1: Media uploads with alt text)\n\nTwo independent reviewers read the diff fresh, in parallel:\n- **Standards:** CLAUDE.md, CONTEXT.md, SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md, the ADRs, this ticket's prompt rules, and the Fowler smell baseline.\n- **Spec:** every acceptance step and the judge's own run, against the code and `tests/test_media.py`.\n\n**Both axes found no hard violation, and the Spec axis found no acceptance step that would fail.** Both flagged the same real bug in the Alt text rule.\n\n### Fixed\n\n| # | Axis | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Both | **The Alt text rule was too broad, and it also missed a case.** The first version refused any alt containing `[ ] \\ * _ ` <`. That refused `team_photo`, `5 * 3` and `Team [photo]`, which render unchanged. It also let `R &amp; D` through, which a post shows as `R  D` because entities are dropped. | The rule is now a round trip. The snippet is rendered through the Posts' own Markdown pipeline (`render_markdown`), and the upload is refused only if the `<img alt>` that comes out differs from what was typed. `test_step5_alt_text_markdown_leaves_alone_reaches_the_post_as_typed` covers 7 alts that are accepted and reach a post as typed. `test_step5_alt_text_that_markdown_would_change_is_refused` covers 7 that are refused, including `R &amp; D`, `a ] b` and `[a](b)`. Escaping can't replace refusing, because markdown-it drops even backslash-escaped characters from an image's alt. The probe output is in the session. |\n| 2 | Standards | **Race in naming:** the name check and the write were separate steps. Two simultaneous uploads of `team.png` could pick the same name. The second would then overwrite the first, fail its INSERT, and `unlink()` the first upload's file. | `_create_file` creates each file with `open(path, \"xb\")` and moves on to `-2`, `-3`, … on `FileExistsError`. A failed INSERT can now only delete the upload's own file. |\n| 3 | Standards | The Copy button said \"Copied\" even when the fallback `execCommand(\"copy\")` failed. | It shows \"Copied\" only when a copy happened, and \"Press Ctrl+C\" otherwise. The field also selects itself on focus. |\n| 4 | Standards | **Shadowing and a misplaced check (smells).** The live-preview form field `to_root` shadowed the `to_root()` helper imported into `content_crud.py`. The regex that checks its shape lived in the router, not next to the function whose output it describes. | Renamed the helper `templating.to_root_from(path)` and moved the check beside it as `templating.is_to_root(value)`. |\n| 5 | Standards | Test layout: `test_step1_an_upload_without_a_file…` sat under the Step 2 heading. Media isolation lived only in `test_media.py`, so older tests that call `render_site()` would copy the developer's real `media/` into their temp output. | The test moved under Step 1. `tests/conftest.py`'s autouse fixture gained **two added lines** (a comment and `monkeypatch.setattr(settings, \"MEDIA\", tmp_path / \"media\")`). No existing line or assertion changed (`git diff --stat`: 2 insertions). |\n\n### Deliberately not changed (judgement calls)\n\n- **`cms publish` copies every file in `media/`, including images used only by Drafts** (Standards, set against \"Only published content reaches site/\"). This was the student's explicit decision: anything put in `media/` is meant to be public. It is documented in the CONTEXT.md **Media library** entry. Draft *text* still never leaves the database.\n- **The dev server's public pages show a broken image to a logged-out visitor**, because `/media/` requires a login (both axes). Also the student's decision: the admin serves `media/` to logged-in users for the library and the editor preview. The judge previews the export with `python3 -m http.server`, where `../media/x.png` loads; the walk confirms it.\n- **A hand-typed `./media/x.png` isn't rewritten** (Spec). `./` says \"relative to this page\", so it stays as written. That is the T17 rule for every explicitly relative link (`test_other_links_are_exported_exactly_as_written`). The snippet's form, `media/x.png`, is always rewritten.\n- **\"2 MB\" is 2 × 1024 × 1024 = 2,097,152 bytes** (Spec, a decimal-vs-binary edge). Kept: it's the usual meaning in code, and `test_step3_an_image_of_exactly_2_mb_is_accepted` pins the boundary.\n- **`render_markdown` takes both `to_root` and `media_root`** (Standards, a flag-like pair of parameters). They describe two different pages: a file in `site/`, or the admin page a preview sits on. No caller passes both, and the docstring says what each one rewrites.\n- **`CSRF_EXPIRED_MESSAGE` is defined again in `routes/media.py`** (Duplicated Code). This follows `routes/users.py`, which defines its own. Merging them means editing earlier routers for a refactor unrelated to this ticket.\n- **Scope extras** (Spec, b): uploads get a slug name with `-2` on a clash (needed so a crafted name can't leave `media/`), and the library shows who uploaded each image and when. Kept.\n\n### Verification\n\n- **Tests:** `tests/test_media.py` has 57 tests, each named `test_step<k>_…` for the step it checks. 4 are Chromium tests: upload on a 390px phone, the empty-alt message on a phone, Copy, and the live preview loading the image.\n- **Guards proven to fail:** I broke each guard on purpose, and each time a test failed:\n  - the `media/` containment check and the image-only filter in `served_file`\n  - filename cleaning\n  - the first-bytes check\n  - the 2 MB boundary\n  - the Alt text round trip\n  - the preview's `to_root` shape check\n  - the copy into `site/media/`\n- **Full suite:** **343 passed** (286 at `mp2plus-base` + 57). No pre-existing test or assertion changed. `check_submission.py --stage 2`: **22/22**. `git grep --untracked` finds no `href=\"/` or `src=\"/` in any template.\n- **Judge-style walk over real HTTP:** 31/31, on a throwaway database and `media/`. It covers:\n  - The three refusals with their messages (empty alt, `.html`, `.html` renamed `.png`), plus the 2 MB limit.\n  - An upload, then the snippet pasted into a Post. The image loads in the live and edit-screen previews.\n  - The Admin publishes, then `cms publish`.\n  - `python -m http.server -d site`: every `<img>` has `alt=` and loads, and every page fits at 390px.\n  - The upload POST replayed without its token gets a 403.\n- **Schema:** one new table, `media`, created by `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`. `scripts/seed_demo.py` runs clean twice from `.env.example` values on a fresh database. An existing `cms.db` gains the table when it is first opened, so no re-seed is needed. No new setting: `settings.MEDIA` is a fixed path, like `SITE`.\n- **Screenshots:** `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-media-1280.png` and `mp2plus-media-390.png`, showing the library with one image. The 390px shot first showed the Copy button wrapping. That was fixed, and the shot retaken.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3564,"cache_read_input_tokens":292387,"output_tokens":2806,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":22},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3564,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2806,"cache_read_input_tokens":292387,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3564,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3564},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01K7xoFeg9X7BLBTujZB4DCz":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Rajan-E-disk-My-work-IPHS400-code-mp2-cms\\39a0ae77-23dc-47a0-8ea7-552f47020b4e\\scratchpad\\t21-review-comment.md","content":"## /code-review findings — T21 (MP2plus F1: Media uploads with alt text)\n\nTwo independent reviewers read the diff fresh, in parallel:\n- **Standards:** CLAUDE.md, CONTEXT.md, SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md, the ADRs, this ticket's prompt rules, and the Fowler smell baseline.\n- **Spec:** every acceptance step and the judge's own run, against the code and `tests/test_media.py`.\n\n**Both axes found no hard violation, and the Spec axis found no acceptance step that would fail.** Both flagged the same real bug in the Alt text rule.\n\n### Fixed\n\n| # | Axis | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Both | **The Alt text rule was too broad, and it also missed a case.** The first version refused any alt containing `[ ] \\ * _ ` <`. That","originalFile":"## /code-review findings — T21 (MP2plus F1: Media uploads with alt text)\n\nTwo independent reviewers read the diff fresh, in parallel:\n- **Standards:** CLAUDE.md, CONTEXT.md, SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md, the ADRs, this ticket's prompt rules, and the Fowler smell baseline.\n- **Spec:** every acceptance step and the judge's own run, against the code and `tests/test_media.py`.\n\n**Both axes found no hard violation, and the Spec axis found no acceptance step that would fail.** Both flagged the same real bug in the Alt text rule.\n\n### Fixed\n\n| # | Axis | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Both | **The Alt text rule was too broad, and it also missed a case.** The first version refused any alt containing `[ ] \\ * _ ` <`. That refused `team_photo`, `5 * 3` and `Team [photo]`, which render unchanged. It also let `R &amp; D` through, which a post shows as `R  D` because entities are dropped. | The rule is now a round trip. The snippet is rendered through the Posts' own Markdown pipeline (`render_markdown`), and the upload is refused only if the `<img alt>` that comes out differs from what was typed. `test_step5_alt_text_markdown_leaves_alone_reaches_the_post_as_typed` covers 7 alts that are accepted and reach a post as typed. `test_step5_alt_text_that_markdown_would_change_is_refused` covers 7 that are refused, including `R &amp; D`, `a ] b` and `[a](b)`. Escaping can't replace refusing, because markdown-it drops even backslash-escaped characters from an image's alt. The probe output is in the session. |\n| 2 | Standards | **Race in naming:** the name check and the write were separate steps. Two simultaneous uploads of `team.png` could pick the same name. The second would then overwrite the first, fail its INSERT, and `unlink()` the first upload's file. | `_create_file` creates each file with `open(path, \"xb\")` and moves on to `-2`, `-3`, … on `FileExistsError`. A failed INSERT can now only delete the upload's own file. |\n| 3 | Standards | The Copy button said \"Copied\" even when the fallback `execCommand(\"copy\")` failed. | It shows \"Copied\" only when a copy happened, and \"Press Ctrl+C\" otherwise. The field also selects itself on focus. |\n| 4 | Standards | **Shadowing and a misplaced check (smells).** The live-preview form field `to_root` shadowed the `to_root()` helper imported into `content_crud.py`. The regex that checks its shape lived in the router, not next to the function whose output it describes. | Renamed the helper `templating.to_root_from(path)` and moved the check beside it as `templating.is_to_root(value)`. |\n| 5 | Standards | Test layout: `test_step1_an_upload_without_a_file…` sat under the Step 2 heading. Media isolation lived only in `test_media.py`, so older tests that call `render_site()` would copy the developer's real `media/` into their temp output. | The test moved under Step 1. `tests/conftest.py`'s autouse fixture gained **two added lines** (a comment and `monkeypatch.setattr(settings, \"MEDIA\", tmp_path / \"media\")`). No existing line or assertion changed (`git diff --stat`: 2 insertions). |\n\n### Deliberately not changed (judgement calls)\n\n- **`cms publish` copies every file in `media/`, including images used only by Drafts** (Standards, set against \"Only published content reaches site/\"). This was the student's explicit decision: anything put in `media/` is meant to be public. It is documented in the CONTEXT.md **Media library** entry. Draft *text* still never leaves the database.\n- **The dev server's public pages show a broken image to a logged-out visitor**, because `/media/` requires a login (both axes). Also the student's decision: the admin serves `media/` to logged-in users for the library and the editor preview. The judge previews the export with `python3 -m http.server`, where `../media/x.png` loads; the walk confirms it.\n- **A hand-typed `./media/x.png` isn't rewritten** (Spec). `./` says \"relative to this page\", so it stays as written. That is the T17 rule for every explicitly relative link (`test_other_links_are_exported_exactly_as_written`). The snippet's form, `media/x.png`, is always rewritten.\n- **\"2 MB\" is 2 × 1024 × 1024 = 2,097,152 bytes** (Spec, a decimal-vs-binary edge). Kept: it's the usual meaning in code, and `test_step3_an_image_of_exactly_2_mb_is_accepted` pins the boundary.\n- **`render_markdown` takes both `to_root` and `media_root`** (Standards, a flag-like pair of parameters). They describe two different pages: a file in `site/`, or the admin page a preview sits on. No caller passes both, and the docstring says what each one rewrites.\n- **`CSRF_EXPIRED_MESSAGE` is defined again in `routes/media.py`** (Duplicated Code). This follows `routes/users.py`, which defines its own. Merging them means editing earlier routers for a refactor unrelated to this ticket.\n- **Scope extras** (Spec, b): uploads get a slug name with `-2` on a clash (needed so a crafted name can't leave `media/`), and the library shows who uploaded each image and when. Kept.\n\n### Verification\n\n- **Tests:** `tests/test_media.py` has 57 tests, each named `test_step<k>_…` for the step it checks. 4 are Chromium tests: upload on a 390px phone, the empty-alt message on a phone, Copy, and the live preview loading the image.\n- **Guards proven to fail:** I broke each guard on purpose, and each time a test failed:\n  - the `media/` containment check and the image-only filter in `served_file`\n  - filename cleaning\n  - the first-bytes check\n  - the 2 MB boundary\n  - the Alt text round trip\n  - the preview's `to_root` shape check\n  - the copy into `site/media/`\n- **Full suite:** **343 passed** (286 at `mp2plus-base` + 57). The probe output is in the session. |","newString":" Escaping can't replace refusing, because markdown-it drops even backslash-escaped characters from an image's alt (`a \\* b` renders as `a  b`). |","originalFile":"## /code-review findings — T21 (MP2plus F1: Media uploads with alt text)\n\nTwo independent reviewers read the diff fresh, in parallel:\n- **Standards:** CLAUDE.md, CONTEXT.md, SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md, the ADRs, this ticket's prompt rules, and the Fowler smell baseline.\n- **Spec:** every acceptance step and the judge's own run, against the code and `tests/test_media.py`.\n\n**Both axes found no hard violation, and the Spec axis found no acceptance step that would fail.** Both flagged the same real bug in the Alt text rule.\n\n### Fixed\n\n| # | Axis | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Both | **The Alt text rule was too broad, and it also missed a case.** The first version refused any alt containing `` [ ] \\ * _ ` < ``. That refused `team_photo`, `5 * 3` and `Team [photo]`, which render unchanged. It also let `R &amp; D` through, which a post shows as `R  D` because entities are dropped. | The rule is now a round trip. The snippet is rendered through the Posts' own Markdown pipeline (`render_markdown`), and the upload is refused only if the `<img alt>` that comes out differs from what was typed. `test_step5_alt_text_markdown_leaves_alone_reaches_the_post_as_typed` covers 7 alts that are accepted and reach a post as typed. `test_step5_alt_text_that_markdown_would_change_is_refused` covers 7 that are refused, including `R &amp; D`, `a ] b` and `[a](b)`. Escaping can't replace refusing, because markdown-it drops even backslash-escaped characters from an image's alt. The probe output is in the session. |\n| 2 | Standards | **Race in naming:** the name check and the write were separate steps. Two simultaneous uploads of `team.png` could pick the same name. The second would then overwrite the first, fail its INSERT, and `unlink()` the first upload's file. | `_create_file` creates each file with `open(path, \"xb\")` and moves on to `-2`, `-3`, … on `FileExistsError`. A failed INSERT can now only delete the upload's own file. |\n| 3 | Standards | The Copy button said \"Copied\" even when the fallback `execCommand(\"copy\")` failed. | It shows \"Copied\" only when a copy happened, and \"Press Ctrl+C\" otherwise. The field also selects itself on focus. |\n| 4 | Standards | **Shadowing and a misplaced check (smells).** The live-preview form field `to_root` shadowed the `to_root()` helper imported into `content_crud.py`. The regex that checks its shape lived in the router, not next to the function whose output it describes. | Renamed the helper `templating.to_root_from(path)` and moved the check beside it as `templating.is_to_root(value)`. |\n| 5 | Standards | Test layout: `test_step1_an_upload_without_a_file…` sat under the Step 2 heading. Media isolation lived only in `test_media.py`, so older tests that call `render_site()` would copy the developer's real `media/` into their temp output. | The test moved under Step 1. `tests/conftest.py`'s autouse fixture gained **two added lines** (a comment and `monkeypatch.setattr(settings, \"MEDIA\", tmp_path / \"media\")`). No existing line or assertion changed (`git diff --stat`: 2 insertions). |\n\n### Deliberately not changed (judgement calls)\n\n- **`cms publish` copies every file in `media/`, including images used only by Drafts** (Standards, set against \"Only published content reaches site/\"). This was the student's explicit decision: anything put in `media/` is meant to be public. It is documented in the CONTEXT.md **Media library** entry. Draft *text* still never leaves the database.\n- **The dev server's public pages show a broken image to a logged-out visitor**, because `/media/` requires a login (both axes). Also the student's decision: the admin serves `media/` to logged-in users for the library and the editor preview. The judge previews the export with `python3 -m http.server`, where `../media/x.png` loads; the walk confirms it.\n- **A hand-typed `./media/x.png` isn't rewritten** (Spec). `./` says \"relative to this page\", so it stays as written. That is the T17 rule for every explicitly relative link (`test_other_links_are_exported_exactly_as_written`). The snippet's form, `media/x.png`, is always rewritten.\n- **\"2 MB\" is 2 × 1024 × 1024 = 2,097,152 bytes** (Spec, a decimal-vs-binary edge). Kept: it's the usual meaning in code, and `test_step3_an_image_of_exactly_2_mb_is_accepted` pins the boundary.\n- **`render_markdown` takes both `to_root` and `media_root`** (Standards, a flag-like pair of parameters). They describe two different pages: a file in `site/`, or the admin page a preview sits on. No caller passes both, and the docstring says what each one rewrites.\n- **`CSRF_EXPIRED_MESSAGE` is defined again in `routes/media.py`** (Duplicated Code). This follows `routes/users.py`, which defines its own. Merging them means editing earlier routers for a refactor unrelated to this ticket.\n- **Scope extras** (Spec, b): uploads get a slug name with `-2` on a clash (needed so a crafted name can't leave `media/`), and the library shows who uploaded each image and when. Kept.\n\n### Verification\n\n- **Tests:** `tests/test_media.py` has 57 tests, each named `test_step<k>_…` for the step it checks. 4 are Chromium tests: upload on a 390px phone, the empty-alt message on a phone, Copy, and the live preview loading the image.\n- **Guards proven to fail:** I broke each guard on purpose, and each time a test failed:\n  - the `media/` containment check and the image-only filter in `served_file`\n  - filename cleaning\n  - the first-bytes check\n  - the 2 MB boundary\n  - the Alt text round trip\n  - the preview's `to_root` shape check\n  - the copy into `site/media/`\n- **Full suite:** **343 passed** (286 at `mp2plus-base` + 57). No pre-existing test or assertion changed. `check_submission.py --stage 2`: **22/22**. `git grep --untracked` finds no `href=\"/` or `src=\"/` in any template.\n- **Judge-style walk over real HTTP:** 31/31, on a throwaway database and `media/`. It covers:\n  - The three refusals with their messages (empty alt, `.html`, `.html` renamed `.png`), plus the 2 MB limit.\n  - An upload, then the snippet pasted into a Post. The image loads in the live and edit-screen previews.\n  - The Admin publishes, then `cms publish`.\n  - `python -m http.server -d site`: every `<img>` has `alt=` and loads, and every page fits at 390px.\n  - The upload POST replayed without its token gets a 403.\n- **Schema:** one new table, `media`, created by `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`. `scripts/seed_demo.py` runs clean twice from `.env.example` values on a fresh database. An existing `cms.db` gains the table when it is first opened, so no re-seed is needed. No new setting: `settings.MEDIA` is a fixed path, like `SITE`.\n- **Screenshots:** `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-media-1280.png` and `mp2plus-media-390.png`, showing the library with one image. The 390px shot first showed the Copy button wrapping. The rule\n  is a round trip through render_markdown, because markdown-it drops\n  even backslash-escaped characters from an image's alt.\n- cms publish copies media/ into site/media/. render_markdown makes a\n  media/ URL relative to the file it lands in (../media/x.png from a\n  Post). {"parentUuid":"ee3745a3-464b-4e54-a283-9b83068ae0c3","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CgEdJLow54dNMt7aRnGkm","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"F1 (issue #21) is implemented and committed locally as `c755c3f`. The review findings, and what I did about each, are posted on the issue: https://github.com/Rajan-Thakur/iphs400-mp2-cms/issues/21#issuecomment-6306834982\n\n**Checks**\n- **Tests:** 343 pass (286 from before plus 57 new in `tests/test_media.py`, each named `test_step<k>_…`). Four of them run in Chromium at 390px.\n- **Checker:** `check_submission.py --stage 2` is 22/22. No template has `href=\"/` or `src=\"/`.\n- **Walk:** I clicked through all 7 acceptance steps over real HTTP on a throwaway database and `media/`, and all 31 checks passed. That included `cms publish` and serving `site/` with `http.server`: every `<img>` has `alt=` and loads.\n- **Security guards:** I broke each one on purpose (path containment, first-bytes check, 2 MB limit, the preview's `to_root` check, the copy into `site/media/`) and a test failed every time.\n- **Typechecking** didn't run: the project has no type checker, and adding one would be a new dependency.\n\n**Database:** I added one table, `media`. You asked me to tell you to run `rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py`. You don't need to, and it would delete your client site's content: your existing `cms.db` gets the new table on its own the first time it's opened. The seed script also runs clean from `.env.example`. If you want a fresh demo database anyway, back up `cms.db` first.\n\n**Choices you should know about**\n- **Alt text** is refused when Markdown would change it once the snippet is pasted into a post. For example, `x*y*z` would show as `xyz`, and `R &amp; D` as `R  D`. Ordinary text like `team_photo` or `Team [photo]` is accepted. Escaping can't fix the refused cases, because the Markdown library drops even escaped characters from an image's alt text.\n- **Refused uploads** get the message with status 400. A form posted without its CSRF token gets 403.\n- **2 MB means 2,097,152 bytes**, the usual meaning in code.\n- **On the local server**, `/media/` images only show when logged in, as you decided earlier. The judge's `http.server` preview isn't affected.\n- **Existing tests:** `tests/conftest.py` gained two lines so tests never touch your real `media/`. That's added lines only, with no assertion changed, and I declared it in the comment on #21.\n- **`CONTEXT.md`** now has a Media section with three glossary terms (Media library, Alt text, Snippet). Edit them if you'd rather they were in your own words.\n\n**Still yours to do:** push, add the F1 row to the report, and run the two checks from the manual's runbook before you start F5. Both screenshots (`docs/screenshots/mp2plus-media-1280.png` and `-390.png`) are in the commit. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>I reviewed commit c755c3f (\"T21: Media uploads with alt text\", the one commit ahead of `origin/main`) plus the uncommitted changes, which only touch `notes/`. I did not post, commit or push anything.\n\n**Don't use the T14 numbering.** The review target says to commit with \"T14:\" and \"Closes #14\", but this work is ticket T21 on issue #21. #14 is T13's issue, closed long ago. The existing commit's `T21: … Closes #21` is the correct form, and your memory notes say the findings comment is already on #21.\n\nI confirmed these by running probes against an isolated database and media folder: the invisible-alt-text case (#4), the backslash refusal (#5) and the `.png` filename case (#7). Windows reserved names such as `con.png` and `nul.png` upload and serve fine on this Windows 11 machine, so they aren't listed.\n\n```json\n[\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/publish.py\",\n    \"line\": 112,\n    \"summary\": \"copytree publishes every Editor upload to the public site with no Admin action, and the library has no delete, so a mistaken upload can't be withdrawn through the CMS.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"An Editor (who per CONTEXT.md 'cannot publish') uploads an image that no Post uses, or one only a Draft uses. The next `cms publish` copies it to site/media/&lt;file&gt; and `cms deploy` pushes it to public gh-pages. The only way to pull it back is deleting the file by hand, which leaves a dangling library row and a broken thumbnail.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/publish.py\",\n    \"line\": 112,\n    \"summary\": \"The export copies media/ with no filter, while the admin's served_file serves only image files directly inside media/. Non-images, subfolders and symlink targets all reach site/.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"copytree's default symlinks=False copies a link's target. A `media/x.png -&gt; ../.env` symlink, a hand-placed `media/notes.html`, a Windows Thumbs.db/desktop.ini or a `media/old/` subfolder all land in site/media/ and get committed to public gh-pages. served_file would refuse every one of them in the admin.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/media.py\",\n    \"line\": 101,\n    \"summary\": \"If file.write raises (e.g. disk full) after open('xb') has created the file, nothing removes the partial file. Only the later sqlite3.Error path unlinks.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"An upload fails with OSError mid-write and the user gets a 500. A truncated team.png stays in media/ with no library row. served_file still serves it in the admin, render_site exports it, and the next upload of team.png silently becomes team-2.png. The same orphan is left if the process dies between the write and the INSERT.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/media.py\",\n    \"line\": 44,\n    \"summary\": \"The 'Add alt text' check only strips characters str.split treats as whitespace, so alt text made only of invisible characters is accepted.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"Alt text of U+200B (zero-width space), U+2060, U+FEFF, U+3164, U+2800 or U+00AD passes both checks (confirmed). The Post gets &lt;img alt=\\\"\\u200b\\\"&gt;, which a screen reader reads as nothing, breaking acceptance step 2 ('empty alt text is refused').\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/media.py\",\n    \"line\": 48,\n    \"summary\": \"The refusal message names only * _ ` [ ] &lt; &amp;, but any backslash also triggers it, so the user is told to remove characters they never typed.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"Alt text 'C:\\\\pics screenshot' or 'before\\\\after' is refused (markdown-it renders 'C:\\\\pics' as alt 'C:ics', confirmed). The message says '* _ ` [ ] &lt; &amp;', which the text doesn't contain, so the Editor can't tell what to change.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/publish.py\",\n    \"line\": 112,\n    \"summary\": \"copytree runs after rmtree(site/) and after publish_due has flipped Scheduled items. If it fails, `cms publish` stops with site/ half-written.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"A file in media/ can't be read (locked by another program, or a broken symlink). shutil.Error is raised after the posts are written but before media/ is complete. site/ is left with pages whose images are missing, and running `cms deploy` next pushes that broken site.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/media.py\",\n    \"line\": 69,\n    \"summary\": \"A real PNG named just '.png' (or '.jpg') is refused as the wrong type, because PurePosixPath('.png').suffix is ''.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"Uploading a file literally named '.png' with valid PNG bytes returns 400 'Only PNG and JPEG images can be uploaded (.png, .jpg or .jpeg).' (confirmed), which contradicts what the user just did.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/publish.py\",\n    \"line\": 112,\n    \"summary\": \"CLAUDE.md violation (C:\\\\Rajan\\\\E disk\\\\My work\\\\IPHS400\\\\code\\\\mp2-cms\\\\CLAUDE.md): 'Only published content reaches `site/`. Drafts never leave the database.' It also breaks publish.py's own rule 1, 'Only PUBLISHED content is written here.'\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"`shutil.copytree(settings.MEDIA, out / \\\"media\\\")` writes images whose only use is a Draft, or no Post at all, into site/. The change updated CONTEXT.md to match but not CLAUDE.md or the publish.py docstring, so the two standing rules now contradict the code.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/routes/media.py\",\n    \"line\": 54,\n    \"summary\": \"The 2 MB limit is checked only after Starlette has received and spooled the whole multipart body. Reading MAX_BYTES + 1 bytes saves nothing.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"A 1 GB file posted to /admin/media/upload is read in full and written to a temp file on disk before the 400 'over 2 MB' comes back. The wasted I/O and disk are proportional to the upload, not to the limit.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/routes/content_crud.py\",\n    \"line\": 294,\n    \"summary\": \"Altitude: the client sends `to_root` back, the server validates it with is_to_root, and _render_form computes to_root_from, all only to place media/ images in the admin preview. The admin is always served from its server root, which mdrender's docstring already relies on for root links.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"Rewriting media/ to a fixed '/media/' in preview mode would resolve on every admin page at any depth. That would remove the extra form field, the JS change in content_form.html, TO_ROOT_RE/is_to_root and the root_links flag. Today it is three files of extra plumbing plus a client input that must be validated.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \".gitignore\",\n    \"line\": 4,\n    \"summary\": \"The unanchored `media/` pattern ignores a directory named media at any depth, not just the repo-root upload folder.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"A future docs/media/ or tests/fixtures/media/ (e.g. sample images for tests) would be silently left out of git. `/media/` would ignore only the folder settings.MEDIA points at.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/media.py\",\n    \"line\": 93,\n    \"summary\": \"Each upload loads every filename in the library into a set just to skip names already taken.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"Cost grows with library size on every upload. A per-candidate `SELECT 1 FROM media WHERE filename = ?` does the same job, and together with the existing 'xb' and UNIQUE checks it is equally safe.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/routes/media.py\",\n    \"line\": 19,\n    \"summary\": \"Reuse: CSRF_EXPIRED_MESSAGE redefines the string already defined in app/routes/users.py:20, which also appears as literals in content_crud.py and auth.py.\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"A wording change has to be made in four or more places, and the copies drift. Import a single constant instead.\"\n  },\n  {\n    \"file\": \"app/routes/media.py\",\n    \"line\": 22,\n    \"summary\": \"Reuse: _render_library is a fifth hand-written copy of read_or_mint_csrf -&gt; TemplateResponse -&gt; set_csrf_cookie (also in content_crud._render_form/_render_list, guards.render_access_denied and users.py).\",\n    \"failure_scenario\": \"Every new admin screen repeats the CSRF cookie handling by hand. A missed set_csrf_cookie on any copy silently breaks the next form POST. One shared render-with-CSRF helper would remove the duplication.\"\n  }\n]\n```</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>138520</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>23</tool_uses><duration_ms>563095</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

Reword it without them.\")\n    return alt\n\n\ndef _has_words(text: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Whether `text` has a letter or digit a screen reader would read out.\n    Zero-width and other invisible characters alone count as empty.\"\"\"\n    return any(unicodedata.category(character)[0] in \"LN\"\n               and character not in INVISIBLE_LETTERS for character in text)","originalFile":"\"\"\"The Media library: images uploaded for use in Posts, each with Alt text\n(see CONTEXT.md). The file goes in media/, which is git-ignored like the\ndatabase; its row in the `media` table keeps the Alt text. No ORM (see spec\nImplementation Decisions).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport itertools\nimport re\nimport sqlite3\nfrom html import unescape\nfrom pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath\n\nfrom app import db as db_module\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.mdrender import render_markdown\n\nMAX_BYTES = 2 * 1024 * 1024  # 2 MB\n\n# The extensions accepted, each with the type's name and the first bytes\n# every file of that type starts with, so a renamed .html file is caught.\nSIGNATURES = {\n    \".png\": (\"PNG\", b\"\\x89PNG\\r\\n\\x1a\\n\"),\n    \".jpg\": (\"JPEG\", b\"\\xff\\xd8\\xff\"),\n    \".jpeg\": (\"JPEG\", b\"\\xff\\xd8\\xff\"),\n}\n\n\nclass UploadRefused(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"An upload that breaks one of the library's rules; the message says\n    which, in words for the upload form.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef snippet(item) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The Markdown that places a library item in a Post.\"\"\"\n    return f\"![{item['alt_text']}](media/{item['filename']})\"\n\n\ndef clean_alt_text(raw: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"`raw` on one line, with runs of spaces collapsed. Raises\n    UploadRefused if nothing is left, or if a Post would show different\n    alt text once the item's snippet is pasted in.\"\"\"\n    alt = \" \".join(raw.split())\n    if not alt:\n        raise UploadRefused(\"Add alt text: a short description of the image for \"\n                            \"someone who can't see it.\")\n    if _published_alt(alt) != alt:\n        raise UploadRefused(\"Markdown would change this alt text in a post: it reads some \"\n                            \"uses of * _ ` [ ] < & as formatting. Reword it without them.\")\n    return alt\n\n\ndef _published_alt(alt: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"The alt text a Post shows for a snippet carrying `alt`, rendered by\n    the Posts' own Markdown pipeline (None if it makes no image at all).\n    Markdown reads * _ ` [ ] < & as syntax there, and markdown-it drops even\n    backslash-escaped characters from an image's alt, so escaping can't help.\"\"\"\n    html = render_markdown(snippet({\"alt_text\": alt, \"filename\": \"image.png\"}))\n    match = re.search(r'<img [^>]*alt=\"([^\"]*)\"', html)\n    return unescape(match.group(1)) if match else None\n\n\ndef check_image(filename: str, data: bytes) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The lowercase extension of an acceptable image: a PNG or JPEG by both\n    its name and its first bytes, MAX_BYTES or smaller. Raises UploadRefused\n    otherwise. `data` may be cut short at MAX_BYTES + 1 bytes.\"\"\"\n    if not filename:\n        raise UploadRefused(\"Choose an image to upload.\")\n    extension = PurePosixPath(filename).suffix.lower()\n    if extension not in SIGNATURES:\n        raise UploadRefused(\"Only PNG and JPEG images can be uploaded (.png, .jpg or .jpeg).\")\n    if len(data) > MAX_BYTES:\n        raise UploadRefused(\"That image is over 2 MB. Make it smaller and upload it again.\")\n    kind, signature = SIGNATURES[extension]\n    if not data.startswith(signature):\n        raise UploadRefused(f\"That file isn't a real {kind} image, whatever its name says.\")\n    return extension\n\n\ndef _safe_stem(filename: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The upload's own name, without folders or extension, as lowercase\n    letters, digits and hyphens: \"C:\\\\pics\\\\Team Photo (1).PNG\" -> \"team-photo-1\".\"\"\"\n    stem = PurePosixPath(filename.replace(\"\\\\\", \"/\")).stem\n    return re.sub(r\"[^a-z0-9]+\", \"-\", stem.lower()).strip(\"-\")[:60].strip(\"-\") or \"image\"\n\n\ndef _create_file(conn: sqlite3.Connection, filename: str, extension: str, data: bytes) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Write `data` to a new file in media/ named after the upload: \"team.png\",\n    then \"team-2.png\", \"team-3.png\", ... It never replaces a file already\n    there, even one another upload creates at the same moment, nor takes a\n    name the library already uses.\"\"\"\n    stem = _safe_stem(filename)\n    taken = {row[\"filename\"] for row in conn.execute(\"SELECT filename FROM media\")}\n    for number in itertools.count(1):\n        path = settings.MEDIA / (f\"{stem}{extension}\" if number == 1\n                                 else f\"{stem}-{number}{extension}\")\n        if path.name in taken:\n            continue\n        try:\n            with open(path, \"xb\") as file:\n                file.write(data)\n        except FileExistsError:\n            continue\n        return path\n\n\ndef save_upload(filename: str, data: bytes, alt_text: str, uploaded_by: int) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Write the image to media/ under a safe, unused name and record its\n    Alt text in the library. Returns the name it was saved as; raises\n    UploadRefused, storing nothing, if the upload breaks a rule.\"\"\"\n    extension = check_image(filename, data)\n    alt_text = clean_alt_text(alt_text)\n    settings.MEDIA.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        path = _create_file(conn, filename, extension, data)\n        try:\n            conn.execute(\n                \"INSERT INTO media (filename, alt_text, uploaded_by) VALUES (?, ?, ?)\",\n                (path.name, alt_text, uploaded_by),\n            )\n            conn.commit()\n        except sqlite3.Error:\n            path.unlink()  # this upload's own file: _create_file never reuses one\n            raise\n        return path.name\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef list_media() -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n    \"\"\"Every image in the library, newest first, with who uploaded it.\"\"\"\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT media.*, users.email AS uploaded_by_email FROM media \"\n            \"JOIN users ON users.id = media.uploaded_by ORDER BY media.id DESC\"\n        ).fetchall()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef served_file(filename: str) -> Path | None:\n    \"\"\"media/<filename>, if that is an image file directly inside media/;\n    else None, so a crafted name (\"..\\\\cms.db\", \"x.html\") is never served.\"\"\"\n    if PurePosixPath(filename).suffix.lower() not in SIGNATURES:\n        return None\n    path = settings.MEDIA / filename\n    try:\n        inside = path.resolve().parent == settings.MEDIA.resolve()\n    except OSError:\n        return None\n    return path if inside and path.is_file() else None\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":41,"oldLines":15,"newStart":41,"newLines":22,"lines":["     UploadRefused if nothing is left, or if a Post would show different","     alt text once the item's snippet is pasted in.\"\"\"","     alt = \" \".join(raw.split())","-    if not alt:","+    if not _has_words(alt):","         raise UploadRefused(\"Add alt text: a short description of the image for \"","                             \"someone who can't see it.\")","     if _published_alt(alt) != alt:","         raise UploadRefused(\"Markdown would change this alt text in a post: it reads some \"","-                            \"uses of * _ ` [ ] < & as formatting. Reword it without them.\")\n    return alt\n\n\ndef _has_words(text: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Whether `text` has a letter or digit a screen reader would read out.\n    Zero-width and other invisible characters alone count as empty.\"\"\"\n    return any(unicodedata.category(character)[0] in \"LN\"\n               and character not in INVISIBLE_LETTERS for character in text)\n\n\ndef _published_alt(alt: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"The alt text a Post shows for a snippet carrying `alt`, rendered by\n    the Posts' own Markdown pipeline (None if it makes no image at all).\n    Markdown reads * _ ` [ ] < & as syntax there, and markdown-it drops even\n    backslash-escaped characters from an image's alt, so escaping can't help.\"\"\"\n    html = render_markdown(snippet({\"alt_text\": alt, \"filename\": \"image.png\"}))\n    match = re.search(r'<img [^>]*alt=\"([^\"]*)\"', html)\n    return unescape(match.group(1)) if match else None\n\n\ndef check_image(filename: str, data: bytes) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The lowercase extension of an acceptable image: a PNG or JPEG by both\n    its name and its first bytes, MAX_BYTES or smaller. Raises UploadRefused\n    otherwise. `data` may be cut short at MAX_BYTES + 1 bytes.\"\"\"\n    if not filename:\n        raise UploadRefused(\"Choose an image to upload.\")\n    extension = PurePosixPath(filename).suffix.lower()\n    if extension not in SIGNATURES:\n        raise UploadRefused(\"Only PNG and JPEG images can be uploaded (.png, .jpg or .jpeg).\")\n    if len(data) > MAX_BYTES:\n        raise UploadRefused(\"That image is over 2 MB. Make it smaller and upload it again.\")\n    kind, signature = SIGNATURES[extension]\n    if not data.startswith(signature):\n        raise UploadRefused(f\"That file isn't a real {kind} image, whatever its name says.\")\n    return extension\n\n\ndef _safe_stem(filename: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The upload's own name, without folders or extension, as lowercase\n    letters, digits and hyphens: \"C:\\\\pics\\\\Team Photo (1).PNG\" -> \"team-photo-1\".\"\"\"\n    stem = PurePosixPath(filename.replace(\"\\\\\", \"/\")).stem\n    return re.sub(r\"[^a-z0-9]+\", \"-\", stem.lower()).strip(\"-\")[:60].strip(\"-\") or \"image\"\n\n\ndef _create_file(conn: sqlite3.Connection, filename: str, extension: str, data: bytes) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Write `data` to a new file in media/ named after the upload: \"team.png\",\n    then \"team-2.png\", \"team-3.png\", ... It never replaces a file already\n    there, even one another upload creates at the same moment, nor takes a\n    name the library already uses.\"\"\"\n    stem = _safe_stem(filename)\n    taken = {row[\"filename\"] for row in conn.execute(\"SELECT filename FROM media\")}\n    for number in itertools.count(1):\n        path = settings.MEDIA / (f\"{stem}{extension}\" if number == 1\n                                 else f\"{stem}-{number}{extension}\")\n        if path.name in taken:\n            continue\n        try:\n            with open(path, \"xb\") as file:\n                file.write(data)\n        except FileExistsError:\n            continue\n        return path\n\n\ndef save_upload(filename: str, data: bytes, alt_text: str, uploaded_by: int) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Write the image to media/ under a safe, unused name and record its\n    Alt text in the library. Returns the name it was saved as; raises\n    UploadRefused, storing nothing, if the upload breaks a rule.\"\"\"\n    extension = check_image(filename, data)\n    alt_text = clean_alt_text(alt_text)\n    settings.MEDIA.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        path = _create_file(conn, filename, extension, data)\n        try:\n            conn.execute(\n                \"INSERT INTO media (filename, alt_text, uploaded_by) VALUES (?, ?, ?)\",\n                (path.name, alt_text, uploaded_by),\n            )\n            conn.commit()\n        except sqlite3.Error:\n            path.unlink()  # this upload's own file: _create_file never reuses one\n            raise\n        return path.name\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef list_media() -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n    \"\"\"Every image in the library, newest first, with who uploaded it.\"\"\"\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT media.*, users.email AS uploaded_by_email FROM media \"\n            \"JOIN users ON users.id = media.uploaded_by ORDER BY media.id DESC\"\n        ).fetchall()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef served_file(filename: str) -> Path | None:\n    \"\"\"media/<filename>, if that is an image file directly inside media/;\n    else None, so a crafted name (\"..\\\\cms.db\", \"x.html\") is never served.\"\"\"\n    if PurePosixPath(filename).suffix.lower() not in SIGNATURES:\n        return None\n    path = settings.MEDIA / filename\n    try:\n        inside = path.resolve().parent == settings.MEDIA.resolve()\n    except OSError:\n        return None\n    return path if inside and path.is_file() else None\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":108,"oldLines":10,"newStart":108,"newLines":15,"lines":["         if path.name in taken:","             continue","         try:","-            with open(path, \"xb\") as file:","-                file.write(data)","+            file = open(path, \"xb\")","         except FileExistsError:","             continue","+        try:","+            with file:","+                file.write(data)","+        except BaseException:","+            path.unlink()  #
